title.zh: 卷九十四 列傳第六十四 隱逸
title.raw: 卷九十四 列傳第六十四 隱逸 Volume 94 Biographies 64: Hermits and Recluses

sentences.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；

translations.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;
translations.idiomatic: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.

sentences.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。

translations.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.
translations.idiomatic: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.

sentences.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；

translations.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;
translations.idiomatic: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;

sentences.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。

translations.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.
translations.idiomatic: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.

sentences.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；

translations.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;
translations.idiomatic: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;

sentences.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。

translations.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.

sentences.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。

translations.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.

sentences.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。

translations.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.

sentences.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?
translations.idiomatic: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.

sentences.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。

translations.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.

sentences.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。

translations.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.

sentences.zh: 孫登，字公和，汲郡共人也。

translations.literal: Sun Deng, styled Gonghe, was a man of Gong in Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng, courtesy name Gonghe, came from Gong in Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 無家屬，于郡北山為土窟居之，夏則編草為裳，冬則被髮自覆。

translations.literal: He had no family dependents; on the north mountain of the commandery he dug an earthen pit and dwelt there; in summer he wove grass into garments, in winter he let down his hair to cover himself.
translations.idiomatic: He kept no household. On the mountain north of the city he hollowed out an earth cave for a home: in summer he braided straw into a coat, in winter he spread his long hair like a blanket.

sentences.zh: 好讀《易》，撫一弦琴，見者皆親樂之。

translations.literal: He loved to read the "Changes" and stroked a one-stringed zither; all who saw him drew close and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Book of Changes and would pluck a single-stringed lute; everyone who met him felt drawn and glad.

sentences.zh: 性無恚怒，人或投諸水中，欲觀其怒，登既出，便大笑。

translations.literal: By nature he had no resentment or anger; someone once threw him into the water wishing to see him angry, but when Deng came out he simply burst into laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Anger was foreign to him. Once men threw him into a pond hoping to rouse his temper; he climbed out and only laughed.

sentences.zh: 時時遊人間，所經家或設衣食者，一無所辭，去皆捨棄。

translations.literal: From time to time he wandered among men; wherever he passed, if a household set out food or clothing he never declined, but when he left he cast it all aside.
translations.idiomatic: He would drift through the villages now and then. If people offered him food or clothes he accepted without fuss, and left everything behind when he walked on.

sentences.zh: 嘗住宜陽山，有作炭人見之，知非常人，與語，登亦不應。

translations.literal: He once stayed on Mount Yiyang; a charcoal-burner saw him, knew he was no ordinary man, and spoke to him, but Deng did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: While staying on Mount Yiyang he was spotted by a charcoal-maker who saw at once that he was no common wanderer. The man spoke to him; Deng gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞之，使阮籍往觀，既見，與語，亦不應。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen heard of it, he sent Ruan Ji to observe him; after they met and Ji spoke to him, still he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei sent Ruan Ji to look in on him. Ji talked with him after they met; again Deng said nothing.

sentences.zh: 嵇康又從之遊三年，問其所圖，終不答，康每歎息。

translations.literal: Xi Kang again followed him and roamed three years, asking what he aimed at, and to the end he did not answer; Kang often sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kang stayed with him for three years, asking what design he had in mind, and never received a word in reply. Kang could only sigh again and again.

sentences.zh: 將別，謂曰：「先生竟無言乎？

translations.literal: About to part, Kang said to him, "Sir, will you truly say nothing?
translations.idiomatic: As Kang was leaving he said, "Master, have you no parting counsel at all?

sentences.zh: 」登乃曰：「子識火乎？

translations.literal: " Deng then said, "Do you understand fire?
translations.idiomatic: Deng replied, "Do you understand fire?

sentences.zh: 火生而有光，而不用其光，果在於用光。

translations.literal: Fire is born and has light, yet does not use its light; the kernel lies in using the light.
translations.idiomatic: Fire is born with a flame, yet its strength is not in brandishing that flame; the point is knowing how to use the light without burning yourself.

sentences.zh: 人生而有才，而不用其才，而果在於用才。

translations.literal: Man is born and has talent, yet does not use his talent; the kernel lies in using talent.
translations.idiomatic: A man is born with gifts, yet the danger is not in hiding them but in how he spends them; everything turns on the use he makes of his talent.

sentences.zh: 故用光在乎得薪，所以保其耀；

translations.literal: Therefore using light lies in obtaining fuel; by this one preserves its radiance;
translations.idiomatic: A lamp needs fuel to give steady light; tend the fuel and the glow endures.

sentences.zh: 用才在乎識真，所以全其年。

translations.literal: using talent lies in recognizing the genuine; by this one completes one's years.
translations.idiomatic: Talent needs a clear eye for what is real; only then can a man live out his natural span.

sentences.zh: 今子才多識寡，難乎免於今之世矣！

translations.literal: Now you, sir, have much talent and little discernment; it will be hard to escape harm in today's world!
translations.idiomatic: You are rich in gifts but poor in judgment; in the world as it is now, you will be hard put to stay out of trouble.

sentences.zh: 子無求乎？

translations.literal: Have you no desire for office?
translations.idiomatic: Will you not seek a post after all?

sentences.zh: 」康不能用，果遭非命，乃作《幽憤詩》曰：「昔慚柳下，今愧孫登。

translations.literal: " Kang could not use this advice and indeed met an unnatural death; then he composed the "Poem of Hidden Resentment," saying, "Once I was ashamed before Liuxia; now I am ashamed before Sun Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Kang did not take the warning to heart and soon died a violent death. In his "Poem of Hidden Anguish" he wrote, "I once fell short of Liuxia Hui; now I am humbled before Sun Deng.

sentences.zh: 」或謂登以魏晉去就，易生嫌疑，故或嘿者也。

translations.literal: " Some say that because of the choices between Wei and Jin it was easy to incur suspicion, therefore sometimes he was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Some thought Deng held his tongue because any word about loyalty to Wei or Jin could invite deadly suspicion.

sentences.zh: 竟不知所終。

translations.literal: In the end it is not known where he ended.
translations.idiomatic: No one knows where he finally went.

sentences.zh: 董京，字威輦，不知何郡人也。

translations.literal: Dong Jing, styled Weinian— it is not known of what commandery he was.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jing, courtesy name Weinian, was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 初與隴西計吏俱至洛陽，被髮而行，逍遙吟詠，常宿白社中。

translations.literal: At first he came to Luoyang together with a Longxi clerk on mission; with hair unbound he walked, wandering freely, chanting and intoning, and often lodged in the White Community.
translations.idiomatic: He first reached Luoyang in the company of a Longxi county clerk, hair streaming loose, strolling and humming verses, and usually slept in the White Community hall.

sentences.zh: 時乞於市，得殘碎繒絮，結以自覆，全帛佳綿則不肯受。

translations.literal: From time to time he begged in the market; obtaining torn scraps of silk wadding he knotted them to cover himself; whole bolts or fine floss he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He begged in the streets for ragged scraps of silk batting and knotted them into a cloak; he turned down whole pieces of cloth or good cotton.

sentences.zh: 或見推排罵辱，曾無怒色。

translations.literal: Sometimes he was shoved aside and reviled and insulted, yet never showed anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: People might jostle and curse him; his face never darkened.

sentences.zh: 孫楚時為著作郎，數就社中與語，遂載與俱歸，京不肯坐。

translations.literal: Sun Chu at the time was secretary in the editorial office; he repeatedly went to the community to speak with him, then carried him off in a cart to return together, but Jing would not sit.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu, then an editorial secretary, often visited the hall to talk with him. Once Chu put him in a carriage to take him home, but Jing refused even to sit inside.

sentences.zh: 楚乃貽之書，勸以今堯舜之世，胡為懷道迷邦。

translations.literal: Chu then sent him a letter, urging him with the present age of Yao and Shun, why harbor the Way and lose the state.
translations.idiomatic: Chu wrote urging him that this was an age of Yao and Shun reborn, and asked why he clutched the Way to himself while the kingdom went wanting.

sentences.zh: 京答之以詩曰：「周道斁兮頌聲沒，夏政衰兮五常汨。

translations.literal: Jing answered him with a poem saying, "The Zhou way is ruined, hymn sounds are gone; Xia government declines, the five constants are drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Jing answered in verse: "Zhou's great road lies in ruins and the hymns are stilled; Xia's rule has rotted and the five constant virtues are lost in the mud.

sentences.zh: 便便君子，顧望而逝，洋洋乎滿目，而作者七。

translations.literal: The easy-going gentlemen look about and depart; vast, filling the eyes, yet those who act are seven.
translations.idiomatic: The smooth courtiers glance around and slip away, while swaggering men fill every corner—yet the makers of policy are only the Seven.

sentences.zh: 豈不樂天地之化也？

translations.literal: Is it not that they delight in the transformation of heaven and earth?
translations.idiomatic: Do they not rejoice in heaven and earth's endless change?

sentences.zh: 哀哉乎時之不可與，對之以獨處。

translations.literal: Alas! The age cannot be joined with; I answer it by dwelling alone.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, this is not an age one can join; I answer it by keeping to myself.

sentences.zh: 無娛我以為歡，清流可飲，至道可餐，何為棲棲，自使疲單？

translations.literal: Nothing amuses me to make joy; clear streams may be drunk, the ultimate Way may be feasted on—why bustle about and weary yourself alone?
translations.idiomatic: I need no pleasure but my own: I can drink from a clear stream and feed on the highest Way—why should I scurry about until I am worn hollow?

sentences.zh: 魚懸獸檻，鄙夫知之。

translations.literal: Fish hung up and beasts in pens—vulgar men know it.
translations.idiomatic: Any fool knows what it means when fish hang on a line and beasts pace a cage.

sentences.zh: 夫古之至人，藏器於靈，縕袍不能令暖，軒冕不能令榮；

translations.literal: As for the utmost men of old, they hid their implements in the spirit; a padded hemp robe could not make them warm, carriage and crown could not make them glorious;
translations.idiomatic: The sages of old sheathed their gifts deep in the soul: a patched cloak could not warm them with pride, nor chariot and coronet lend them glory;

sentences.zh: 動如川之流，靜如川之渟。

translations.literal: in movement like a stream's flowing, in stillness like a stream's resting.
translations.idiomatic: in motion they were a river in flood, at rest a pool that never stirs.

sentences.zh: 鸚鵡能言，泗濱浮磬，眾人所玩，豈合物情！

translations.literal: The parrot can speak, the floating chime-stone from Si bank—what the crowd plays with—how could these match the truth of things!
translations.idiomatic: A parrot may talk, a chime from the Si's shore may float—baubles the mob toys with. Do you call that the way things really are?

sentences.zh: 玄鳥紆幕，而不被害？

translations.literal: The dark bird winds through the curtain—yet is not harmed?
translations.idiomatic: The swallow weaves beneath the eaves—yet goes unharmed?

sentences.zh: 𩿦隼遠巢，咸以欲死。

translations.literal: The osprey and falcon build nests far off—all alike die for desire.
translations.idiomatic: Kites and falcons nest on remote cliffs—yet every one of them can die for want.

sentences.zh: 眄彼梁魚，逡巡倒尾，沈吟不決，忽焉失水。

translations.literal: Gaze at those bridge fish, hesitating, tail reversed, brooding undecided, suddenly they lose the water.
translations.idiomatic: Look at the fish beneath the bridge: they hang back, tails curled, unable to choose—and in a blink the water is gone.

sentences.zh: 嗟呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 魚鳥相與，萬世而不悟；

translations.literal: Fish and birds together, for myriad ages and never awakened;
translations.idiomatic: Bird and fish go on the same old way for age after age and never wake to it;

sentences.zh: 以我觀之，乃明其故。

translations.literal: when I observe them, then I clarify their cause.
translations.idiomatic: from where I stand I see exactly why it is so.

sentences.zh: 焉知不有達人，深穆其度，亦將窺我，顰顣而去。

translations.literal: How do we know there is not a man of penetration, deeply silent in his measure, who will also peep at me, knit his brows, and depart?
translations.idiomatic: Who is to say some wise soul, grave and still within, is not watching me even now, frowning as he turns away?

sentences.zh: 萬物皆賤，惟人為貴，動以九州為狹，靜以環堵為大。

translations.literal: The myriad things are all base; only man is noble; in movement he takes the nine provinces as narrow, in stillness he takes a ring of walls as great.
translations.idiomatic: Creation ranks everything low but sets man high: restless, he finds the nine regions too small; at peace, a single cramped room is empire enough.

sentences.zh: 」後數年，遁去，莫知所之，於其所寢處惟有一石竹子及詩二篇。

translations.literal: " After several years he vanished; none knew where he had gone; at the place where he had slept there was only a stone bamboo staff and two poems.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he disappeared without trace. All that remained where he had slept was a bamboo staff carved from stone and two poems.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：「乾道剛簡，坤體敦密，茫茫太素，是則是述。

translations.literal: The first said, "The way of Qian is hard and simple; the body of Kun is thick and dense; vast, vast Grand Simplicity—this is what is, this is what is followed.
translations.idiomatic: The first read: "Heaven's way is firm and plain; earth's frame is rich and deep; boundless was the Primal Simplicity—such is the pattern we inherit.

sentences.zh: 末世流奔，以文代質，悠悠世目，孰知其實！

translations.literal: In the latter age currents rush; culture replaces substance; long, long the world's eyes—who knows its reality!
translations.idiomatic: Our late age races downstream, polish crowding out truth; the world's dull gaze—who still knows what is real?

sentences.zh: 逝將去此至虛，歸我自然之室。

translations.literal: I will go away from this utmost void, return to my chamber of spontaneity.
translations.idiomatic: I am leaving this hollow show for the house nature built for me.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「孔子不遇，時彼感麟。

translations.literal: " Again it said, "Confucius did not meet his time; then he was moved by the unicorn.
translations.idiomatic: The second said: "Confucius never found his season; the unicorn moved him to grief.

sentences.zh: 麟乎麟！

translations.literal: Unicorn, O unicorn!
translations.idiomatic: Unicorn, unicorn!

sentences.zh: 胡不遁世以存真？」

translations.literal: Why do you not flee the world to preserve the genuine?
translations.idiomatic: Why will you not leave the world and keep what is true?

sentences.zh: 夏統，字仲御，會稽永興人也。

translations.literal: Xia Tong, styled Zhongyu, was a man of Yongxing in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Tong, courtesy name Zhongyu, was a native of Yongxing in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，養親以孝聞，睦于兄弟，每采梠求食，星行夜歸，或至海邊，拘螊𧑅以資養。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned and poor, he was known for filial care of his parents, harmonious with brothers; often he gathered firewood seeking food, traveling by starlight and returning by night, sometimes going to the seashore to catch crabs and shellfish to supply their support.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he won a name for supporting his mother with filial care and lived at peace with his brothers. He would gather brushwood before dawn and trudge home in the dark, or walk to the shore to catch crabs and shellfish to help feed the family.

sentences.zh: 雅善談論。

translations.literal: He was refined and skilled in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He was an elegant and persuasive speaker.

sentences.zh: 宗族勸之仕，謂之曰：「卿清亮質直，可作郡綱紀，與府朝接，自當顯至，如何甘辛苦于山林，畢性命于海濱也！

translations.literal: His lineage urged him to take office, saying to him, "You, sir, are clear, bright, plain, and upright; you could serve as commandery recorder, connect with the prefectural court, and naturally would rise to eminence—how can you willingly endure hardship in mountains and forests and exhaust your life on the seashore!
translations.idiomatic: His kinsmen pressed him to enter government. "You are honest, lucid, and upright," they said. "You could be a commandery clerk, move among the high officials, and rise in time—why choose the hardship of the hills and spend your whole life on the coast?

sentences.zh: 」統悖然作色曰：「諸君待我乃至此乎！

translations.literal: " Tong abruptly changed color and said, "You gentlemen esteem me to reach this!
translations.idiomatic: Tong's face went dark. "Is this how little you think of me?

sentences.zh: 使統屬太平之時，當與元凱評議出處，遇濁代，念與屈生同汙共泥；

translations.literal: Had Tong belonged to an age of great peace, I ought with Yuan and Kai to debate going out or staying in; meeting a turbid generation, I would think to share mud and filth with Master Qu;
translations.idiomatic: Had I lived under a flawless sage-king, I might have debated office and retirement with the likes of the Eight Yuan and Eight Kai. In a foul age I would gladly foul myself beside Qu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 若汙隆之間，自當耦耕沮溺，豈有辱身曲意於郡府之間乎！

translations.literal: if between decline and rise, naturally I ought to plough in pair with Ju and Ni—how could there be debasing the body and bending intent between commandery and prefectural offices!
translations.idiomatic: In an age neither wholly bright nor wholly dark I would hoe side by side with Jie Ni and Chang Zu. Never would I cringe and crawl in some yamen gate!

sentences.zh: 聞君之談，不覺寒毛盡戴，白汗四匝，顏如渥丹，心熱如炭，舌縮口張，兩耳壁塞也。

translations.literal: Hearing your discourse, without realizing it every hair stands on end, white sweat runs all around, the face is like cinnabar wash, the heart burns like charcoal, the tongue shrinks and the mouth gapes, both ears are blocked like walls.
translations.idiomatic: Your words set every hair on my skin on end, sent cold sweat in rivers down my ribs, painted my cheeks fever-red, set my heart smoldering like coals, glued my tongue to the roof of my mouth, and stuffed my ears as if with clay.

sentences.zh: 」言者大慚。

translations.literal: " The speakers were greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: His relatives were mortified into silence.

sentences.zh: 統自此遂不與宗族相見。

translations.literal: From this Tong then did not meet with his lineage kin.
translations.idiomatic: After that he refused to see his clan at all.

sentences.zh: 會母疾，統侍醫藥，宗親因得見之。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, Tong attended her with medicine, and thereby lineage kin got to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew sick he nursed her with physic, so his kinsmen had a chance to visit.

sentences.zh: 其從父敬甯祠先人，迎女巫章丹、陳珠二人，並有國色，莊服甚麗，善歌儛，又能隱形匿影。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Jingning sacrificed to the ancestors, welcoming two witch-women, Zhang Dan and Chen Zhu, both having state-level beauty, ritual garments very splendid, skilled in singing and dancing, and also able to hide form and conceal shadow.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Jingning was holding a sacrifice to the ancestors and had hired two shamankas, Zhang Dan and Chen Zhu—women of breathtaking beauty in gorgeous ritual dress, who sang and danced superbly and could make themselves vanish from sight.

sentences.zh: 甲夜之初，撞鐘擊鼓，間以絲竹，丹、珠乃拔刀破舌，吞刀吐火，雲霧杳冥，流光電發。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the first watch, they struck bells and beat drums, interspersed with strings and winds; Dan and Zhu then drew knives and split their tongues, swallowed knives and spat fire; cloud and mist were dark and dim, flowing light flashed like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: As the first watch began, bells and drums rolled, strings and pipes wove between. Zhang and Chen slashed their tongues with knives, swallowed blades, breathed fire—smoke hid the hall and lightnings seemed to crackle through the murk.

sentences.zh: 統諸從兄弟欲往觀之，難統，於是共紿之曰：「從父間疾病得瘳，大小以為喜慶，欲因其祭祀，並往賀之，卿可俱行乎？

translations.literal: Tong's various cousins wished to go observe it; they found Tong difficult, therefore together they deceived him, saying, "Our uncle's intermittent illness has obtained recovery; young and old take it as joyful celebration; wishing to take advantage of his sacrifice, all go together to congratulate him—will you go together?
translations.idiomatic: Tong's cousins wanted to watch the show but knew he would refuse, so they lied: "Uncle's recurring illness has lifted; the whole family is celebrating. We mean to visit him during the sacrifice to offer our joy. Won't you come along?

sentences.zh: 」統從之。

translations.literal: " Tong followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Tong went with them.

sentences.zh: 入門，忽見丹、珠在中庭，輕步佪舞，靈談鬼笑，飛觸挑柈，酬酢翩翻。

translations.literal: Entering the gate, suddenly he saw Dan and Zhu in the central courtyard, light steps circling in dance, spirit talk and ghost laughter, flying touches lifting platters, toasting back and forth fluttering.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the gate he saw Zhang and Chen whirling in the courtyard on light feet, chattering like spirits, laughing like ghosts, leaping to catch cups and platters, wheeling through the drinking games in a blur.

sentences.zh: 統驚愕而走，不由門，破籓直出。

translations.literal: Tong was startled and ran, not by the gate, breaking the fence straight out.
translations.idiomatic: Tong bolted in horror, not toward the door but straight through a fence.

sentences.zh: 歸責諸人曰：「昔淫亂之俗興，衛文公為之悲惋；

translations.literal: Returning he blamed the various people, saying, "In the past when the custom of debauchery arose, Duke Wen of Wei lamented it;
translations.idiomatic: Back home he rebuked them: "When licentious ways spread through Wei, Duke Wen of Wei wept for the realm;

sentences.zh: 蝀蝀之氣見，君子尚不敢指；

translations.literal: when the rainbow's vapor appeared, the gentleman still did not dare point;
translations.idiomatic: when the rainbow omen showed in the sky, even gentlemen feared to name it;

sentences.zh: 季桓納齊女，仲尼載馳而退；

translations.literal: Ji Huan took a Qi girl, Zhongni drove swiftly and withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: when Ji Huanzi took the dancing-girls of Qi, Confucius turned his chariot and fled south;

sentences.zh: 子路見夏南，憤恚而忼愾。

translations.literal: Zilu saw Xia Nan and was indignant and wrathful.
translations.idiomatic: when Zilu looked on Xia Ji, his rage shook him to the marrow.

sentences.zh: 吾常恨不得頓叔向之頭，陷華父之眼。

translations.literal: I always hated that I could not chop off Shuxiang's head and gouge out Huafu's eyes.
translations.idiomatic: I have often wished I could strike off Shuxiang's head and blind Huafu with my thumbs.

sentences.zh: 奈何諸君迎此妖物，夜與遊戲，放傲逸之情，縱奢淫之行，亂男女之禮，破貞高之節，何也？

translations.literal: How is it that you gentlemen welcome these uncanny creatures, play with them by night, unleash arrogant dissolute feelings, indulge extravagant debauched conduct, disorder the rites of men and women, break chaste and lofty integrity—why?
translations.idiomatic: And now you bring such creatures under your roof, sport with them through the night, give free rein to pride and lust, trample the bounds between men and women, and shatter every claim to purity—why?

sentences.zh: 」遂隱床上，被髮而臥，不復言。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he hid on the bed, spread his hair, and lay down, and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself on his couch, hair streaming, and would not speak again.

sentences.zh: 眾親踧踖，即退遣丹、珠，各各分散。

translations.literal: The assembled kin were uneasy, immediately withdrew and dismissed Dan and Zhu, each scattering.
translations.idiomatic: The relatives, squirming with shame, sent the two women away at once and slipped off in all directions.

sentences.zh: 後其母病篤，乃詣洛市藥。

translations.literal: Later when his mother's illness was severe, he then went to Luoyang to buy medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother later sank toward death, he traveled to Luoyang to buy drugs.

sentences.zh: 會三月上巳，洛中王公已下並至浮橋，士女駢填，車服燭路。

translations.literal: It happened to be the third month's shangsi festival; from princes and dukes downward in Luoyang all arrived at the floating bridge, gentlemen and ladies crowded thick, carriages and robes lit the road.
translations.idiomatic: It was the spring festival on the third day of the third month. Everyone from princes downward had gone to the Floating Bridge; noblemen and women jammed the way until carriage canopies and silks lit the road like torches.

sentences.zh: 統時在船中曝所市藥，諸貴人車乘來者如雲，統並不之顧。

translations.literal: Tong at the time was in a boat airing the medicine he had bought; the noble guests' carriages arriving were like clouds, yet Tong paid them no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Tong sat in a small boat sunning his bundles of herbs while great coaches rolled past like clouds; he never lifted his eyes.

sentences.zh: 太尉賈充怪而問之，統初不應，重問，乃徐答曰：「會稽夏仲御也。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Jia Chong wondered at it and questioned him; at first Tong did not answer; asked again, he then slowly replied, "I am Xia Zhongyu of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Jia Chong, intrigued, hailed him. Tong ignored the first call; when Chong pressed again he answered slowly, "Xia Zhongyu of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 」充使問其土地風俗，統曰：「其人循循，猶有大禹之遺風，大伯之義讓，嚴遵之抗志，黃公之高節。

translations.literal: " Chong had him asked about the land's customs; Tong said, "Its people are orderly; still there is the surviving wind of Great Yu, the righteous yielding of the Great Elder, the defiant resolve of Yan Zun, the lofty integrity of Lord Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Chong asked about the customs of his country. Tong said, "We are a steady, patient folk. We still breathe something of Yu the Great, of Taibo who yielded a throne, of Yan Zun who scorned office, and of the old Lord Huang who chose death rather than serve the Qin.

sentences.zh: 」又問「卿居海濱，頗能隨水戲乎？

translations.literal: " Again he asked, "You dwell by the sea—are you rather able to sport upon the water?
translations.idiomatic: Chong added, "You live on the coast—can you play tricks on the water?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「可。

translations.literal: " He answered saying, "I can.
translations.idiomatic: "I can," said Tong.

sentences.zh: 」統乃操柂正櫓，折旋中流，初作鯔鷠躍，後作鯆䱐引，飛鷁首，掇獸尾，奪長梢而船直逝者三焉。

translations.literal: " Tong then took the helm and straightened the oar, wheeling in midcurrent; at first he made mullet-leap, afterward ray-stretch, flying wild-goose head, plucking beast tail, seizing the long pole so that the boat shot straight three times.
translations.idiomatic: Tong seized helm and sweep and spun the boat in the current—first a leap like mullet, then a stretch like a stingray, then the bow reared like a wild goose, the stern dipped like a beast's tail; three times he snatched the long pole and sent the skiff darting straight through the chop.

sentences.zh: 於是風波振駭，雲霧杳冥，俄而白魚跳入船者有八九。

translations.literal: Thereupon wind and waves shook alarmingly; cloud and mist were dark and dim; presently white fish that leaped into the boat were eight or nine.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and water roared; mist swallowed the banks. In moments eight or nine white fish vaulted into the boat.

sentences.zh: 觀者皆悚遽，充心尤異之，乃更就船與語，其應如響，欲使之仕，即俯而不答。

translations.literal: The onlookers all were startled and alarmed; Chong's heart was especially struck as strange; then he again approached the boat to speak with him; his responses were like echoes; wishing to make him take office, Tong then bowed his head and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd gasped. Chong was more astonished than anyone. He stepped down to the gunwale and questioned him; Tong answered as quick as an echo. When Chong hinted at an appointment, Tong only looked down and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 充又謂曰：「昔堯亦歌，舜亦歌，子與人歌而善，必反而後和之，明先聖前哲無不盡歌。

translations.literal: Chong again said to him, "In the past Yao also sang, Shun also sang; when the Master heard others sing well, he must turn and then harmonize with them—this clarifies that former sages and prior wise men none failed to sing.
translations.idiomatic: Chong tried again: "Yao sang, Shun sang; Confucius, hearing a fine song, always turned back to join the chorus. Every sage raised his voice.

sentences.zh: 卿頗能作卿土地間曲乎？

translations.literal: Are you rather able to compose a tune of your native place?
translations.idiomatic: Can you sing us something from your own country?

sentences.zh: 」統曰：「先公惟寓稽山，朝會萬國，授化鄙邦，崩殂而葬。

translations.literal: " Tong said, "The former lord only lodged on Mount Kuaiji; court assembly of the myriad states; he imparted transformation to our humble state; he collapsed and was buried.
translations.idiomatic: Tong said, "Our ancient lord dwelt on Mount Kuaiji, gathered the myriad states in audience, and spread civilization through our humble land; when he died he was buried there.

sentences.zh: 恩澤雲布，聖化猶存，百姓感詠，遂作《慕歌》。

translations.literal: Kind favor spread like clouds; sagely transformation still survives; the hundred surnames were moved and chanted; therefore they made the "Song of Longing.
translations.idiomatic: His kindness fell like rain clouds; his teaching lingers still. The people sang of their longing, and so we have the 'Song of Admiration.'

sentences.zh: 又孝女曹娥，年甫十四，貞順之德過越梁宋，其父墮江不得戶，娥仰天哀號，中流悲歎，便投水而死，父子喪屍，後乃俱出，國人哀其孝義，為歌《河女》之章。

translations.literal: Again the filial daughter Cao E, age just fourteen, her chaste and compliant virtue surpassed Yue, Liang, and Song; her father fell into the river and his body could not be recovered; E looked up to heaven and wailed, midstream sighed in grief, then threw herself into the water and died; father and son lost their corpses; afterward both came out; the people of the state pitied her filial righteousness and for her composed the piece "River Maid.
translations.idiomatic: There is also the filial girl Cao E, who at fourteen showed a devotion brighter than any tale from Yue, Liang, or Song. Her father drowned in the river and his body could not be found. She cried to heaven from midstream, then leaped in and died. Later both corpses rose together. The people mourned her devotion and sang the ballad we call 'The River's Daughter.'

sentences.zh: 伍子胥諫吳王，言不納用，見戮投海，國人痛其忠烈，為作《小海唱》。

translations.literal: Wu Zixu remonstrated with the king of Wu; his words were not adopted, and he was executed and cast into the sea; the people grieved for his loyal ardor and for him composed the "Little Sea Song."
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zixu warned the king of Wu and was ignored, they killed him and threw his body in the sea. The people mourned his fierce loyalty and sang the ballad called the 'Little Sea.'

sentences.zh: 今欲歌之。

translations.literal: Now I wish to sing it.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to sing it for you now.

sentences.zh: 」眾人僉曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The crowd all said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The listeners cried as one, "Yes—do!"

sentences.zh: 」統於是以足叩船，引聲喉囀，清激慷慨，大風應至，含水𠻳天，雲雨響集，叱吒歡呼，雷電晝冥，集氣長嘯，沙塵煙起。

translations.literal: " Tong then tapped the boat with his foot, drew out his voice in his throat, clear, piercing, and impassioned; a great wind answered and arrived; he held water in his mouth and sprayed the sky; cloud and rain sounds gathered; he shouted and cheered; thunder and lightning made noon dark; he gathered his breath in a long whistle; sand, dust, and smoke rose.
translations.idiomatic: Tong struck the hull with his foot and let his voice roll out—high, fierce, and full. Wind answered from nowhere; he spat a spray toward the sky until clouds and rain seemed to answer, roared and cheered until thunder rolled at noon, drew one long breath that howled like a gale, and kicked up dust like smoke.

sentences.zh: 王公已下皆恐，止之乃已。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward all were frightened; only when they stopped him did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone from the nobles down was terrified, and they had to beg him to stop before the storm died away.

sentences.zh: 諸人顧相謂曰：「若不游洛水，安見是人！

translations.literal: The men looked at one another and said, "If we had not come to sport on the Luo River, how could we have seen such a man!
translations.idiomatic: They turned to one another and said, "Had we not played on the Luo today, we would never have met this man!"

sentences.zh: 聽《慕歌》之聲，便仿佛見大禹之容。

translations.literal: Hearing the sound of the "Song of Longing," it was as though one dimly saw the countenance of Great Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard the 'Song of Admiration,' they could almost see the face of Yu the Great before them.

sentences.zh: 聞《河女》之音，不覺涕淚交流，即謂伯姬高行在目前也。

translations.literal: Hearing the sound of the "River Maid," without realizing it tears streamed down—then they said the high conduct of Bo Ji was present before their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The 'River's Daughter' left them weeping freely, as if the noble widow Bo Ji stood in their midst.

sentences.zh: 聆《小海》之唱，謂子胥、屈平立吾左右矣。

translations.literal: Listening to the song of the "Little Sea," they said Wu Zixu and Qu Ping stood at their left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The 'Little Sea' made them feel as though Zixu and Qu Yuan stood on either hand.

sentences.zh: 」充欲耀以文武鹵簿，覬其來觀，因而謝之，遂命建硃旗，舉幡校，分羽騎為隊，軍伍肅然。

translations.literal: " Chong wished to dazzle him with the civil and martial halberd escort, hoping he would come to watch and thereby apologize to him; therefore he ordered crimson banners raised and pennants with insignia lifted, dividing feathered riders into ranks so the host stood in grim order.
translations.idiomatic: Chong meant to overawe him with the full imperial guard—hoping he would look up from the river and soften—so he unfurled scarlet flags, broke out the drum corps, and drew up armored horse in disciplined ranks.

sentences.zh: 須臾，鼓吹亂作，胡葭長鳴，車乘紛錯，縱橫馳道，又使妓女之徒服袿襡，炫金翠，繞其船三匝。

translations.literal: In a moment, drums and pipes broke loose in confusion, Hu reed-pipes wailed long, carriages crossed in tangle, racing lengthwise and athwart the imperial roads; he also had singing-girls in pleated jackets shimmer with gold and kingfisher feathers and circle Tong's boat three times.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly music blared, long horns screamed, carriages clashed and careened along the avenues, and a ring of courtesans in brocade jackets—flashing gold and green—swept three circuits around his skiff.

sentences.zh: 統危坐如故，若無所聞。

translations.literal: Tong sat upright as before as if he heard nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Tong sat bolt upright and never seemed to hear a note.

sentences.zh: 充等各散曰：「此吳兒是木人石心也。

translations.literal: Chong and the others dispersed, saying, "This Wu lad has a heart of wood and stone."
translations.idiomatic: Chong and his party withdrew muttering, "The boy from Wu is wood and stone from the ribs up."

sentences.zh: 」統歸會稽，竟不知所終。

translations.literal: " Tong returned to Kuaiji; in the end it is not known where he ended.
translations.idiomatic: Tong went home to Kuaiji, and after that no one knows his fate.

sentences.zh: 朱沖，字巨容，南安人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Chong, styled Jurong, was a man of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chong, courtesy name Jurong, came from Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 少有至行，閑靜寡欲，好學而貧，常以耕藝爲事。

translations.literal: In youth he had consummate conduct, was calm and quiet with few desires, loved learning but was poor, and often took farming and gardening as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed uncommon decency: quiet, almost without wants, hungry for books yet destitute, he lived by tilling and tending crops.

sentences.zh: 鄰人失犢，認沖犢以歸，後得犢於林下，大慚，以犢還沖，沖竟不受。

translations.literal: A neighbor lost a calf and took Chong's calf home; later he found his calf in the grove and was greatly ashamed, and returned the calf to Chong, but Chong in the end would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor misidentified Chong's calf as his own and led it away; when he found his beast under the trees he brought Chong's calf back, shamefaced, but Chong would not take it.

sentences.zh: 有牛犯其禾稼，沖屢持芻送牛而無恨色。

translations.literal: When an ox trampled his grain, Chong repeatedly brought fodder to send the ox off without a look of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When someone's ox ruined his field, Chong kept bringing hay to the owner to feed it, never showing resentment.

sentences.zh: 主愧之，乃不復爲暴。

translations.literal: The owner was ashamed of this and thereafter did not let it rampage again.
translations.idiomatic: The owner, ashamed, kept the beast from doing further damage.

sentences.zh: 咸寧四年，詔補博士，沖稱疾不應。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning, an edict appointed him erudite; Chong pleaded illness and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianning 4 the court named him a doctorate; he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔曰：「東宮官屬亦宜得履蹈至行敦悅典籍者，其以沖爲太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Soon again an edict said, "The Eastern Palace staff also ought to include those who tread the utmost conduct and delight in the classics—let Chong be appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict soon followed: the heir apparent needed men of proven integrity who loved the canon—appoint Chong right tutor of the household.

sentences.zh: 」沖每聞徵書至，輒逃入深山，時人以爲梁管之流。

translations.literal: " Whenever Chong heard that a summons had arrived, he fled into the deep mountains; people of the time considered him of the stream of Liang and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever word of a call reached him, he bolted for the deep hills; contemporaries ranked him with Guanning of the eastern coast.

sentences.zh: 沖居近夷俗，羌戎奉之若君，沖亦以禮讓爲訓，邑里化之，路不拾遺，邨無凶人，毒蟲猛獸皆不爲害。

translations.literal: Chong dwelt close to barbarian customs; the Qiang and Rong served him as they would a lord, and Chong also instructed them in courtesy and yielding, so the village was transformed; nothing picked up on the road was kept, the hamlet had no violent men, and venomous insects and fierce beasts did none harm.
translations.idiomatic: He lived among tribesmen who honored him like a chief. He taught them deference, and the whole district changed: lost goods stayed where they fell, brawls vanished, and even snakes and beasts did not strike.

sentences.zh: 卒以壽終。

translations.literal: He ended his life at a full old age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 范粲，字承明，陳留外黃人，漢萊蕪長丹之孫也。

translations.literal: Fan Can, styled Chengming, was a man of Waihuang in Chenliu, a grandson of Fan Dan, magistrate of Laiwu in Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Can, courtesy name Chengming, was from Waihuang in Chenliu—a grandson of Fan Dan, who had been magistrate of Laiwu under the Han.

sentences.zh: 粲高亮貞正，有丹風，而博涉強記，學皆可師，遠近請益者甚眾，性不矜莊，而見之皆肅如也。

translations.literal: Can was lofty, bright, chaste, and upright; he had Dan's bearing, yet was broadly read with a strong memory, and all his learning could serve as a model; those near and far who sought instruction were very many; by nature he was not stiffly solemn, yet all who saw him were awed.
translations.idiomatic: He was as stern and honest as his grandfather Fan Dan, with a memory that drank in books. Students flocked to him from every quarter. He wore no air of pomp, yet everyone who met him stood straighter.

sentences.zh: 魏時州府交辟，皆無所就。

translations.literal: In Wei times the province and prefecture repeatedly summoned him; he took none of the posts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei, provincial and commandery posts came again and again; he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃應命為治中，轉別駕，辟太尉掾、尚書郎，出為征西司馬，所曆職皆有聲稱。

translations.literal: After a long while he then answered appointment as administrative adviser, transferred to chief clerk, was summoned as aide to the grand commandant and as gentleman of the palace, then went out as marshal on the western campaign; in every post he held he had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: At length he accepted a place as administrative adviser, rose to chief clerk, served as aide to the grand commandant and gentleman of the palace, then marched west as army marshal—winning praise in each office.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝輔政，遷武威太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan assisted the government, he was moved to governor of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took charge of the regency, Can was named governor of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 到郡，選良吏，立學校，勸農桑。

translations.literal: Arriving in the commandery, he selected good clerks, established schools, and urged farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: There he picked able officers, opened schools, and pushed farming and silk work.

sentences.zh: 是時戎夷頗侵疆場，粲明設防備，敵不敢犯，西域流通，無烽燧之警。

translations.literal: At that time the Rong and Yi often raided the borders; Can clearly set defenses so the enemy did not dare attack; the Western Regions flowed through trade and there was no alarm from beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians harried the frontier, but his clear dispositions kept them out; the Silk Road stayed open and the signal fires stayed cold.

sentences.zh: 又郡壤富實，珍玩充積，粲檢制之，息其華侈。

translations.literal: Moreover the commandery soil was rich and treasures filled the storehouses; Can checked and regulated this and stilled its luxury.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was rich and temptation everywhere; he tightened discipline and cut back extravagance.

sentences.zh: 以母老罷官。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he resigned office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office when his mother grew frail.

sentences.zh: 郡既接近寇戎，粲又重鎮輒去職，朝廷尤之，左遷樂涫令。

translations.literal: The commandery being close to raiding enemies, and Can again a key stronghold who abruptly left his post, the court blamed him and demoted him to magistrate of Leku.
translations.idiomatic: The court faulted him for walking away from a sensitive post on the barbarian edge and demoted him to magistrate of Leku.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉太宰從事中郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to retainer clerk with the grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was shifted to retainer clerk under the grand steward.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，以至孝稱。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and was famed for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's death plunged him into mourning famed for its grief.

sentences.zh: 服闕，復為太宰中郎。

translations.literal: When mourning was ended, he again became steward's retainer.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning term ended he returned as the steward's clerk.

sentences.zh: 齊王芳被廢，遷于金墉城，粲素服拜送，哀慟左右。

translations.literal: When Prince Qi of Cao Fang was deposed and moved to the Metal-walled City, Can in plain garb bowed in farewell, grieving so that those around him were moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Fang, the prince of Qi, was cast down and sent to the Metal Rampart palace, Can went in undyed linen to bow him off and wept until bystanders wept with him.

sentences.zh: 時景帝輔政，召群官會議，粲又不到，朝廷以其時望，優容之。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Jing assisted the government, he summoned the officials to a joint conference; Can again did not arrive; the court, because of his contemporary prestige, treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing called a plenary council; Can stayed away again, yet the court indulged him because of his moral weight.

sentences.zh: 粲又稱疾，闔門不出。

translations.literal: Can again pleaded illness and shut his gate, not going out.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness once more and barred his gate.

sentences.zh: 於是特詔為侍中，持節使於雍州。

translations.literal: Thereupon a special edict made him palace attendant with staff of authority and sent him on mission to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict named him palace attendant with credentials and ordered him to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 粲因陽狂不言，寢所乘車，足不履地。

translations.literal: Can therefore feigned madness and would not speak; he slept in the carriage he rode and his feet did not touch the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned madness and fell silent, living in his carriage so his feet never touched earth.

sentences.zh: 子孫恆侍左右，至有婚宦大事，輒密諮焉。

translations.literal: His sons and grandsons constantly attended at his side; even for great matters of marriage or office they secretly consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and grandsons waited on him always; even weddings and appointments they settled only after whispered questions at his pillow.

sentences.zh: 合者則色無變，不合則眠寢不安，妻子以此知其旨。

translations.literal: If it agreed, his color did not change; if it did not agree, then his sleep was restless; by this his wife and children knew his intent.
translations.idiomatic: If he approved, his face stayed calm; if not, he tossed all night—so his household read his mind.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，泰始中，粲同郡孫和時為太子中庶子，表薦粲，稱其操行高潔，久嬰疾病，可使郡縣輿致京師，加以聖恩，賜其醫藥，若遂瘳除，必有益於政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, in the Taishi years Sun He of Can's commandery, then junior tutor to the heir apparent, submitted a memorial recommending Can, praising his conduct as lofty and pure, long afflicted by illness, and saying the commandery and county could carry him in a litter to the capital; if the sagely favor granted him medicine and he then recovered, he would surely benefit governance.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin Wudi took the throne, Sun He—then junior tutor to the heir apparent and a townsman of Can—memorialized that Can's life was ascetic and his body long ill, that the counties should bring him to Luoyang in a litter, and that imperial physicians might restore him to the state's service.

sentences.zh: 乃詔郡縣給醫藥，又以二千石祿養病，歲以為常，加賜帛百匹。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the commandery and county to supply medicine, and also to support his illness with the salary of a two-thousand-bushel rank, yearly as a rule, adding a gift of one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered local officials to furnish physic and pay him a two-thousand-bushel stipend year after year to nurse his health, plus a hundred rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 子喬以父疾篤，辭不敢受，詔不許。

translations.literal: His son Qiao, because his father's illness was grave, declined and dared not accept; the edict did not permit refusal.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan Qiao, thinking the sickness grave, tried to decline the bounty; the edict refused the refusal.

sentences.zh: 乙太康六年卒，時年八十四，不言三十六載，終於所寢之車。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Taikang at age eighty-four; for thirty-six years he did not speak, and ended in the carriage in which he slept.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taikang 6 at eighty-four, having kept silence thirty-six years, and breathed his last in the cart that was his bed.

sentences.zh: 長子喬。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Fan Qiao.

sentences.zh: 喬字伯孫。

translations.literal: Qiao's courtesy name was Bosun.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qiao, courtesy name Bosun.

sentences.zh: 年二歲時，祖馨臨終，撫喬首曰：「恨不見汝成人！

translations.literal: At age two, when his grandfather Xin was at the point of death, he stroked Qiao's head and said, "I regret that I will not see you grown!"
translations.idiomatic: When Qiao was two, his dying grandfather Xin cupped his head and said, "I shall not live to see you a man!"

sentences.zh: 」因以所用硯與之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he gave him the inkstone he used.
translations.idiomatic: With that he pressed his own inkstone into the child's hands.

sentences.zh: 至五歲，祖母以告喬，喬便執硯涕泣。

translations.literal: When he reached five, his grandmother told Qiao, and Qiao then grasped the inkstone and wept.
translations.idiomatic: At five, when his grandmother told him the story, he clutched the inkstone and wept.

sentences.zh: 九歲請學，在同輩之中，言無媟辭。

translations.literal: At nine he requested schooling; among his peers his speech had no lewd words.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he began formal study; even among playmates he never used a coarse word.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，受業于樂安蔣國明。

translations.literal: At the capping age he received instruction from Jiang Guoming of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he studied under Jiang Guoming of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 濟陰劉公榮有知人之鑒，見喬，深相器重。

translations.literal: Liu Gongrong of Jiyin had a gift for judging men; when he saw Qiao he deeply esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongrong of Jiyin was famed for reading character; one meeting with Qiao won his deepest respect.

sentences.zh: 友人劉彥秋夙有聲譽，嘗謂人曰：「范伯孫體應純和，理思周密，吾每欲錯其一事而終不能。

translations.literal: His friend Liu Yanqiu long had a fine reputation; he once said to people, "Fan Bosun's substance answers to pure harmony; his reasoning is close-woven; I often wish to fault him on one point but to the end cannot."
translations.idiomatic: His friend Liu Yanqiu, himself celebrated, said, "Fan Bosun's nature is mild and his mind tight as mesh; I have tried a hundred times to catch him in a slip and never can."

sentences.zh: 」光祿大夫李銓嘗論楊雄才學優於劉向，喬以為向定一代之書，正群籍之篇，使雄當之，故非所長，遂著《劉楊優劣論》，文多不載。

translations.literal: " Minister Li Quan once argued that Yang Xiong's talent and learning surpassed Liu Xiang's; Qiao held that Xiang had fixed the books of an age and corrected the chapters of the canon—were Xiong to take his place, that was indeed not his strength—thereupon he composed the "On the Relative Merits of Liu and Yang"; the text is mostly not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Li Quan claimed Yang Xiong outshone Liu Xiang, Qiao answered that Xiang had settled the classics of an era—work Xiong could not have matched—and wrote a treatise comparing the two; the piece is omitted here for length.

sentences.zh: 喬好學不倦。

translations.literal: Qiao loved learning and did not tire.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao never wearied of books.

sentences.zh: 父粲陽狂不言，喬與二弟並棄學業，絕人事，侍疾家庭，至粲沒，足不出邑里。

translations.literal: When his father Can feigned madness and would not speak, Qiao with his two younger brothers abandoned their studies, cut off human affairs, and nursed the illness in the household until Can died, not stepping beyond the village.
translations.idiomatic: When his father feigned madness and silence, Qiao and his two brothers quit school, shut out the world, and nursed him until he died—never leaving their hamlet in all those years.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉劉毅嘗抗論於朝廷曰：「使范武威疾若不篤，是為伯夷、叔齊復存於今。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Liu Yi once spoke bluntly at court, saying, "If Fan Wuwei's illness is not grave, then Bo Yi and Shu Qi live again today.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi once told the court, "If Governor Fan's sickness is feigned, then Bo Yi and Shu Qi walk among us again.

sentences.zh: 如其信篤，益是聖主所宜哀矜。

translations.literal: If it is truly grave, all the more is it what a sage ruler ought to pity.
translations.idiomatic: If it is genuine, a sage king should pity him all the more.

sentences.zh: 其子久侍父疾，名德著茂，不加敘用，深為朝廷惜遺賢之譏也。

translations.literal: His sons have long attended a father's sickness; their fame and virtue shine bright—failure to employ them is a reproach the court will bear for wasting worthies."
translations.idiomatic: The sons have served a sick father for years with shining virtue; to leave them unranked is to invite the charge that the throne wastes good men."

sentences.zh: 」元康中，詔求廉讓沖退覆道寒素者，不計資，以參選敘。

translations.literal: " In the Yuankang period an edict sought men who were honest, yielding, retiring, and covered the Way in humble plainness, without regard to seniority, to be entered in selection.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuankang the throne sought modest scholars of cold pedigree, rank no object.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎王琨乃薦喬曰：「喬稟德真粹，立操高潔，儒學精深，含章內奧，安貧樂道，棲志窮巷，簞瓢詠業，長而彌堅，誠當今之寒素，著厲俗之清彥。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the palace Wang Kun then recommended Qiao, saying, "Qiao is endowed with virtue true and pure, established in conduct lofty and clean, deep in Confucian learning, holding pattern within, content with poverty and joyful in the Way, lodging his intent in a poor lane, with basket and gourd chanting his occupation—longer yet more firm—truly the cold plainness of today, a clear paragon to brace vulgar ways."
translations.idiomatic: Palace gentleman Wang Kun recommended him: pure in endowment, high in principle, steeped in the canon yet inward-turned, happy in poverty and fixed in purpose—"the very cold-clad scholar the age needs."

sentences.zh: 」時張華領司徒，天下所舉凡十七人，于喬特發優論。

translations.literal: " At the time Zhang Hua headed the ministry of education; of all the empire's nominees seventeen were listed, and for Qiao alone a superior appraisal was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua presided over the ministry; seventeen names came up from the realm, but only Qiao drew a special encomium.

sentences.zh: 又吏部郎郗隆亦思求海內幽遁之士，喬供養衡門，至於白首，於是除樂安令。

translations.literal: Also personnel director Xi Long wished to seek recluses within the seas; Qiao supported his parents at a brushwood gate until hoary age—thereupon he was appointed magistrate of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel director Xi Long also combed for hidden talent; learning that Qiao had kept his parents in a lane of wattles until their hair turned white, the court named him magistrate of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 辭疾不拜。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and never went.

sentences.zh: 喬凡一舉孝廉，八薦公府，再舉清白異行，又舉寒素，一無所就。

translations.literal: Qiao in all was once recommended filial and incorrupt, eight times recommended to the ducal offices, twice recommended for unsullied conduct out of the ordinary, and again recommended for cold plainness—he took none of them.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated once as filial-incorrupt, eight times to the Three Ducal Offices, twice for outstanding purity, once again for cold pedigree—and never accepted.

sentences.zh: 初，喬邑人臘夕盜斫其樹，人有告者，喬陽不聞，邑人愧而歸之。

translations.literal: At first, on New Year's eve a townsman stole and cut his tree; someone informed Qiao, but Qiao feigned not to hear; the townsman, ashamed, returned it.
translations.idiomatic: Once on New Year's Eve a neighbor felled one of his trees; when someone tattled, Qiao pretended not to hear until the culprit, ashamed, brought the timber back.

sentences.zh: 喬往喻曰：「卿節日取柴，欲與父母相歡娛耳，何以愧為！

translations.literal: Qiao went to instruct him, saying, "On the holiday you took firewood wanting to share joy with your parents—why be ashamed!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiao went to him and said, "You only wanted fuel for a feast with your parents—what shame is there in that?"

sentences.zh: 」其通物善導，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " His penetrating things and kindly guidance were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His tact in smoothing such matters was always like this.

sentences.zh: 外黃令高頵歎曰：「諸士大夫未有不及私者，而范伯孫恂恂率道，名諱未嘗經于官曹，士之貴異，於今而見。

translations.literal: Magistrate Gao Jun of Waihuang sighed, "Among gentlemen none fails to pursue private ends, yet Fan Bosun is earnest in following the Way; his name has never once passed through official offices—the nobility of scholars is visible today in him.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Gao Jun of Waihuang marveled, "Every gentleman chases some private gain, yet Bosun walks the Way with open hands—his name has never darkened a clerk's ledger. Here is proof that when the great Way fades, humanity and duty still appear."

sentences.zh: 大道廢而有仁義，信矣！

translations.literal: The great Way was ruined and then humanity and duty appeared—true indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: When the great Way is lost, ritual and right rise—how true that is!"

sentences.zh: 」其行身不穢，為物所嘆服如此。

translations.literal: " His conduct in life was unstained; he was admired by others to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: He lived without stain and won such admiration.

sentences.zh: 以元康八年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Yuankang at age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuankang 8 at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 魯勝，字叔時，代郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Sheng, styled Shushi, was a man of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sheng, courtesy name Shushi, came from Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有才操，為佐著作郎。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and integrity, and served as assistant editorialist.
translations.idiomatic: Young, able, and principled, he became assistant editorialist.

sentences.zh: 元康初，遷建康令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he was moved to magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he was named magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 到官，著《正天論》云：「以冬至之後立晷測影，准度日月星。

translations.literal: Arriving at office, he composed the "Correcting Heaven Treatise," saying, "After the winter solstice set a gnomon and measure shadow to gauge sun, moon, and stars.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he wrote a treatise called "Setting Heaven Right," arguing that from the winter solstice one should set a gnomon and read shadows to calibrate sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 臣案日月裁徑百里，無千里；

translations.literal: Your subject investigates: sun and moon are only a hundred li across, not a thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: He maintained that sun and moon span only a hundred leagues, not a thousand;

sentences.zh: 星十里，不百里。

translations.literal: stars ten li, not a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: and stars ten leagues, not a hundred.

sentences.zh: 」遂表上求下群公卿士考論。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial asking that it be sent down for the assembled dukes, ministers, and gentlemen to examine and debate.
translations.idiomatic: He tabled the essay and begged the high ministers to debate it.

sentences.zh: 「若臣言合理，當得改先代之失，而正天地之紀。

translations.literal: "If your subject's words accord with reason, then let him amend the errors of former ages and set right the pattern of heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: "If I speak with reason," he wrote, "let the court mend the mistakes of earlier calendars and set heaven's pattern straight.

sentences.zh: 如無據驗，甘即刑戮，以彰虛妄之罪。

translations.literal: If there is no supporting verification, I willingly accept execution at once to expose the crime of empty falsehood."
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot prove my case, I will gladly die to show the world I was a fraud."

sentences.zh: 」事遂不報。

translations.literal: " The matter in the end received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The throne never answered.

sentences.zh: 嘗歲日望氣，知將來多故，便稱疾去官。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day he once observed vapors and knew that coming years would bring much turmoil; then he pleaded illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Watching the year's omens at New Year he foresaw chaos and resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 中書令張華遣子勸其更仕，再徵博士，舉中書郎，皆不就。

translations.literal: Director Zhang Hua sent his son to urge him to take office again; twice he was summoned as erudite and recommended as palace secretary—he took none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua sent his son to coax him back; twice the court called him as erudite and nominated him palace secretary—he refused each time.

sentences.zh: 其著述為世所稱，遭亂遺失，惟注《墨辯》，存其敘曰：

translations.literal: His writings were praised by the world; lost in the disorders, only his commentary on the "Mohist Canons" survives, preserving its preface, which says:
translations.idiomatic: His other works perished in the wars; only his notes on the Mohist logic survive, with this preface:

sentences.zh: 名者所以別同異，明是非，道義之門，政化之準繩也。

translations.literal: Names are what distinguish same from different, clarify right from wrong; they are the gate of the Way and its duties, the plumb-line of government and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: "Names," he writes, "sort the same from the different and right from wrong; they are the doorway of moral teaching and the cord of statecraft."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「必也正名，名不正則事不成。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "There must be the correction of names; if names are not correct, affairs are not completed."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "The first task is to set names straight; when names wander, nothing can be finished."

sentences.zh: 」墨子著書，作《辯經》以立名本，惠施、公孫龍祖述其學，以正別名顯於世。

translations.literal: " Mozi wrote books and made the "Dialectic Canon" to establish the root of naming; Hui Shi and Gongsun Long carried on his learning and by correcting names became famous in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Mozi framed the 'Dialectic Canon' to ground naming; Hui Shi and Gongsun Long continued that teaching and won fame by parsing terms.

sentences.zh: 孟子非墨子，其辯言正辭則與墨同。

translations.literal: Mencius opposed Mozi, yet his disputatious words and correct phrases were the same as Mozi's.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius attacked Mozi, yet his own arguments matched Mohist rigor.

sentences.zh: 荀卿、莊周等皆非毀名家，而不能易其論也。

translations.literal: Xun Qing, Zhuang Zhou, and others all slandered the school of names, yet could not overturn its doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi and Zhuangzi mocked the logicians yet could not refute them.

sentences.zh: 名必有形，察形莫如別色，故有堅白之辯。

translations.literal: Names must have forms; to inspect form nothing surpasses distinguishing colors—therefore there is the debate of hard and white.
translations.idiomatic: Names cling to shapes; to read shapes one must sort colors—hence the paradox of hard and white.

sentences.zh: 名必有分明，分明莫如有無，故有無序之辯。

translations.literal: Names must have clear division; for clear division nothing surpasses being and nonbeing—therefore there is the debate of order in being and nonbeing.
translations.idiomatic: Names demand clear cuts; clearest cuts lie in being and nonbeing—hence the dispute over how nothing orders itself.

sentences.zh: 是有不是，可有不可，是名兩可。

translations.literal: What is may be not; what can be may be not able—this is the "both can" of names.
translations.idiomatic: What is may also not be; what can be done may be impossible—this is the 'double permission' of naming.

sentences.zh: 同而有異，異而有同，是之謂辯同異。

translations.literal: Same yet having difference, different yet having sameness—this is called debating sameness and difference.
translations.idiomatic: The same holds difference, the different holds sameness—this is how logicians split and join categories.

sentences.zh: 至同無不同，至異無不異，是謂辯同辯異。

translations.literal: Utmost same has nothing not same, utmost difference has nothing not different—this is called debating same, debating different.
translations.idiomatic: At the limit of sameness nothing fails to match; at the limit of difference nothing fails to part—those are the debates of pure same and pure difference.

sentences.zh: 同異生是非，是非生吉凶，取辯於一物而原極天下之汙隆，名之至也。

translations.literal: Sameness and difference beget right and wrong; right and wrong beget good and ill fortune; taking debate in one thing and tracing to the utmost the world's rise and decay—this is the utmost of naming.
translations.idiomatic: From same and different come right and wrong; from right and wrong, fortune and disaster. To argue one thing and thereby map the world's rise and fall—that is naming at its height.

sentences.zh: 自鄧析至秦時名家者，世有篇籍，率頗難知，後學莫復傳習，於今五百餘歲，遂亡絕，《墨辯》有上下《經》，《經》各有《說》，凡四篇，與其書眾篇連第，故獨存。

translations.literal: From Deng Xi down to the masters of names in Qin times, generation after generation had writings, but on the whole they were quite hard to understand; later students no longer transmitted or practiced them, and for more than five hundred years to the present they have perished and been cut off. The Mohist Canons have upper and lower Classics, and each Classic has Explanations—four pieces in all—which because they were numbered in sequence with the other chapters of that book alone survive.
translations.idiomatic: From Deng Xi through the Qin logicians, treatises survived yet were nearly unreadable; for five hundred years no one taught them, and they died out. Only the Mohist Canons endure—upper and lower classics, each with its commentary, four scrolls bound into the Mozi so they escaped oblivion.

sentences.zh: 今引說就經，各附其章，疑者闕之。

translations.literal: Now I draw the explanations up to the classics and attach each to its section; where there is doubt I leave a gap.
translations.idiomatic: I align each exegesis with its canon and mark doubtful lines; where the text fails, I leave the space blank.

sentences.zh: 又采諸眾雜集為《刑》《名》二篇，略解指歸，以俟君子。

translations.literal: I also gathered various miscellanies into two pieces, Punishments and Names, briefly sketching their purport to await a gentleman of discernment.
translations.idiomatic: I added two short essays, On Punishments and On Names, mapping their drift for a later reader who cares.

sentences.zh: 其或興微繼絕者，亦有樂乎此也！

translations.literal: If among them there are those who would revive what is faint and continue what is broken, might they not also find joy in this!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever would relight a dying lamp may find some pleasure here too.

sentences.zh: 董養，字仲道，陳留浚儀人也。

translations.literal: Dong Yang, styled Zhongdao, was a man of Junyi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yang, courtesy name Zhongdao, came from Junyi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，到洛下，不幹祿求榮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he arrived in Luoyang and did not seek salary or glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Taishi years he came to Luoyang seeking neither stipend nor fame.

sentences.zh: 及楊後廢，養因遊太學，升堂歎曰：「建斯堂也，將何為乎？

translations.literal: When Empress Yang was deposed, Yang therefore toured the Imperial Academy, ascended the hall, and sighed, "This hall was raised—what is it for?
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Yang was cast down, he climbed the academy hall and cried, "Why did we build this hall?

sentences.zh: 每覽國家赦書，謀反大逆皆赦，至於殺祖父母、父母不赦者，以為王法所不容也。

translations.literal: Whenever I read the state's amnesty edicts, great treason and rebellion are all pardoned, yet killing grandparents or parents is not pardoned—because royal law cannot contain it.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesties forgive treason yet never forgive parricide—that is where the law draws its line.

sentences.zh: 奈何公卿處議，文飾禮典，以至此乎！

translations.literal: How can it be that the dukes and ministers, sitting in council, garnish the ritual canons until things reach this pass!
translations.idiomatic: How could ministers varnish the rites until the law reads upside down?

sentences.zh: 天人之理既滅，大亂作矣。

translations.literal: The pattern of heaven and man is already extinguished; great chaos will arise.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven and humanity part company, the great upheaval follows.

sentences.zh: 」因著《無化論》以非之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed the Treatise on Non-Transformation to condemn it.
translations.idiomatic: He answered with his essay 'Against Change.'

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，洛城東北步廣里中地陷，有二鵝出焉，其蒼者飛去，白者不能飛。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia years the ground in Buguang ward northeast of Luoyang collapsed and two geese emerged; the gray one flew away, the white could not fly.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia the earth opened in Buguang ward and two geese crawled out—one gray that flew off, one white that could not.

sentences.zh: 養聞歎曰：「昔周時所盟會狄泉，即此地也。

translations.literal: Yang heard it and sighed, "In Zhou times the covenant place at the Di Spring was just this ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yang said, "This is the Di Spring where the Zhou lords swore their oaths.

sentences.zh: 今有二鵝，蒼者胡象，白者國家之象，其可盡言乎！

translations.literal: Now there are two geese: the gray is the image of the Hu, the white the image of the state—can one speak it to the end!
translations.idiomatic: The gray bird is the barbarians, the white our dynasty—need I spell the omen out?

sentences.zh: 顧謂謝鯤、阮孚曰：「《易》稱知機其神乎，君等可深藏矣。

translations.literal: " Turning to Xie Kun and Ruan Fu he said, "The Changes says, 'He who knows the pivot is spiritlike'—you gentlemen had better bury yourselves deep.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Xie Kun and Ruan Fu: 'The Book of Changes praises those who see the turning point—dig in deep, friends.

sentences.zh: 」乃與妻荷擔入蜀，莫知所終。

translations.literal: " Then he and his wife shouldered carrying-poles and entered Shu; none knows where they ended.
translations.idiomatic: He shouldered a pole and led his wife into Shu, and was never heard from again.

sentences.zh: 霍原，字休明，燕國廣陽人也。

translations.literal: Huo Yuan, styled Xiuming, was a man of Guangyang in the state of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yuan, courtesy name Xiuming, was from Guangyang in Yan.

sentences.zh: 少有志力，叔父坐法當死，原入獄訟之，楚毒備加，終免叔父。

translations.literal: In youth he had determination and strength; his uncle by law of a crime deserved death, Yuan entered prison to plead the case, full torture was applied, and in the end he spared his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he took tortures in prison to save an uncle condemned to die.

sentences.zh: 年十八，觀太學行禮，因留習之。

translations.literal: At eighteen he watched the Grand Academy perform rites and therefore stayed to practice them.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he watched the academy rites and stayed to master them.

sentences.zh: 貴游子弟聞而重之，欲與相見，以其名微，不欲晝往，乃夜共造焉。

translations.literal: Sons of the nobility heard and esteemed him, wishing to meet him; because his name was lowly they did not wish to go by day, so together they visited him by night.
translations.idiomatic: Great lords' sons respected him but thought his name too slight for a daylight call, so they came by torchlight.

sentences.zh: 父友同郡劉岱將舉之，未果而病篤，臨終，敕其子沈曰：「霍原慕道清虛，方成奇器，汝後必薦之。

translations.literal: His father's friend Liu Dai of the same commandery was about to recommend him, but without result fell gravely ill; at the point of death he charged his son Shen, saying, "Huo Yuan loves the Way, clear and empty; he will become a rare vessel—you must recommend him later.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai, his father's friend, meant to sponsor him but died first, telling his son Shen, 'Huo Yuan is a vessel in the making—remember to lift him up.'

sentences.zh: 」後歸鄉里。

translations.literal: " Later he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan went home to the hills.

sentences.zh: 高陽許猛素服其名，會為幽州刺史，將詣之，主簿當車諫不可出界，猛歎恨而止。

translations.literal: Xu Meng of Gaoyang had long admired his name; when he became governor of Youzhou he meant to visit him, but his chief clerk remonstrated from the cart that he could not go beyond the border, and Meng sighed with regret and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xu Meng of Gaoyang meant to call on him until his clerk barred a governor from crossing the line—Meng gave up with a sigh.

sentences.zh: 原山居積年，門徒百數，燕王月致羊酒。

translations.literal: Yuan dwelt in the mountains many years; disciples numbered in the hundreds; the prince of Yan monthly sent sheep and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He taught a hundred disciples in the hills while the prince of Yan sent monthly sheep and wine.

sentences.zh: 及劉沈為國大中正，元康中，進原為二品，司徒不過，沈乃上表理之。

translations.literal: When Liu Shen became grand impartial and just for the state, in Yuankang he advanced Yuan to second rank; the minister of education would not pass it, so Shen submitted a memorial to argue the case.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen ranked him second class; the ministry of education balked until Shen memorialized again.

sentences.zh: 詔下司徒參論，中書監張華令陳准奏為上品，詔可。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the minister of education to deliberate jointly; director Zhang Hua ordered Chen Zhun to memorialize him as highest grade, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua had Chen Zhun move him to the top grade, and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 元康末，原與王褒等俱以賢良徵，累下州郡，以禮發遣，皆不到。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuankang, Yuan with Wang Bao and others was summoned as worthy and good; repeatedly the commandery was ordered to dispatch him with ritual, and each time he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuankang he was summoned with Wang Bao as a worthy; the counties escorted him with full rites and he still would not go.

sentences.zh: 後王浚稱制謀僭，使人問之，原不答，浚心銜之。

translations.literal: Later Wang Jun seized power and plotted usurpation; he sent men to ask him, and Yuan did not answer; Jun harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun seized the government and sounded him out, Yuan stayed silent, and Jun nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 又有遼東囚徒三百餘人，依山為賊，意欲劫原為主事，亦未行。

translations.literal: Moreover more than three hundred convicts of Liaodong, relying on the mountains as bandits, wished to seize Yuan to be their leader, but also did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred Liaodong fugitives in the hills wanted him for chieftain but never acted.

sentences.zh: 時有謠曰：「天子在何許？

translations.literal: At the time a rhyme said, "Where is the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme asked, 'Where sits the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 近在豆田中。

translations.literal: Near at hand in the bean field.
translations.idiomatic: In the bean patch just ahead.'

sentences.zh: 」浚以豆為霍，收原斬之，懸其首。

translations.literal: " Jun took bean as Huo and seized Yuan and executed him, hanging up his head.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun read bean as Huo, seized Yuan, beheaded him, and spiked his head.

sentences.zh: 諸生悲哭，夜竊屍共埋殯之。

translations.literal: The students wept in grief; by night they stole the corpse and together buried it.
translations.idiomatic: His students stole the body by night and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 遠近駭愕，莫不冤痛之。

translations.literal: Far and near were shocked; none did not feel him wronged.
translations.idiomatic: The realm cried injustice.

sentences.zh: 郭琦，字公偉，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Guo Qi, styled Gongwei, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qi, courtesy name Gongwei, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少方直，有雅量，博學，善五行，作《天文志》、《五行傳》，注《穀梁》、《京氏易》百卷。

translations.literal: In youth he was square and straight, had a refined capacity, was broadly learned, skilled in the five phases, and composed the Monograph on Heaven, the Traditions of the Five Phases, and a hundred rolls of commentary on the Guliang Annals and the Jing family Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Young, upright, and learned in astrology, he wrote treatises on heaven, the five phases, and a hundred fascicles on the Guliang and Jing Changes.

sentences.zh: 鄉人王遊等皆就琦學。

translations.literal: His townsman Wang You and others all came to Qi to study.
translations.idiomatic: Townsmen such as Wang You studied at his feet.

sentences.zh: 武帝欲以琦為佐著作郎，問琦族人尚書郭彰。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu wished to make Qi assistant editorialist and asked Qi's clansman Minister Guo Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu meant to name him assistant editor and asked his kinsman Guo Zhang.

sentences.zh: 彰素疾琦，答云：「不識」。

translations.literal: Zhang by nature detested Qi and answered, "I do not know him."
