translations.idiomatic: Zhang hated him and said flatly, 'I never heard of him.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若如卿言，烏丸家兒能事卿，即堪為郎矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If it is as you say, then a Wuhuan household lad who can serve you would be fit to be a gentleman!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor retorted, 'If a Wuhuan stable-boy is good enough for you, he is good enough for my editorial office.'

sentences.zh: 」遂決意用之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he resolved to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: So the emperor appointed Qi anyway.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，又欲用琦，琦曰：「我已為武帝吏，不容復為今世吏。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao of Lun usurped the throne, he again wished to use Qi; Qi said, "I have already been an official to Emperor Wu; I cannot again be an official to today's world.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized the throne and offered a post, Qi answered, 'I served Emperor Wu; I will not serve your court.

sentences.zh: 」終身處於家。

translations.literal: " To the end of his life he remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed home for life.

sentences.zh: 伍朝，字世明，武陵漢壽人也。

translations.literal: Wu Chao, styled Shiming, was a man of Hanshou in Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chao, courtesy name Shiming, came from Hanshou in Wuling.

sentences.zh: 少有雅操，閒居樂道，不修世事。

translations.literal: In youth he had refined integrity, dwelt in retirement and delighted in the Way, and did not cultivate worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He loved quiet and the Way, and shunned the world's business.

sentences.zh: 性好學，以博士徵，不就。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning; he was summoned as erudite but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as erudite, he never went.

sentences.zh: 刺史劉弘薦朝為零陵太守，主者以非選例，不聽。

translations.literal: Inspector Liu Hong recommended Chao as governor of Lingling; the clerk in charge said it was not according to selection precedent and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong tried to name him governor of Lingling; the ministry blocked it as irregular.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎胡濟奏曰：「臣以為當今資喪亂之餘運，承百王之遺弊，進趨者乘國故以僥倖，守道者懷蘊櫝以終身，故令敦褒之化虧，退讓之風薄。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the palace Hu Ji memorialized, saying, "Your subject considers that the present rides the aftermath of ruin and loss, inherits the dregs of a hundred kings' ills; those who press forward ride state troubles to luck, while those who keep the Way hug their talents in a box to the end of life—therefore the transformation of honest praise is damaged and the wind of yielding and retiring is thin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ji told the throne that after chaos flatterers rose while the steadfast hid—so honest praise had waned.

sentences.zh: 案朝遊心物外，不屑時務，守靜衡門，志道日新，年過耳順而所尚無虧，誠江南之奇才，丘園之逸老也。

translations.literal: As for Chao, his mind roams outside things; he disdains the affairs of the moment, guards stillness at a brushwood gate, his aspiration for the Way renewed daily; past the age of sixty what he esteems is without flaw—truly a strange talent of the southland, a recluse elder of hill and garden.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's mind wanders beyond things; past sixty he still keeps a wattled gate and grows daily in the Way—a southern marvel, a hermit sage.

sentences.zh: 不加飾進，何以勸善！

translations.literal: If we do not add ornament and advancement, how shall we encourage the good!
translations.idiomatic: If we never honor such men, how do we teach the good?

sentences.zh: 且白衣為郡，前漢有舊，宜聽光顯，以獎風尚。

translations.literal: Moreover for a plain-robed man to become governor there is precedent in Former Han; it is fitting to hear the brilliance to reward custom and air.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners became magistrates under the Former Han—let this man shine to stiffen public morals.

sentences.zh: 」奏可，而朝不就，終於家。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved, yet Chao did not go, and ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: The edict passed, yet Chao stayed home and died there.

sentences.zh: 魯褒，字元道，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Bao, styled Yuandao, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bao, courtesy name Yuandao, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 好學多聞，以貧素自立。

translations.literal: He loved learning and heard much, and by poverty and plainness established himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned, widely read, and proud to stay poor.

sentences.zh: 元康之後，綱紀大壞，褒傷時之貪鄙，乃隱姓名，而著《錢神論》以刺之。

translations.literal: After Yuankang, the great net was badly torn; Bao grieved at the age's greed and baseness, therefore hid his name and composed the Discourse on the God of Cash to satirize it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuankang the moral net rotted; he hid his name and wrote the 'God of Cash' to mock the money-grubbers.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: In outline it said:
translations.idiomatic: It opens:

sentences.zh: 錢之為體，有乾坤之象，內則其方，外則其圓。

translations.literal: As a body, cash images Qian and Kun: within it is square, without it is round.
translations.idiomatic: Coin is shaped like heaven and earth—square inside, round skin.

sentences.zh: 其積如山，其流如川。

translations.literal: Its piles are like mountains; its flow like a river.
translations.idiomatic: Stacked it is a mountain; spent it is a stream.

sentences.zh: 動靜有時，行藏有節，市井便易，不患耗折。

translations.literal: In motion and rest it has its seasons; in going and hiding it has its measure; in market and well it is convenient to exchange, and one does not worry about wear or loss.
translations.idiomatic: It moves in season, rests by rule, trades easily in the market, and does not fear wear.

sentences.zh: 難折象壽，不匱象道，故能長久，為世神寶。

translations.literal: Hard to break, it images long life; never exhausted, it images the Way—therefore it can long endure and be the spirit treasure of the age.
translations.idiomatic: It breaks seldom like long life, runs never dry like the Way—so the world worships it.

sentences.zh: 親之如兄，字曰孔方，失之則貧弱，得之則富昌。

translations.literal: Men cherish it like an elder brother; its style is Kongfang—lose it and you are poor and weak; gain it and you are rich and thriving.
translations.idiomatic: Men call it Elder Brother Kongfang: lose him and you starve; win him and you flourish.

sentences.zh: 無翼而飛，無足而走，解嚴毅之顏，開難發之口。

translations.literal: Without wings it flies; without feet it runs; it unlocks stern faces and opens mouths that will not speak.
translations.idiomatic: It flies without wings, runs without feet, melts stern brows, loosens silent tongues.

sentences.zh: 錢多者處前，錢少者居後。

translations.literal: Those with much cash go in front; those with little stand behind.
translations.idiomatic: The rich coin walks first; the poor coin trails.

sentences.zh: 處前者為君長，在後者為臣僕。

translations.literal: Those in front are lords and elders; those behind are servants and slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The fore ranks play lord; the rear play slave.

sentences.zh: 君長者豐衍而有餘，臣僕者窮竭而不足。

translations.literal: The lords overflow with plenty; the servants are drained and wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Front ranks swim in surplus; the rear run dry.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「哿矣富人，哀此煢獨。」

translations.literal: The Odes says, 'How pleasant the rich man; pity these alone and helpless.'
translations.idiomatic: As the Classic of Poetry says, 'Happy the rich—pity the poor alone.'

sentences.zh: 錢之為言泉也，無遠不往，無幽不至。

translations.literal: As for cash, the word means 'spring': nothing far it does not go, nothing hidden it does not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Cash means 'springwater': it runs everywhere, even to the dark.

sentences.zh: 京邑衣冠，疲勞講肄，厭聞清談，對之睡寐，見我家兄，莫不驚視。

translations.literal: The caps and gowns of the capital, weary of lectures, tired of pure conversation, fall asleep facing it; when they see my elder brother none fail to stare wide-eyed.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's gentry, bored with seminars, nap through abstruse talk yet snap awake at Elder Brother.

sentences.zh: 錢之所祐，吉無不利，何必讀書，然後富貴！

translations.literal: Where cash lends its aid, auspicious is nothing not favorable—why must one read books and only then become noble and rich!
translations.idiomatic: Where it blesses, luck follows—who needs books if cash smiles?

sentences.zh: 昔呂公欣悅於空版，漢祖克之於贏二，文君解布裳而被錦繡，相如乘高蓋而解犢鼻，官尊名顯，皆錢所致。

translations.literal: In old days Lord Lü rejoiced in an empty tally, Han's founder conquered with an extra two cash; Wenjun cast off her linen skirt for brocade, Xiangru rode a high canopy and shed his calf-nose apron—rank high and names bright were all brought about by cash.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gong bowed to an empty bond, Gaozu won with two extra coins, Zhuo Wenjun traded sackcloth for silk, Sima Xiangru swapped cowherd shorts for a grand carriage—every rise came from cash.

sentences.zh: 空版至虛，而況有實；

translations.literal: The empty tally is utmost void—how much more what has substance!
translations.idiomatic: An empty bond is hollow—think what solid coin can do.

sentences.zh: 贏二雖少，以致親密。

translations.literal: The extra two were few, yet they won intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Two little coins bought an empire's favor.

sentences.zh: 由此論之，謂為神物。

translations.literal: Judging by this, call it a numinous thing.
translations.idiomatic: So men call it divine.

sentences.zh: 無德而尊，無勢而熱，排金門而入紫闥。

translations.literal: Without virtue yet honored, without power yet hot—it pushes the golden gate and enters the purple portals.
translations.idiomatic: Virtueless yet revered, powerless yet mighty—it shoulders past the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 危可使安，死可使活，貴可使賤，生可使殺。

translations.literal: Danger it can make safe; death it can make live; noble it can make base; alive it can make killed.
translations.idiomatic: It turns peril to peace, death to life, honor to shame, and living men to corpses.

sentences.zh: 是故忿爭非錢不勝，幽滯非錢不拔，怨仇非錢不解，令問非錢不發。

translations.literal: Therefore in angry quarrel without cash you do not win; in hidden obstruction without cash you do not rise; in hatred and vengeance without cash you do not resolve; in fair fame without cash you does not spread.
translations.idiomatic: No feud ends, no deadlock lifts, no grudge clears, no fair name flies without its nod.

sentences.zh: 洛中硃衣，當途之士，愛我家兄，皆我已已。

translations.literal: The vermilion robes of Luoyang, the men who block the road—all love my elder brother and never weary of him.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson officials and palace climbers never tire of my elder brother Kongfang.

sentences.zh: 執我之手，抱我終始，不計優劣，不論年紀，賓客輻輳，門常如市。

translations.literal: They grasp my hand and cling to my end, reckoning neither better nor worse, speaking neither of age; guests crowd like spokes to a hub, the gate ever like a market.
translations.idiomatic: They shake his hand from youth to age, heedless of rank or years; his gate is always a market.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「錢無耳，可使鬼。

translations.literal: The proverb says, 'Cash has no ears, yet can move ghosts.'
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs, 'Money has no ears, but it can command ghosts.'

sentences.zh: 」凡今之人，惟錢而已。

translations.literal: " As for people today, it is only cash.
translations.idiomatic: So men today worship only cash.

sentences.zh: 故曰軍無財，士不來；

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, an army without wealth, its knights will not come;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: no pay, no troops.

sentences.zh: 軍無賞，士不往。

translations.literal: An army without rewards, its knights will not go.
translations.idiomatic: No bounty, no charge.

sentences.zh: 仕無中人，不如歸田。

translations.literal: Without a go-between in office, better to return to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Serve without a broker in the ministry and you may as well plow.

sentences.zh: 雖有中人，而無家兄，不異無翼而欲飛，無足而欲行。

translations.literal: Even if there is a go-between, without my elder brother it is no different from wishing to fly without wings or walk without feet.
translations.idiomatic: Even with a patron, without Kongfang you are a bird without wings, a man without legs.

sentences.zh: 蓋疾時者共傳其文。

translations.literal: In general those who hated the times together passed around his text.
translations.idiomatic: Every cynic of the age copied his essay.

sentences.zh: 褒不仕，莫知其所終。

translations.literal: Bao did not take office; none knows where he ended.
translations.idiomatic: Bao never served; no one knows his end.

sentences.zh: 氾騰，字無忌，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Fan Teng, styled Wuji, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Teng, courtesy name Wuji, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，除郎中。

translations.literal: He was recommended filial and incorrupt and appointed gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Raised as filial-incorrupt, he became a gentleman of the palace.

sentences.zh: 屬天下兵亂，去官還家。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into military chaos, he left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When war swept the empire he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 太守張閟造之，閉門不見，禮遺一無所受。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Min visited him; he shut the gate and would not see him, and accepted none of the courteous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Min called; he barred the door and refused every gift.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「生於亂世，貴而能貧，乃可以免。

translations.literal: He sighed, saying, "Born in a disorderly age, to be noble yet able to be poor—only thus can one escape.
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'In a dark age stay high-minded and poor—that is how you survive.'

sentences.zh: 」散家財五十萬，以施宗族，柴門灌園，琴書自適。

translations.literal: " He scattered fifty myriad cash of family wealth to give to his lineage kin, wattled his gate, irrigated his garden, and with zither and books pleased himself.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away half a million to kin, wattled his gate, hoed his garden, and took his ease with lute and books.

sentences.zh: 張軌徵之為府司馬，騰曰：「門一杜，其可開乎！

translations.literal: Zhang Gui summoned him as clerk to his headquarters; Teng said, "Once the gate is shut, can it be opened!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui wanted him as marshal; Teng said, 'A shut gate should not reopen.

sentences.zh: 」固辭。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He refused flatly.

sentences.zh: 病兩月餘而卒。

translations.literal: After more than two months of illness he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after two months' illness.

sentences.zh: 任旭，字次龍，臨海章安人也。

translations.literal: Ren Xu, styled Cilong, was a man of Zhang'an in Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xu, courtesy name Cilong, came from Zhang'an in Linhai.

sentences.zh: 父訪，吳南海太守。

translations.literal: His father Fang was governor of Nanhai for Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren Fang had governed Nanhai under Wu.

sentences.zh: 旭幼孤弱，兒童時勤於學。

translations.literal: Xu in youth was orphaned and weak; in childhood he was diligent in study.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he studied with fierce diligence.

sentences.zh: 及長，立操清修，不染流俗，鄉曲推而愛之。

translations.literal: When grown, he established conduct clear and cultivated, dyed not by vulgar currents; the village pushed him forward and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he kept his life clean and won the hamlet's love.

sentences.zh: 郡將蔣秀嘉其名，請為功曹。

translations.literal: The commandery general Jiang Xiu admired his name and invited him to be merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: General Jiang Xiu of the commandery, admiring him, asked him to serve as merit clerk.

sentences.zh: 秀居官貪穢，每不奉法，旭正色苦諫。

translations.literal: Xiu in office was greedy and foul, often not obeying the law; Xu with stern countenance bitterly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xiu was corrupt and lawless; Xu rebuked him bluntly again and again.

sentences.zh: 秀既不納，旭謝去，閉門講習，養志而已。

translations.literal: Xiu would not accept; Xu took leave, shut his gate, lectured and studied, and nourished his intent only.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu brushed him off, Xu resigned, barred his door, and lived for his studies and his conscience.

sentences.zh: 久之，秀坐事被收，旭狼狽營送，秀慨然歎曰：「任功曹真人也。

translations.literal: After a long while Xiu was seized on a charge; Xu in disarray worked to send him off; Xiu sighed with feeling, saying, "Clerk Ren is a true man.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu fell under arrest, Xu scrambled to help him on his way; Xiu sighed, 'Ren Xu is the real thing.

sentences.zh: 吾違其讜言，以至於此，復何言哉！

translations.literal: I disobeyed his blunt counsel and reached this pass—what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: I ignored his straight talk and came to this—what is left to say?'

sentences.zh: 」尋察孝廉，除郎中，州郡仍舉為郡中正，固辭歸家。

translations.literal: " Soon he was examined filial and incorrupt, appointed gentleman of the palace; the province and commandery again nominated him as impartial and just for the commandery; he firmly declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu passed as filial-incorrupt, served briefly as gentleman, was pressed to be local evaluator, and each time went home instead.

sentences.zh: 永康初，惠帝博求清節俊異之士，太守仇馥薦旭清貞潔素，學識通博，詔下州郡以禮發遣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongkang, Emperor Hui broadly sought men of pure integrity and outstanding talent; Prefect Qiu Fu recommended Xu as chaste, clean, plain, his learning broad and penetrating; an edict ordered the commandery to dispatch him with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongkang 1 Emperor Hui cast a wide net for recluses; Prefect Qiu Fu praised Xu's purity and learning, and the court ordered him escorted with honors.

sentences.zh: 旭以朝廷多故，志尚隱遁，辭疾不行。

translations.literal: Xu, because the court had many troubles, his aspiration inclined to hidden retreat, pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Xu pleaded illness—the court was chaos and his heart was in the hills.

sentences.zh: 尋天下大亂，陳敏作逆，江東名豪並見羈縶，惟旭與賀循守死不回。

translations.literal: Soon the realm fell into great chaos; Chen Min rebelled; the famous magnates east of the Yang were all seized and bound; only Xu and He Xun guarded death and would not turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min rose, every Jiangdong notable was caged; only Xu and He Xun chose death over submission.

sentences.zh: 敏卒不能屈。

translations.literal: Min in the end could not bend them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min never broke them.

sentences.zh: 元帝初鎮江東，聞其名，召為參軍，手書與旭，欲使必到，旭固辭以疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan first garrisoned the east, hearing his name he summoned him as adviser, personally wrote to Xu wishing to make him surely come; Xu firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, first settling the east, summoned him as staff adviser and wrote in his own hand; Xu still pleaded sickness.

sentences.zh: 後帝進位鎮東大將軍，復召之；

translations.literal: Later when the emperor advanced to general who stabilizes the east, he summoned him again;
translations.idiomatic: When the prince rose to general of the east, he called again;

sentences.zh: 及為左丞相，辟為祭酒，並不就。

translations.literal: and when he became left chancellor, he summoned him as libationer—he took none of these posts.
translations.idiomatic: when he became left chancellor he offered the wine-cup post—Xu refused every one.

sentences.zh: 中興建，公車徵，會遭母憂。

translations.literal: When the restoration was founded, the state carriage summoned him; it happened he encountered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At the court's revival the summons came; his mother died that same hour.

sentences.zh: 于時司空王導啟立學校，選天下明經之士，旭與會稽虞喜俱以隱學被召。

translations.literal: At that time Minister Wang Dao proposed establishing schools and selecting men of clear classics from the empire; Xu with Yu Xi of Kuaiji were both summoned for their hidden learning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao then opened schools and wanted Xu and Yu Xi, famed recluses, to join.

sentences.zh: 事未行，會有王敦之難，尋而帝崩，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The affair had not been carried out when there occurred Wang Dun's rebellion; soon the emperor died, and the matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's coup came first; the emperor died; the plan died with him.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，又徵拜給事中，旭稱疾篤，經年不到，尚書以稽留除名，僕射荀崧議以為不可。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, he again summoned and appointed him palace counselor; Xu claimed grave illness, and for a full year did not arrive; the ministry struck his name for delay, but vice-director Xun Song argued it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming named him palace counselor; Xu stayed away a year until the ministry struck his name—Xun Song protested.

sentences.zh: 太寧末，明帝復下詔備禮徵旭，始下而帝崩。

translations.literal: At the end of Taining, Emperor Ming again issued an edict summoning Xu with full ritual; the edict had just been issued when the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taining another honored summons went out; the edict landed the day the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 咸和二年卒，太守馮懷上疏謂宜贈九列值蘇峻作亂，事竟不行。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Xianhe; Prefect Feng Huai submitted a memorial saying he should be posthumously honored to the nine ranks, but it happened Su Jun rebelled, and the affair in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianhe 2; Feng Huai asked posthumous rank to the Nine Ministers, but Su Jun's revolt buried the request.

sentences.zh: 子琚，位至大宗正，終於家。

translations.literal: His son Ju rose to grand director of the imperial clan and ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ren Ju reached grand director of the imperial surname and died at home.

sentences.zh: 郭文，字文舉，河內軹人也。

translations.literal: Guo Wen, styled Wenju, was a man of Zhi in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wen, courtesy name Wenju, came from Zhi in Henei.

sentences.zh: 少愛山水，尚嘉遁。

translations.literal: In youth he loved mountains and rivers and esteemed fine reclusion.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wild country and the name of recluse.

sentences.zh: 年三十，每游山林，彌旬忘反。

translations.literal: At thirty he often roamed forests and mountains, forgetting to return for a full ten days.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he would vanish into the hills for weeks on end.

sentences.zh: 父母終，服畢，不娶，辭家遊名山，歷華陰之崖，以觀石室之石函。

translations.literal: When his parents died and mourning was finished, he did not marry, left home to roam famous mountains, passed the cliffs of Huayin to view the stone casket in the stone chamber.
translations.idiomatic: After burying his parents he took no wife, left kin, and climbed Huayin to see the stone reliquary.

sentences.zh: 洛陽陷，乃步擔入吳興余杭大辟山中窮谷無人之地，倚木於樹，苫覆其上而居焉，亦無壁障。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell, he shouldered a carrying-pole and walked into the great Pi mountains of Wuxing Yuhang, to a remote valley without men; he leaned timbers on trees, thatched above them, and dwelt there, without even a wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he walked into the Pi range in Yuhang, leaned poles against trees, thatched a roof, and lived without walls.

sentences.zh: 時猛獸為暴，入屋害人，而文獨宿十餘年，卒無患害。

translations.literal: At the time fierce beasts ravaged, entering houses and harming people, yet Wen alone lodged there more than ten years and in the end suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts raided every hut but left him alone for ten years.

sentences.zh: 恆著鹿裘葛巾，不飲酒食肉，區種菽麥，采竹葉木實，貿鹽以自供。

translations.literal: He constantly wore deerskin and a ge cloth kerchief, drank no wine and ate no meat, hoed beans and wheat, gathered bamboo leaves and tree fruits, and bartered for salt to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wore buckskin and hemp kerchief, ate no meat, hoed beans, lived on forage, and traded for salt.

sentences.zh: 人或酬下價者，亦即與之。

translations.literal: If someone paid a low price, he still gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: If buyers underpaid, he let them.

sentences.zh: 後人識文，不復賤酬。

translations.literal: Later when people recognized Wen, they no longer underpaid.
translations.idiomatic: Once they knew him, they paid fair coin.

sentences.zh: 食有餘穀，輒恤窮匱。

translations.literal: When he had surplus grain he always relieved the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: He shared spare grain with the hungry.

sentences.zh: 人有臻遺，取其粗者，示不逆而已。

translations.literal: When people brought gifts he took only the coarse items, showing he did not refuse outright.
translations.idiomatic: When gifts came he took only the plain pieces to show courtesy, not greed.

sentences.zh: 有猛獸殺大麀鹿於庵側，文以語人，人取賣之，分錢與文。

translations.literal: A fierce beast killed a large deer beside his hut; Wen told people; they took and sold it and divided the cash with Wen.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger left a deer at his door; he told neighbors, they sold it and offered him coin.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「我若須此，自當賣之。

translations.literal: Wen said, "If I needed this, I would have sold it myself.
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, 'Had I wanted money I would have sold it myself.

sentences.zh: 所以相語，正以不須故也。

translations.literal: The reason I told you was precisely because I do not need it.
translations.idiomatic: I mentioned it only because I do not need the silver.'

sentences.zh: 」聞者皆嗟歎之。

translations.literal: " Those who heard all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, they marveled.

sentences.zh: 嘗有猛獸忽張口向文，文視其口中有橫骨，乃以手探去之，猛獸明旦致一鹿於其室前。

translations.literal: Once a fierce beast suddenly opened its mouth toward Wen; Wen saw a crossbone stuck in its mouth, then reached with his hand and removed it; the next morning the fierce beast brought a deer before his chamber.
translations.idiomatic: A beast gaped at him; he pulled a bone from its jaw; at dawn it laid a deer before his door.

sentences.zh: 獵者時往寄宿，文夜為擔水而無倦色。

translations.literal: Hunters sometimes came to lodge overnight; Wen by night carried water for them without a weary look.
translations.idiomatic: Hunters camped with him; he fetched their water night after night, untiring.

sentences.zh: 余杭令顧颺與葛洪共造之，而攜與俱歸。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Yuhang, Gu Yang, with Ge Hong together visited him and carried him back with them.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Gu Yang and Ge Hong visited him and carried him back to town.

sentences.zh: 颺以文山行或須皮衣，贈以韋袴褶一具，文不納，辭歸山中。

translations.literal: Yang, because Wen in mountain travel might need fur garments, presented him with one set of leather trousers and pleated jacket; Wen would not accept and returned to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yang gave him leather breeches for the cold; Wen refused and walked back to the hills.

sentences.zh: 颺追遣使者置衣室中而去，文亦無言，韋衣乃至爛於戶內，竟不服用。

translations.literal: Yang afterward sent a messenger who placed the clothes in the chamber and departed; Wen also said nothing; the leather garments even rotted inside the door; in the end he never wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang left the clothes in his hut; Wen never touched them until they rotted on the floor.

sentences.zh: 王導聞其名，遣人迎之，文不肯就船車，荷擔徒行。

translations.literal: Wang Dao heard his name and sent men to welcome him; Wen would not board boat or cart, but shouldered a pole and went on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao sent a coach; Wen shouldered his pole and walked.

sentences.zh: 既至，導置之西園，園中果木成林，又有鳥獸麋鹿，因以居文焉。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Dao placed him in the West Park, where fruit trees made a forest and moreover there were birds, beasts, and deer—thereby he lodged Wen there.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao housed him in West Park among orchards and tame deer.

sentences.zh: 於是朝士咸共觀之，文頹然踑踞，傍若無人。

translations.literal: Thereupon court gentlemen all together viewed him; Wen sat slumped, squatting with knees spread, as if no one were beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials came to gawk; Wen squatted like a stone, indifferent to the crowd.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠嘗問文曰：「人皆有六親相娛，先生棄之何樂？

translations.literal: Wen Qiao once asked Wen, "All men have six kin to enjoy themselves with—why do you abandon them, sir, and what joy is there?
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao asked why he abandoned family for the hills.

sentences.zh: 」文曰：「本行學道，不謂遭世亂，欲歸無路，是以來也。

translations.literal: " Wen said, "Originally I practiced the Way; I did not expect to meet the age in chaos; I wished to return but had no road—therefore I have come.
translations.idiomatic: Wen answered, 'I went out to study the Way; chaos penned me in with no road home—so I drifted here.'

sentences.zh: 」又問曰：「饑而思食，壯而思室，自然之性，先生安獨無情乎？

translations.literal: " Again he asked, "Hungry then one thinks of food; in vigor one thinks of chamber—such is nature's temper; how is it, sir, that you alone are without feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Qiao pressed: hunger and desire are natural—are you without feeling?'

sentences.zh: 」文曰：「情由憶生，不憶故無情。

translations.literal: " Wen said, "Feeling arises from memory; without memory therefore there is no feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, 'Passion feeds on memory; I forget, so I am still.'

sentences.zh: 」又問曰：「先生獨處窮山，若疾病遭命，則為烏鳥所食，顧不酷乎？

translations.literal: " Again he asked, "Sir, alone in a poor mountain, if illness meets fate, then you will be food for crows and kites—is it not cruel?
translations.idiomatic: Qiao asked whether dying alone on a peak was not cruel.

sentences.zh: 」文曰：「藏埋者亦為螻蟻所食，復何異乎！

translations.literal: " Wen said, "Those who are buried in earth are also eaten by ants—is there any difference!
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, 'Buried men feed ants too—what is the difference?'

sentences.zh: 」又問曰：「猛獸害人，人之所畏，而先生獨不畏邪？

translations.literal: " Again he asked, "Fierce beasts harm people; that is what men fear—yet sir, you alone are not afraid?
translations.idiomatic: Qiao asked why he did not fear beasts.

sentences.zh: 」文曰：「人無害獸之心，則獸亦不害人。

translations.literal: " Wen said, "When men have no mind to harm beasts, then beasts also do not harm people.
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, 'Men who wish beasts no harm need not fear them.'

sentences.zh: 」又問曰：「苟世不寧，身不得安。

translations.literal: " Again he asked, "Suppose the age is not peaceful and the person cannot be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao asked how he would serve a troubled age.

sentences.zh: 今將用先生以濟時，若何？

translations.literal: Now we wish to employ sir to aid the times—how about it?
translations.idiomatic: The court would use him to save the times—would he?

sentences.zh: 」文曰：「山草之人，安能佐世！

translations.literal: " Wen said, "A man of mountain grass—how can he assist the age!
translations.idiomatic: Wen laughed: 'A weed from the hills cannot prop the age.'

sentences.zh: 」導嘗眾客共集，絲竹並奏，試使呼之。

translations.literal: " Dao once gathered many guests together; strings and winds played together; he tried ordering Wen summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao once held a banquet with music and called him in.

sentences.zh: 文瞪眸不轉，跨躡華堂如行林野。

translations.literal: Wen stared without turning his eyes, strode across the splendid hall as though walking forest and field.
translations.idiomatic: Wen stared straight ahead and crossed the marble hall like a path in the woods.

sentences.zh: 于時坐者咸有鉤深味遠之言，文常稱不達來語。

translations.literal: At that time those seated all had words that hooked the deep and tasted the far; Wen always said he did not understand the speech that had come.
translations.idiomatic: Guests spouted abstruse philosophy; Wen always said he could not follow.

sentences.zh: 天機鏗宏，莫有窺其門者。

translations.literal: Heaven's mechanism was vast and ringing; none could spy his gate.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was a locked drum—no one found the key.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠嘗稱曰：「文有賢人之性，而無賢人之才，柳下、梁踦之亞乎！

translations.literal: Wen Qiao once praised him, saying, "Wen has the nature of a worthy man but not the talent of a worthy man—perhaps he is of the class of Liuxia Hui and Liang Qi!
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao ranked him near Liuxia Hui—virtue without court polish.

sentences.zh: 」永昌中，大疫，文病亦殆。

translations.literal: " In the Yongchang period there was a great pestilence; Wen's illness also was near death.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang a plague swept the city; Wen nearly died.

sentences.zh: 王導遺藥，文曰：「命在天，不在藥也。

translations.literal: Wang Dao sent medicine; Wen said, "Life lies with heaven, not with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao sent physic; Wen said, 'Life belongs to heaven, not to drugs.

sentences.zh: 夭壽長短，時也。」

translations.literal: Short life or long is a matter of season."
translations.idiomatic: Long or short span is timing alone.'

sentences.zh: 居導園七年，未嘗出入。

translations.literal: He dwelt in Dao's park seven years and never went out.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years in Wang Dao's park—never a step outside.

sentences.zh: 一旦忽求還山，導不聽。

translations.literal: One morning he suddenly begged to return to the mountains; Dao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: One dawn he begged to return; Wang Dao refused.

sentences.zh: 後逃歸臨安，結廬舍於山中。

translations.literal: Later he fled back to Lin'an and built a hut in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped back to Lin'an and raised a hut.

sentences.zh: 臨安令萬寵迎置縣中。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Lin'an, Wan Chong, welcomed him and lodged him in the county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Wan Chong housed him in the yamen.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻反，破余杭，而臨安獨全，人皆異之，以為知機。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, he destroyed Yuhang, yet Lin'an alone remained intact; people all marveled, thinking he knew the pivot.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun sacked Yuhang, Lin'an stood untouched—folk called it foresight.

sentences.zh: 自後不復語，但舉手指麾，以宣其意。

translations.literal: Afterward he no longer spoke but only raised his fingers in gesture to declare his intent.
translations.idiomatic: After that he spoke only with hand signs.

sentences.zh: 病甚，求還山，欲枕石安屍，不令人殯葬，寵不聽。

translations.literal: When his illness was severe he begged to return to the mountains, wishing to pillow his corpse on stone and not let men bury him; Chong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he asked to lie on stone without funeral; Wan Chong refused.

sentences.zh: 不食二十餘日，亦不瘦。

translations.literal: For more than twenty days he did not eat, yet he did not grow thin.
translations.idiomatic: He fasted twenty days yet never wasted.

sentences.zh: 寵問曰：「先生復可得幾日？

translations.literal: Chong asked, "Sir, how many days have you left?
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chong asked how many days remained.

sentences.zh: 」文三舉手，果以十五日終。

translations.literal: " Wen thrice raised his hand; indeed on the fifteenth day he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wen lifted three fingers—he died on the fifteenth day as he signaled.

sentences.zh: 寵葬之于所居之處而祭哭之，葛洪、庾闡並為作傳，讚頌其美云。

translations.literal: Chong buried him at the place where he had dwelt and sacrificed and wept for him; Ge Hong and Yu Chan both composed biographies, praising and singing his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chong buried him where he lived; Ge Hong and Yu Chan wrote his lives, praising his grace.

sentences.zh: 龔壯，字子瑋，巴西人也。

translations.literal: Gong Zhuang, styled Ziwei, was a man of Brazil.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang, courtesy name Ziwei, came from Brazil.

sentences.zh: 潔己自守，與鄉人譙秀齊名。

translations.literal: He kept himself pure and guarded his integrity, of one fame with his townsman Qiao Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He matched his townsman Qiao Xiu for stainless repute.

sentences.zh: 父叔為李特所害，壯積年不除喪，力弱不能復仇。

translations.literal: His father was killed by Li Te; Zhuang for years did not remove mourning, his strength being weak and unable to avenge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te had his father killed; Zhuang wore mourning for years, too weak to strike back.

sentences.zh: 及李壽戍漢中，與李期有嫌，期，特孫也，壯欲假壽以報，乃說壽曰：「節下若能並有西土，稱籓于晉，人必樂從。

translations.literal: When Li Shou garrisoned Hanzhong and had a rift with Li Qi—Qi was Li Te's grandson—Zhuang wished to borrow Shou to take revenge, and therefore persuaded Shou, saying, "If you, sir, can swallow the western lands whole and declare vassalage to Jin, men will surely gladly follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shou feuded with Li Qi, Zhuang urged Shou to seize the west and submit to Jin.

sentences.zh: 且舍小就大，以危易安，莫大之策也。

translations.literal: Moreover to forsake the small and embrace the great, to trade peril for safety—there is no greater strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Trade a small throne for a great protectorship—no wiser plan.'

sentences.zh: 」壽然之，遂率眾討期，果克之。

translations.literal: " Shou agreed, then led hosts to attack Qi and indeed overcame him.
translations.idiomatic: Shou agreed, crushed Li Qi, and took power.

sentences.zh: 壽猶襲偽號，欲官之，壯誓不仕，賂遺一無所取。

translations.literal: Shou still assumed a false title and wished to office him; Zhuang swore he would not serve and accepted none of the bribes or gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Shou still played emperor and offered posts; Zhuang refused every bribe.

sentences.zh: 會天久雨，百姓饑墊，壯上書說壽以歸順，允天心，應人望，永為國籓，福流子孫。

translations.literal: It happened heaven rained long; the people starved; Zhuang submitted a memorial urging Shou to submit, accord with heaven's mind, answer men's hopes, forever be a vassal state of the dynasty, and extend blessing to sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: When famine came he memorialized Shou to yield to Jin and save the people.

sentences.zh: 壽省書內愧，秘而不宣。

translations.literal: Shou read the letter, felt shame within, and hid it without proclaiming it.
translations.idiomatic: Shou hid the memorial, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使入胡，壯又諫之，壽又不納。

translations.literal: Then he sent envoys into the Hu; Zhuang again remonstrated; Shou again did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shou then courted the Hu; Zhuang warned again; Shou ignored him.

sentences.zh: 壯謂百行之本莫大忠孝，即假壽殺期，私仇以雪，又欲使其歸朝，以明臣節。

translations.literal: Zhuang considered that of the hundred conducts none is greater than loyalty and filial piety: having borrowed Shou to kill Qi, his private revenge was avenged, yet he also wished to make him return to court to clarify ministerial integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang had used Shou to kill his foe yet still wanted Jin's suzerainty honored.

sentences.zh: 壽既不從，壯遂稱聾，又云手不制物，終身不復至成都，惟研考經典，譚思文章，至李勢時卒。

translations.literal: Shou would not follow; Zhuang then claimed deafness, also said his hands could not grasp things, to the end of his life did not again go to Chengdu, only grinding through the classics and pondering texts, and died under Li Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou refused, Zhuang feigned deafness and paralysis, never returned to Chengdu, studied until Li Shi's day, and died.

sentences.zh: 初，壯每歎中夏多經學，而巴蜀鄙陋，兼遭李氏之難，無復學徒，乃著《邁德論》，文多不載。

translations.literal: At first Zhuang often sighed that the central plain abounded in classical learning while Ba and Shu were rustic; moreover they suffered the Li clan's disasters and had no more students; therefore he composed the "On Surpassing Virtue"; the text is mostly not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote 'On Surpassing Virtue' to mourn learning lost in Shu—text omitted here.

sentences.zh: 孟陋，字少孤，武昌人也。

translations.literal: Meng Lou, styled Shaogu, was a man of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Lou, courtesy name Shaogu, came from Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 吳司空宗之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was great-grandson of Wu's minister of works Meng Zong.
translations.idiomatic: He was great-grandson of Wu minister Meng Zong.

sentences.zh: 兄嘉，桓溫征西長史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Meng Jia was chief clerk on Huan Wen's western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Meng Jia had been chief clerk under Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 陋少而貞立，清操絕倫，布衣蔬食，以文籍自娛。

translations.literal: Lou in youth was chaste and established, his pure conduct unmatched, in plain cloth and coarse food, taking pleasure in books.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was chaste, austere, in sackcloth and gruel, happy only in books.

sentences.zh: 口不及世事，未曾交遊，時或弋釣，孤興獨往，雖家人亦不知其所之也。

translations.literal: His mouth did not touch the affairs of the age; he never socialized; sometimes he shot or fished, alone with his whim—even his household did not know where he went.
translations.idiomatic: He never gossiped, rarely visited anyone, fished or hunted alone—his family never knew his path.

sentences.zh: 喪母，毀瘠殆於滅性，不飲酒食肉十有餘年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he wasted his flesh almost to extinguishing nature; for more than ten years he drank no wine and ate no meat.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's death left him skeletal; he ate no meat over ten years.

sentences.zh: 親族迭謂之曰：「少孤！

translations.literal: Lineage kin in turn said to him, "Shaogu!
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen pleaded, 'Shaogu!

sentences.zh: 誰無父母？

translations.literal: Who lacks parents?
translations.idiomatic: Who has no parents?

sentences.zh: 誰有父母！

translations.literal: Who has parents!
translations.idiomatic: Who keeps parents forever?

sentences.zh: 聖人制禮，令賢者俯就，不肖企及。

translations.literal: The sages fixed ritual to let the worthy bend down and the unworthy strive up.
translations.idiomatic: The sages set rites so the wise may ease grief and fools may aim higher.

sentences.zh: 若使毀性無嗣，更為不孝也。

translations.literal: If you destroy your nature and leave no heir, that is again unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: To die childless is the greater unfilial act.'

sentences.zh: 陋感此言，然後從吉。

translations.literal: Lou was moved by these words; then afterward he followed auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: He heard them, relented, and ended mourning properly.

sentences.zh: 由是名著海內。

translations.literal: From this his name was famed within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: His name then filled the empire.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝輔政，命為參軍，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he ordered him as adviser; he claimed illness and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen summoned him as adviser; he pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 桓溫躬往造焉。

translations.literal: Huan Wen in person went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen himself knocked on his door.

sentences.zh: 或謂溫曰：「孟陋高行，學為儒宗，宜引在府，以和鼎味。

translations.literal: Someone said to Wen, "Meng Lou's conduct is lofty; his learning is patriarch of Confucians—it is fitting to draw him into the office to harmonize the cauldron's flavor."
translations.idiomatic: A friend told Huan Wen, 'Meng Lou's virtue tops the scholars; bring him to your staff to leaven the court.'

sentences.zh: 」溫歎曰：「會稽王尚不能屈，非敢擬議也。

translations.literal: " Wen sighed, saying, "The prince of Kuaiji still could not bend him—how dare I presume to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Wen sighed, 'Even the prince of Kuaiji could not move him—I hardly dare speak of hiring him.'

sentences.zh: 」陋聞之曰：「桓公正當以我不往故耳。

translations.literal: " Lou heard it and said, "Lord Huan only thinks it is because I did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Lou heard and said, 'Huan Wen only thinks I snubbed him on purpose.'

sentences.zh: 億兆之人，無官者十居其九，豈皆高士哉！

translations.literal: Of the myriad million men, nine in ten have no office—are they all lofty gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Nine men in ten lack office—are they all recluses?

sentences.zh: 我疾病不堪恭相王之命，非敢為高也。

translations.literal: I am ill and cannot bear the respectful commands of the minister king—it is not that I dare be lofty.
translations.idiomatic: I am too sick to obey the prince's summons—that is no pose of pride.'

sentences.zh: 」由是名稱益重。

translations.literal: " From this his reputation and title grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: His name only grew weightier after that.

sentences.zh: 博學多通，長於《三禮》。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and penetrating, excelling in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 注《論語》，行於世。

translations.literal: He annotated the Analects, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Analects commentary circulates still.

sentences.zh: 卒以壽終。

translations.literal: He ended his life at a full old age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 韓績，字興齊，廣陵人也。

translations.literal: Han Ji, styled Xingqi, was a man of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji, courtesy name Xingqi, came from Guangling.

sentences.zh: 其先避亂，居於吳之嘉興。

translations.literal: His ancestors fled turmoil and dwelt in Jiaxing of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His clan fled war and settled in Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 父建，仕吳至大鴻臚。

translations.literal: His father Jian served Wu to grand herald.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han Jian rose to grand herald under Wu.

sentences.zh: 績少好文學，以潛退為操，布衣蔬食，不交當世，由是東土並宗敬焉。

translations.literal: Ji in youth loved letters and learning, taking hidden retirement as his conduct, in plain cloth and coarse food, not associating with the age—thereby the eastern lands together honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books, lived poor, shunned office, and the whole east coast revered him.

sentences.zh: 司徒王導聞其名，辟以為掾，不就。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Dao heard his name and summoned him as aide; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao summoned him as clerk; he stayed away.

sentences.zh: 咸康末，會稽內史孔愉上疏薦之，詔以安車束帛徵之。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiankang, interior secretary of Kuaiji Kong Yu submitted a memorial recommending him; an edict ordered him summoned with peace carriage and bundled silks.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xiankang Kong Yu recommended him; the court sent carriage and silk.

sentences.zh: 尚書令諸葛恢奏績名望猶輕，未宜備禮，於是召拜博士。

translations.literal: Director of the secretariat Zhuge Hui memorialized that Ji's fame was still light and it was not yet fitting to use full ritual; thereupon he was summoned and appointed erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui said his name was still slight; the court named him erudite instead.

sentences.zh: 稱老病不起，卒於家。

translations.literal: He claimed old age and illness and would not rise; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded age and died at home.

sentences.zh: 于時高密劉鮞字長魚、城陽邴郁字弘文，並有高名。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Jun of Gaomi, styled Changyu, and Bing Yu of Chengyang, styled Hongwen, both had lofty names.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun of Gaomi and Bing Yu of Chengyang shared his fame.

sentences.zh: 鮞幼不慕俗，長而希古，篤學厲行，化流邦邑。

translations.literal: Jun from youth did not admire the vulgar; grown, he aspired to antiquity, studied deeply and disciplined conduct, transforming his district.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun scorned fashion, copied the ancients, and reshaped his town.

sentences.zh: 郁，魏徵士原之曾孫，少有原風，敕身謹潔，口不妄說，耳不妄聽，端拱恂恂，舉動有禮。

translations.literal: Yu was great-grandson of Wei recluse Bing Yuan; in youth he had Yuan's air, ordering the self chaste and clean, mouth not speaking rashly, ears not listening rashly, sitting upright and earnest, every motion with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yu was Bing Yuan's heir: silent, careful, every gesture correct.

sentences.zh: 咸康中，成帝博求異行之士，鮞、鬱並被公卿薦舉，於是依績及翟湯等例，以博士徵之。

translations.literal: In Xiankang, Emperor Cheng broadly sought men of unusual conduct; Jun and Yu were together recommended by dukes and ministers; thereupon according to the precedent of Ji and Zhai Tang and others they were summoned as erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng sought odd talents; both were nominated like Han Ji and Zhai Tang.

sentences.zh: 鬱辭以疾，鮞隨使者到京師，自陳年老，不拜。

translations.literal: Yu declined on grounds of illness; Jun followed the envoy to the capital, personally declaring old age and not taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pleaded sick; Liu Jun went to the capital, declared himself too old, and refused the cap.

sentences.zh: 各以壽終。

translations.literal: Each ended life at a full old age.
translations.idiomatic: Both died in honored old age.

sentences.zh: 譙秀，字元彥，巴西人也。

translations.literal: Qiao Xiu, styled Yuanyan, was a man of Brazil.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xiu, courtesy name Yuanyan, came from Brazil.

sentences.zh: 祖周，以儒學著稱，顯明蜀朝。

translations.literal: His ancestor Zhou was famed for Confucian learning and illustrious in the Shu court.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Qiao Zhou was a famed scholar of Shu Han.

sentences.zh: 秀少而靜默，不交於世，知天下將亂，預絕人事，雖內外宗親，不與相見。

translations.literal: Xiu from youth was still and silent, did not associate with the world; knowing the realm would soon fall into chaos, beforehand cut off human affairs—even inner and outer lineage kin he did not meet.
translations.idiomatic: He foresaw chaos, cut ties, and would not even see kin.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，州舉秀才，皆不就。

translations.literal: The commandery examined him filial and incorrupt; the province raised him cultivated talent; he took neither.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every provincial summons.

sentences.zh: 及李雄據蜀，略有巴西，雄叔父驤、驤子壽皆慕秀名，具束帛安車徵之，皆不應。

translations.literal: When Li Xiong held Shu and annexed Brazil, Xiong's uncle Xiang and Xiang's son Shou both admired Xiu's name, fully preparing bundled silks and peace carriage to summon him; he answered neither.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong's clan offered carriage and silk; he ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 常冠皮弁，弊衣，躬耕山藪。

translations.literal: He constantly wore leather cap and tattered clothes, personally plowing mountain marsh.
translations.idiomatic: He farmed in buckskin cap and rags.

sentences.zh: 龔壯常嘆服焉。

translations.literal: Gong Zhuang often sighed in admiration at him.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang marveled at his resolve.

sentences.zh: 桓溫滅蜀，上疏薦之，朝廷以秀年在篤老，兼道遠，故不徵，遣使敕所在四時存問。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen destroyed Shu he submitted a memorial recommending him; the court, because Xiu's years were very old and moreover the road was distant, therefore did not summon him, but sent an envoy ordering the place to inquire seasonally.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen recommended him after the conquest of Shu; the court, citing age and distance, only sent seasonal greetings.

sentences.zh: 尋而范賁、蕭敬相繼作亂，秀避難宕渠，鄉里宗族依憑之者以百數。

translations.literal: Soon Fan Ben and Xiao Jing in succession rebelled; Xiu fled trouble to Dangqu; lineage and clan who relied on him numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Ben rose, a hundred clansmen sheltered under his staff.

sentences.zh: 秀年出八十，眾人欲代之負擔，秀曰：「各有老弱，當先營護。

translations.literal: Xiu's years passed eighty; the crowd wished to carry his load for him; Xiu said, "Each has old and weak—one ought first to plan and protect them.
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty, kin wished to carry his gear; he said, 'You have elders and babes to tend first.'

sentences.zh: 吾氣力猶足自堪，豈以垂朽之年累諸君也！

translations.literal: My breath and strength still suffice to bear myself—how could I, in these withered years, burden you gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: I can still shoulder my pack—do not load my age on you.'

sentences.zh: 」年九十餘卒。

translations.literal: He died past ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died past ninety.

sentences.zh: 翟湯，字道深，尋陽人。

translations.literal: Zhai Tang, styled Daoshen, was a man of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Tang, courtesy name Daoshen, was from Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 篤行純素，仁讓廉潔，不屑世事，耕而後食，人有饋贈，雖釜庾一無所受。

translations.literal: He practiced earnestly, pure and plain, benevolent, yielding, honest, and clean; he disdained worldly affairs, plowed and afterward ate; if people sent gifts, even cauldrons and measures he accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: He was kind, frugal, refused gifts—even a pot of grain.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，寇害相繼，聞湯名德，皆不敢犯，鄉人賴之。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia, bandit harm followed one after another; hearing Tang's name and virtue, none dared violate him; his townsfolk relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjia's chaos bandits spared his village for his name.

sentences.zh: 司徒王導辟，不就，隱于縣界南山。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Dao summoned him; he did not go, and hid on South Mountain within the county border.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao summoned him; he hid on South Mountain.

sentences.zh: 始安太守干寶與湯通家，遣船餉之，敕吏云：「翟公廉讓，卿致書訖，便委船還。

translations.literal: Prefect of Shi'an Gan Bao was connected by family to Tang and sent a boat to supply him, instructing the clerk, saying, "Lord Zhai is honest and yielding—you, sir, when you have delivered the letter, then leave the boat and return.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao, his kinsman-by-marriage, sent a boat of supplies, telling the crew to drop the cargo and leave.

sentences.zh: 」湯無人反致，乃貨易絹物，因寄還寶。

translations.literal: " Tang had no man to send it back; therefore he sold goods for silk and sent it back to Bao through a broker.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai sold goods for silk and repaid him.

sentences.zh: 寶本以為惠，而更煩之，益愧歎焉。

translations.literal: Bao had thought it a kindness, yet it only troubled him the more; he increased in shame and admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao meant a favor yet felt only shame and deeper respect.

sentences.zh: 咸康中，征西大將軍庾亮上疏薦之，成帝徵為國子博士，湯不起。

translations.literal: In Xiankang, General Who Stabilizes the West Yu Liang submitted a memorial recommending him; Emperor Cheng summoned him as national university erudite; Tang did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang recommended him; Emperor Cheng named him national erudite; he stayed home.

sentences.zh: 建元初，安西將軍庾翼北征石季龍，大發僮客以充戎役，敕有司特蠲湯所調。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan, General Who Pacifies the West Yu Yi on northern campaign against Shi Hu greatly conscripted retainers and guests to fill military service, ordering the offices specially to remit Tang's levy.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi's levy on retainers skipped Zhai Tang by edict.

sentences.zh: 湯悉推僕使委之鄉吏，吏奉旨一無所受，湯依所調限，放免其僕，使令編戶為百姓。

translations.literal: Tang pushed all servants and handed them to the village clerk; the clerk, receiving the order, accepted nothing; Tang according to the conscription limit dismissed his servants, letting them register as common households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai handed his servants to the clerk, refused special favor, and freed them to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 康帝復以散騎常侍徵湯，固辭老疾，不至。

translations.literal: Emperor Kang again with attendant censor regular summoned Tang; he firmly declined old age and illness and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang summoned him as attendant censor; again he pleaded age.

sentences.zh: 年七十三，卒於家。

translations.literal: At seventy-three he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three at home.

sentences.zh: 子莊，字祖休。

translations.literal: His son Zhuang, styled Zuxiu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhai Zhuang, courtesy name Zuxiu.

sentences.zh: 少以孝友著名，遵湯之操，不交人物，耕而後食，語不及俗，惟以弋釣為事。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed for filial piety and friendship; he observed Tang's conduct, did not associate with people, plowed and afterward ate, speech not touching the vulgar, only taking archery and fishing as occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang copied his father's life: farmed, fished, shunned gossip.

sentences.zh: 及長，不復獵。

translations.literal: When grown, he no longer hunted.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he gave up hunting.

sentences.zh: 或問：「漁獵同是害生之事，而先生止去其一，何哉？

translations.literal: Someone asked, "Fishing and hunting are alike in harming living things—yet the master only removes one; why?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked why he quit hunting but still fished.

sentences.zh: 」莊曰：「獵自我，釣自物，未能頓盡，故先節其甚者。

translations.literal: " Zhuang said, "Hunting comes from myself; fishing comes from the thing—I could not cut off both at once, therefore I first restrained the greater.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang said, 'Hunting is my cruelty; fish choose the hook—I curbed the worse first.'

sentences.zh: 且夫貪餌吞鉤，豈我哉！

translations.literal: Moreover greed for bait and swallowing the hook—is that I!
translations.idiomatic: Fish greedily take hooks—how is that my sin?'

sentences.zh: 」時人以為知言。

translations.literal: " People of the time considered it a knowing saying.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners called it wise.

sentences.zh: 晚節亦不復釣，端居篳門，歠菽飲水。

translations.literal: In his late years he also no longer fished, sitting upright at a brushwood gate, sipping beans and drinking water.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he quit fishing too, lived on beans and water.

sentences.zh: 州府禮命，及公車徵，並不就。

translations.literal: Commandery and prefecture ritual summons and state carriage summons together he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every summons.

sentences.zh: 年五十六，卒。

translations.literal: At fifty-six he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 子矯，亦有高操，屢辭辟命。

translations.literal: His son Jiao also had lofty conduct, repeatedly declining summons.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhai Jiao kept the same path.

sentences.zh: 矯子法賜，孝武帝以散騎郎徵，亦不至。

translations.literal: Jiao's son Fasi was summoned as attendant cavalier by Emperor Xiaowu and likewise did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu summoned Fasi; he too stayed away.

sentences.zh: 世有隱行云。

translations.literal: The age said they had a lineage of hidden conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The family was called a line of recluses.

sentences.zh: 郭翻，字長翔，武昌人也。

translations.literal: Guo Fan, styled Changxiang, was a man of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Fan, courtesy name Changxiang, came from Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 伯父訥，廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His uncle by seniority Ne was governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Guo Ne governed Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父察，安城太守。

translations.literal: His father Cha was governor of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guo Cha governed Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 翻少有志操，辭州郡辟及賢良之舉。

translations.literal: Fan in youth had determination and conduct; he declined provincial summons and recommendations as worthy and good.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful, he refused every nomination.

sentences.zh: 家於臨川，不交世事，惟以漁釣射獵為娛。

translations.literal: His household was at Linchuan; he did not touch worldly affairs, taking only fishing, angling, and hunting as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Linchuan on fishing and hunting.

sentences.zh: 居貧無業，欲墾荒田，先立表題，經年無主，然後乃作。

translations.literal: Poor without livelihood, he wished to open wasteland; first he set up a marker inscription; after a full year without owner, then he worked it.
translations.idiomatic: He marked abandoned land, waited a year, then plowed.

sentences.zh: 稻將熟，有認之者，悉推與之。

translations.literal: When the rice was about to ripen, someone claimed it; he entirely pushed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor claimed the field, he gave the whole crop away.

sentences.zh: 縣令聞而詰之，以稻還翻，翻遂不受。

translations.literal: The magistrate heard and questioned him, returning the rice to Fan; Fan then would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate forced the rice back; Fan still refused.

sentences.zh: 嘗以車獵，去家百餘里，道中逢病人，以車送之，徒步而歸。

translations.literal: Once by cart he hunted, more than a hundred li from home; on the road he met a sick man, gave him the cart to send him, and walked back on foot.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his cart to a sick stranger and walked home.

sentences.zh: 其漁獵所得，或從買者，便與之而不取直，亦不告姓名。

translations.literal: What he gained by fishing and hunting, if there were buyers, he then gave it to them and did not take payment, nor did he tell his name.
translations.idiomatic: He gave game to buyers, took no pay, left no name.

sentences.zh: 由是士庶咸敬貴焉。

translations.literal: Thereby gentlemen and commoners alike revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners alike honored him.

sentences.zh: 與翟湯俱為庾亮所薦，公車博士徵，不就。

translations.literal: Together with Zhai Tang he was recommended by Yu Liang; summoned erudite by state carriage; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang recommended him with Zhai Tang; he ignored the doctorate call.

sentences.zh: 咸康末，乘小船暫歸武昌省墳墓，安西將軍庾翼以帝舅之重，躬往造翻，欲強起之。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiankang he rode a small boat briefly returning to Wuchang to visit tombs; General Who Pacifies the West Yu Yi, by weight of being the emperor's maternal uncle, in person went to visit Fan, wishing to force him to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, the emperor's uncle, boarded his skiff at Wuchang to drag him to office.

sentences.zh: 翻曰：「人性各有所短，焉可強逼！

translations.literal: Fan said, "Human nature each has its short—how can it be forced!
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, 'Every man has limits—do not force mine.'

sentences.zh: 」翼又以其船小狹，欲引就大船。

translations.literal: " Yi again because his boat was small and narrow wished to draw him to a great boat.
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked him onto a larger barge.

sentences.zh: 翻曰：「使君不以鄙賤而辱臨之，此固野人之舟也。

translations.literal: Fan said, "If the commissioner does not disdain my base and lowly self and condescends to visit, this is indeed a wild man's boat.
translations.idiomatic: Fan answered, 'This skiff suits a countryman; honor it as you find it.'

sentences.zh: 」翼俯屈入其船中，終日而去。

translations.literal: " Yi bent low and entered his boat; all day then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi crawled into the tiny boat and sat with him all day.

sentences.zh: 嘗墜刀于水，路人有為取者，因與之。

translations.literal: Once he dropped a knife in the water; a passerby retrieved it for him, and he gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped a knife in a stream; a farmer fished it out and Fan offered it as gift.

sentences.zh: 路人不取，固辭，翻曰：「爾向不取，我豈能得！

translations.literal: The passerby would not take it and firmly declined; Fan said, "If you just now had not taken it, how could I have obtained it!
translations.idiomatic: The man would not keep it; Fan said, 'If you refuse, neither of us owns it.'

sentences.zh: 」路人曰：「我若取此，將為天地鬼神所責矣。

translations.literal: " The passerby said, "If I took this, I would be blamed by heaven, earth, and the ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: The man said, 'If I kept it, heaven would blame me.'

sentences.zh: 」翻知其終不受，復沈刀于水。

translations.literal: " Fan knew he in the end would not accept, again sank the knife in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Fan sank the knife again.

sentences.zh: 路人悵焉，乃復沈沒取之。

translations.literal: The passerby was disappointed; then again dived and retrieved it.
translations.idiomatic: The farmer dove and brought it back, vexed.

sentences.zh: 翻於是不逆其意，乃以十倍刀價與之。

translations.literal: Fan then did not go against his intent, then gave him ten times the knife's price.
translations.idiomatic: Fan paid him tenfold the knife's worth and let him keep it.

sentences.zh: 其廉不受惠，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His honesty in not accepting favor was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his stubborn honesty.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 辛謐，字叔重，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Mi, styled Shuzhong, was a man of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mi, courtesy name Shuzhong, came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父怡，幽州刺史，世稱冠族。

translations.literal: His father Yi was governor of Youzhou; the age called them a cap clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin Yi governed Youzhou; the clan wore high caps in reputation.

sentences.zh: 謐少有志尚，博學善屬文，工草隸書，為時楷法。

translations.literal: Mi in youth had aspiration and esteem, was broadly learned and skilled at composing texts, worked cursive and clerical script, and was model for the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was a scholar and calligrapher others copied.

sentences.zh: 性恬靜，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: By nature quiet and still, he did not rashly associate or roam.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly and made few friends.

sentences.zh: 召拜太子舍人、諸王文學，累徵不起。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed heir-apparent attendant and literary instructor to the various princes; repeatedly summoned, he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him tutor to princes; he never went.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，以謐兼散騎常侍，慰撫關中。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he was appointed concurrently attendant censor regular to comfort Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongjia the court sent him west as envoy.

sentences.zh: 謐以洛陽將敗，故應之。

translations.literal: Mi because Luoyang was about to be defeated, therefore answered.
translations.idiomatic: He went because he saw Luoyang falling.

sentences.zh: 及長安陷沒于劉聰，聰拜太中大夫，固辭不受。

translations.literal: When Chang'an fell to Liu Cong, Cong appointed grand palace grandee; he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong offered a grandee title; he refused.

sentences.zh: 又曆石勒、季龍之世，並不應辟命。

translations.literal: Again through the eras of Shi Le and Shi Hu he answered no summons.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and Shi Hu could not move him either.

sentences.zh: 雖處喪亂之中，頹然高邁，視榮利蔑如也。

translations.literal: Although he dwelt amid ruin and chaos, he was lofty and transcendent, looking on glory and profit as nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Through war after war he stayed aloof from rank.

sentences.zh: 及冉閔僭號，復備禮徵為太常，謐遺閔書曰：「昔許由辭堯，以天下讓之，全其清高之節。

translations.literal: When Ran Min usurped the title, again with full ritual he summoned him as grand master of ceremonies; Mi sent Min a letter saying, "In old days Xu You declined Yao and with the realm yielded to him, preserving his lofty and clean integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Ran Min seized the throne and offered the grand astrologer post, Xin wrote comparing himself to Xu You and Boyi.

sentences.zh: 伯夷去國，子推逃賞，皆顯史牒，傳之無窮。

translations.literal: Boyi left the state; Zituo fled reward—all appear in the histories and transmit without end.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi and Jie Zitui fled power—names that never die.

sentences.zh: 此往而不反者也。

translations.literal: These went and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: They left court never to return.

sentences.zh: 然賢人君子雖居廟堂之上，無異于山林之中，斯窮理盡性之妙，豈有識之者邪！

translations.literal: Yet worthy men and gentlemen, although they dwell atop the temple hall, are no different from being in mountains and forests—such is the subtlety of exhausting pattern and completing nature—how could there be those who recognize it!
translations.idiomatic: Yet a sage at court may be no different from a sage on the hill—who sees that truth?

sentences.zh: 是故不嬰於禍難者，非為避之，但冥心至趣而與吉會耳。

translations.literal: Therefore those not entangled in disaster and harm are not thereby avoiding them; only silent mind and utmost purpose meet with auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who escape calamity are not hiding—they simply still the heart until fortune finds them.

sentences.zh: 謐聞物極則變，冬夏是也；

translations.literal: Mi heard that when a thing reaches its limit it changes—winter and summer are so;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mi wrote that all things turn at the limit—winter and summer prove it.

sentences.zh: 致高則危，累棋是也。

translations.literal: to reach height is to be in danger—a piled chess tower is so.
translations.idiomatic: Stack too high and you topple—like a tower of stones.

sentences.zh: 君王功以成矣，而久處之，非所以顧萬全遠危亡之禍也。

translations.literal: The lord king's merit is already accomplished; yet to dwell long in it is not the way to look to complete safety and distance the calamity of ruin and death.
translations.idiomatic: Your merit is won; to cling to power is not the way to stay safe.

sentences.zh: 宜因茲大捷，歸身本朝，必有許由、伯夷之廉，享松喬之壽，永為世輔，豈不美哉！

translations.literal: It is fitting to take this great victory to return your person to the proper court—surely you will have the honesty of Xu You and Boyi, enjoy the years of Chisong and Wang Qiao, forever be the age's pillar—how could it not be beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Yield now, return to Jin, and win the clean fame of Xu You—live long as a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」因不食而卒。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he refused food and died.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped eating and died.

sentences.zh: 劉驎之

translations.literal: Liu Linzhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Linzhi

sentences.zh: 劉驎之，字子驥，南陽人，光祿大夫耽之族也。

translations.literal: Liu Linzhi, styled Ziji, was a man of Nanyang, of the clan of grand master of the palace Liu Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Linzhi, courtesy name Ziji, of Nanyang, was kin to Liu Dan.

sentences.zh: 驎之少尚質素，虛退寡欲，不修儀操，人莫之知。

translations.literal: Linzhi in youth esteemed plain simplicity, was empty and retiring with few desires, did not cultivate deportment or bearing—no one knew him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved plain living and shunned display—no one noticed him.

sentences.zh: 好遊山澤，志存遁逸。

translations.literal: He loved to roam mountains and marshes; his intent lodged in flight and reclusion.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered peaks and meant to hide.

sentences.zh: 嘗采藥至衡山，深入忘反，見有一澗水，水南有二石囷，一囷閉，一囷開，水深廣不得過。

translations.literal: Once gathering herbs he reached Mount Heng, went deep and forgot to return; he saw a stream; south of the water were two stone granaries, one closed, one open; the water was deep and wide and he could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: On Hengshan he found twin stone silos by a ford too deep to cross.

sentences.zh: 欲還，失道，遇伐弓人，問徑，僅得還家。

translations.literal: Wishing to return, he lost the way; met a bow-cutter, asked the path, barely got home.
translations.idiomatic: He lost the trail until a woodcutter pointed the way home.

sentences.zh: 或說囷中皆仙靈方藥諸雜物，驎之欲更尋索，終不復知處也。

translations.literal: Some said the granaries held immortal recipes and medicines and various things; Linzhi wished to search again, but never again knew the place.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the silos held immortal drugs; he searched again and never found them.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍桓沖聞其名，請為長史，驎之固辭不受。

translations.literal: General Who Chariots and Horses Huan Chong heard his name and invited him as chief clerk; Linzhi firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong offered chief clerk; he refused.

sentences.zh: 沖嘗到其家，驎之于樹條桑，使者致命，驎之曰：「使君既枉駕光臨，宜先詣家君。

translations.literal: Chong once arrived at his house; Linzhi was picking mulberry on a branch; the envoy delivered the command; Linzhi said, "Since the commissioner has condescended to visit in person, he ought first to visit my father.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Chong called, Liu was in the mulberry tree and said, 'Honor my father first.'

sentences.zh: 」沖聞大愧，於是乃造其父。

translations.literal: " Chong heard and was greatly ashamed; thereupon he went to create his father.
translations.idiomatic: Chong flushed and went in to greet the old man first.

sentences.zh: 父命驎之，然後方還，拂短褐與沖言話。

translations.literal: The father ordered Linzhi; only then did he return, brushing his short hemp coat and conversing with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: His father sent him down; Liu brushed his coat and spoke with Chong.

sentences.zh: 父使驎之於內自持濁酒蔬菜供賓，沖敕人代驎之斟酌，父辭曰：「若使從者，非野人之意也。

translations.literal: The father had Linzhi inside personally hold turbid wine and vegetables to supply the guest; Chong ordered someone pour for Linzhi in his stead; the father declined, saying, "If you use followers, it is not the intent of a wild man.
translations.idiomatic: Liu served wine himself; when Chong sent a servant the father said, 'A rustic host pours his own cup.'

sentences.zh: 」沖慨然，至昏乃退。

translations.literal: " Chong sighed; only at dusk did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Chong stayed until dusk, moved.

sentences.zh: 驎之雖冠冕之族，信儀著於群小，凡廝伍之家婚娶葬送，無不躬自造焉。

translations.literal: Although Linzhi was of a capped-and-ribbon clan, his trust and bearing showed among the petty folk; for weddings, burials, and send-offs of common hireling households, none did he not personally visit.
translations.idiomatic: Though born noble, he attended every poor neighbor's wedding and funeral.

sentences.zh: 居於陽岐，在官道之側，人物來往，莫不投之。

translations.literal: He dwelt at Yangqi, beside the official road; people and goods coming and going all turned in to him.
translations.idiomatic: His house stood by the post road; every traveler stopped for his charity.

sentences.zh: 驎之躬自供給，士君子頗以勞累，更憚過焉。

translations.literal: Linzhi personally supplied them; gentlemen thought it laborious and increasingly feared passing there.
translations.idiomatic: He fed them all himself until travelers dreaded the detour.

sentences.zh: 凡人致贈，一無所受。

translations.literal: Whatever people brought as gifts, he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He took no gifts.

sentences.zh: 去驎之家百餘里，有一孤姥，病將死，歎息謂人曰：「誰當埋我，惟有劉長史耳！

translations.literal: More than a hundred li from Linzhi's home was a lone old woman, ill and about to die, who sighed and said to people, "Who will bury me—only Chief Clerk Liu!
translations.idiomatic: A dying crone miles away cried, 'Only Liu will bury me!

sentences.zh: 何由令知。

translations.literal: By what means can I let him know.
translations.idiomatic: How can he hear?'

sentences.zh: 」驎之先聞其有患，故往侯之，值其命終，乃身為營棺殯送之。

translations.literal: " Linzhi had earlier heard she was ill, therefore went to inquire; it happened she expired at that moment; then he personally for her arranged coffin and burial and sent her off.
translations.idiomatic: He had heard her cough, arrived as she died, and buried her himself.

sentences.zh: 其仁愛隱惻若此。

translations.literal: His benevolence and hidden pity were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his kindness.

sentences.zh: 卒以壽終。

translations.literal: He ended his life at a full old age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in honored age.

sentences.zh: 索襲，字偉祖，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Suo Xi, styled Weizu, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Xi, courtesy name Weizu, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 虛靖好學，不應州郡之命，舉孝廉、賢良方正，皆以疾辭。

translations.literal: Empty and still, loving learning, he answered no commandery summons; recommended filial and incorrupt, worthy and upright—each time he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He declined every nomination as ill.

sentences.zh: 游思於陰陽之術，著天文地理十餘篇，多所啟發。

translations.literal: He roamed thought in yin-yang arts and composed more than ten pieces on astronomy and geography, much enlightening.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote on heaven and earth and the dark arts.

sentences.zh: 不與當世交通，或獨語獨笑，或長歎涕泣，或請問不言。

translations.literal: He did not traffic with the age; sometimes he spoke alone and laughed alone, or long sighed and wept, or when asked questions would not speak.
translations.idiomatic: He muttered alone, wept alone, fell silent when questioned.

sentences.zh: 張茂時，敦煌太守陰澹奇而造焉，經日忘反，出而歎曰：「索先生碩德名儒，真可以諮大義。

translations.literal: Under Zhang Mao, Dunhuang prefect Yin Dan, marveling, visited him; for a full day he forgot to return, and coming out sighed, "Master Suo is a great virtue and famed Confucian—truly one may consult him on great right.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yin Dan spent a day with him and called him a walking scripture.

sentences.zh: 」澹欲行鄉射之禮，請襲為三老，曰：「今四表輯寧，將行鄉射之禮，先生年耆望重，道冠一時，養老之義，實系儒賢。

translations.literal: " Dan wished to perform the village archery rite and invited Xi as elder of three, saying, "Now within the four borders there is peace; we are about to perform the village archery rite; the master, old in years and heavy in repute, his Way caps the age—the meaning of supporting the aged truly hangs on such Confucian worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Yin asked him to preside as village elder at the archery rite.

sentences.zh: 既樹非梧桐，而希鸞鳳降翼；

translations.literal: Yet though you have not planted a phoenix tree, you hope for phoenix wings to descend;
translations.idiomatic: You are no phoenix tree yet hope phoenixes to roost—

sentences.zh: 器謝曹公，而冀蓋公枉駕，誠非所謂也。

translations.literal: though your vessel is not Lord Cao, you hope Master Gai will condescend to visit—indeed this is not what is called fitting.
translations.idiomatic: you are no Duke Cao yet hope sages to call—this will not do.'

sentences.zh: 然夫子至聖，有召赴焉；

translations.literal: Yet the Master was utmost sage and when summoned went;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius answered summons—

sentences.zh: 孟軻大德，無聘不至，蓋欲弘闡大猷，敷明道化故也。

translations.literal: Mencius had great virtue—without summons he did not arrive—because he wished to spread the great plan and make clear the transformation of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius waited for the right invite—both taught the world.

sentences.zh: 今之相屈，遵道崇教，非有爵位，意者或可然乎！

translations.literal: Now summoning you bends to the Way and honors teaching; there are no ranks and offices—perhaps it may be so!"
translations.idiomatic: I call you only to honor learning, not for rank—say you will come.'

sentences.zh: 」會病卒，時年七十九。

translations.literal: It happened he died of illness at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 澹素服會葬，贈賤二萬。

translations.literal: Dan in plain garb attended the funeral and presented two myriad cash of condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Dan mourned in undyed linen and sent twenty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 澹曰：「世人之所有餘者，富貴也；

translations.literal: Dan said, "What the world has in surplus is wealth and honor;
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, 'The world hoards riches—

sentences.zh: 目之所好者，五色也；

translations.literal: what the eye loves is the five colors;
translations.idiomatic: eyes crave color—

sentences.zh: 耳之所玩者，五音也。

translations.literal: what the ear plays with is the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: ears crave music.'

sentences.zh: 而先生棄眾人之所收，收眾人之所棄，味無味於慌惚之際，兼重玄於眾妙之內。

translations.literal: Yet the master casts aside what the multitude gathers, gathers what the multitude casts aside; he savors the tasteless in the vast blur, doubles dark mystery within the myriad subtleties.
translations.idiomatic: Master Suo chose poverty, tasted the void, doubled the mystery others flee.

sentences.zh: 宅不彌畝而志忽九州，形居塵俗而棲心天外，雖黔婁之高遠，莊生之不願，蔑以過也。

translations.literal: His house does not fill a mu yet his intent forgets the nine provinces; his form dwells in dust and vulgarity yet his mind roosts beyond heaven—though Qian Lou's loftiness, Zhuangzi's unwillingness, none surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: His hut was tiny yet his mind held the empire; not even Zhuangzi outdid him.'

sentences.zh: 」乃諡曰玄居先生。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they gave the posthumous title Master of Mysterious Dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: They styled him Master of the Dark Retreat.

sentences.zh: 楊軻，天水人也。

translations.literal: Yang Ke was a man of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 少好《易》，長而不娶，學業精微，養徒數百，常食粗飲水，衣褐縕袍，人不堪其憂，而軻悠然自得，疏賓異客，音旨未曾交也。

translations.literal: In youth he loved the Changes; grown, he did not marry; his learning was minute and subtle; he fed several hundred disciples, constantly eating coarse food and drinking plain water, wearing hemp and padded robes; others could not endure his hardship, yet Ke was leisurely self-content; with distant guests and strange visitors he never exchanged words.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the Book of Changes, never married, lived on gruel, and refused small talk with strangers.

sentences.zh: 雖受業門徒，非入室弟子，莫昨親言。

translations.literal: Although disciples received instruction, unless they were chamber disciples he did not personally speak.
translations.idiomatic: Only handpicked disciples heard his voice in person.

sentences.zh: 欲所論授，須旁無雜人，授入室弟子，令遞相宣授。

translations.literal: What he wished to lecture he required that beside him be no miscellaneous people; he instructed chamber disciples and ordered them to pass it in relay.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in secret, relayed through chosen disciples.

sentences.zh: 劉曜僭號，徵拜太常，軻固辭不起，曜亦敬而不逼，遂隱於隴山。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao usurped the title, he summoned and appointed grand master of ceremonies; Ke firmly declined and would not rise; Yao also respected him and did not force him; then he hid on Long Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao named him grand astrologer; he fled to Longshan.

sentences.zh: 曜後為石勒所擒，秦人東徙，軻留長安。

translations.literal: Later Yao was captured by Shi Le; Qin people moved east; Ke remained in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao fell to Shi Le, Ke stayed in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及石季龍嗣偽位。

translations.literal: When Shi Hu succeeded to the false throne,
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu took the throne—

sentences.zh: 備玄纁束帛安車徵之，軻以疾辭。
