translations.literal: with dark and crimson silks and peace carriage he summoned him; Ke declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent silks and carriage; Ke pleaded sick.

sentences.zh: 迫之，乃發。

translations.literal: Pressed, he then set out.
translations.idiomatic: Forced, he went.

sentences.zh: 既見季龍，不拜，與語，不言，命舍之於永昌乙第。

translations.literal: When he had seen Shi Hu, he did not bow; speaking with him, he did not speak; Hu ordered him lodged in the second house of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He faced Shi Hu silent and upright, and was lodged in Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 其有司以軻倨傲，請從大不敬論，季龍不從，下書任軻所尚。

translations.literal: His officials, because Ke was arrogant, asked to apply the great irreverence statute; Hu did not follow, issued a document letting Ke follow what he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers wanted him executed for lese-majesty; Shi Hu refused and let him be.

sentences.zh: 軻在永昌，季龍每有饋餼，輒口授弟子，使為表謝，其文甚美，覽者歎有深致。

translations.literal: Ke in Yongchang—whenever Hu had gifts of food, he orally instructed disciples to compose memorials of thanks; the texts were very fine; readers sighed that they had deep meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His thank-you letters through disciples were praised as profound.

sentences.zh: 季龍欲觀其真趣，乃密令美女夜以動之，軻蕭然不顧。

translations.literal: Hu wished to observe his true temper; therefore secretly ordered a beauty at night to move him; Ke was bleakly unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent a girl to tempt him; he never looked.

sentences.zh: 又使人將其弟子盡行，遣魁壯羯士衣甲持刀，臨之以兵，並竊其所賜衣服而去，軻視而不信，了無懼色。

translations.literal: Again he had people take away all his disciples, sent stalwart Jie soldiers in armor holding blades, threatened him with weapons, and together stole the clothes Hu had granted and departed; Ke looked but did not believe, utterly without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers stole his gifts and leveled swords; he showed no fear.

sentences.zh: 常臥土床，覆以布被，倮寢其中，下無茵褥。

translations.literal: He constantly lay on an earthen bed covered with a cloth quilt, slept naked inside, below without mat or cushion.
translations.idiomatic: He slept naked on bare earth under a rag quilt.

sentences.zh: 潁川荀鋪，好奇之士也，造而談經，軻瞑目不答。

translations.literal: Xun Pu of Yingchuan, a man who loved the strange, visited and discussed the classics; Ke closed his eyes and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The eccentric Xun Pu debated him; Ke feigned sleep.

sentences.zh: 鋪發軻被露其形，大笑之。

translations.literal: Pu lifted Ke's quilt and exposed his body, greatly laughing at him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun stripped his quilt and laughed.

sentences.zh: 軻神體頹然，無驚怒之狀。

translations.literal: Ke's spirit and body were slack, without startled anger.
translations.idiomatic: Ke never flinched.

sentences.zh: 于時咸以為焦先之徒，未有能量其深淺也。

translations.literal: At the time all considered him of the class of Jiao Xian; none could measure his depth.
translations.idiomatic: People compared him to Jiao Xian—none plumbed his depth.

sentences.zh: 後上疏陳鄉思，求還，季龍送以安車蒲輪，蠲十戶供之。

translations.literal: Later he submitted a memorial stating homesickness, begging to return; Hu sent him with peace carriage and rush-wrapped wheels and remitted ten households to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave westward; Shi Hu sent carriage and ten tax-free households.

sentences.zh: 自歸秦州，仍教授不絕。

translations.literal: Returning to Qinzhou, he still taught without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he kept teaching.

sentences.zh: 其後秦人西奔涼州，軻弟子以牛負之，為戍軍追擒，並為所害。

translations.literal: Afterward when Qin people fled west to Liangzhou, Ke's disciples used an ox to carry him; border guards pursued and captured them, and together they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing west, his ox-cart was overtaken by guards who killed master and pupils.

sentences.zh: 公孫鳳

translations.literal: Gongsun Feng
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Feng

sentences.zh: 公孫鳳，字子鸞，上穀人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Feng, styled Ziluan, was a man of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Feng, courtesy name Ziluan, came from Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 隱于昌黎之九城山谷，冬衣單布，寢處士床，夏則並食於器，停令臭敗，然後食之。

translations.literal: He hid in Jiucheng valley of Changli; in winter he wore single cloth, slept on a clay bed; in summer he put food together in a vessel, stopped it until it stank and rotted, then ate it.
translations.idiomatic: He wintered in one layer, summered on rotted gruel in a jar.

sentences.zh: 彈琴吟詠，陶然自得，人咸異之，莫能測也。

translations.literal: He plucked the zither and chanted, pottery pleased with himself; people all marveled and could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: He sang to his lute, self-content; none understood him.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐以安車徵至鄴，及見暐，不言不拜，衣食舉動如在九城。

translations.literal: Murong Wei with peace carriage summoned him to Ye; when he saw Wei, he did not speak or bow; eating, clothing, and motions were as in Jiucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei brought him to Ye; he still would not bow or speak.

sentences.zh: 賓客造請，鮮得與言。

translations.literal: Guests who visited and requested rarely got to speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors seldom won a word.

sentences.zh: 數年病卒。

translations.literal: After several years he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died after a few years.

sentences.zh: 公孫永

translations.literal: Gongsun Yong
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yong

sentences.zh: 公孫永，字子陽，襄平人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Yong, styled Ziyang, was a man of Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yong, courtesy name Ziyang, came from Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 少而好學恬虛，隱于平郭南山，不娶妻妾，非身所墾植，則不衣食之，吟詠岩間，欣然自得，年餘九十，操尚不虧。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and quiet emptiness; he hid on South Mountain of Pingguo, did not take wife or concubine; what he had not personally opened and planted he did not eat or wear; chanting among the cliffs, pleased with himself, past ninety years his conduct did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: He lived ninety years in the hills, eating only what he tilled.

sentences.zh: 與公孫鳳俱被容暐徵至鄴，及見暐，不拜，王公以下造之，皆不與言，雖經隆冬盛暑，端然自若。

translations.literal: Together with Gongsun Feng he was summoned by Murong Wei with tolerance to Ye; when he saw Wei, he did not bow; from princes and dukes downward who visited him, he spoke with none; though through deep winter and sweltering summer, he sat upright naturally.
translations.idiomatic: He and Feng reached court; he bowed to no prince, spoke to no lord, winter or summer.

sentences.zh: 一歲餘，詐狂，暐送之平郭。

translations.literal: After more than a year he feigned madness; Wei sent him back to Pingguo.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he played madman and Murong Wei sent him home.

sentences.zh: 後苻堅又將備禮徵之，難其年耆路遠，乃遣使者致問。

translations.literal: Later Fu Jian again wished with full ritual to summon him; troubled by his old age and the road's distance, he then sent an envoy to convey inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian meant to summon him but sent only greetings because of age and distance.

sentences.zh: 未至而永亡，堅深悼之，諡曰崇虛先生。

translations.literal: Before the envoy arrived Yong died; Jian deeply mourned him and gave the posthumous title Master Who Honors Emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Fu Jian's envoy came; Fu Jian mourned him as Master of Honored Void.

sentences.zh: 張忠，字巨和，中山人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhong, styled Juhe, was a man of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong, courtesy name Juhe, came from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，隱于泰山。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia disorders he hid on Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia fell he fled to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 恬靜寡欲，清虛服氣，餐芝餌石，修導養之法。

translations.literal: Quiet and still with few desires, clear and empty, he swallowed breath, ate mushroom and stone, practiced methods of guidance and nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on qi, herbs, and elixirs.

sentences.zh: 冬則縕袍，夏則帶索，端拱若屍。

translations.literal: In winter he wore padded robe; in summer girdle-rope; sitting upright like a corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Winter coat, summer rope—he sat like a corpse.

sentences.zh: 無琴書之適，不修經典，勸教但以至道虛無為宗。

translations.literal: He had no zither or books for pleasure, did not polish the classics; in instruction he took only utmost Way and emptiness as ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the wordless Way, not the canon.

sentences.zh: 其居依崇岩幽谷，鑿地為窟室。

translations.literal: His dwelling leaned on lofty crags and hidden valleys; he dug earth for a pit-chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He carved a cave in the cliff.

sentences.zh: 弟子亦以窟居，去忠六十餘步，五日一朝。

translations.literal: Disciples also dwelt in pits, sixty-some paces from Zhong, paying court once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Pupils lived in nearby caves and visited every five days.

sentences.zh: 其教以形不以言，弟子受業，觀形而退。

translations.literal: His teaching used form, not speech; disciples received the teaching, observed the form, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He taught by gesture, not lecture.

sentences.zh: 立道壇於窟上，每旦朝拜之。

translations.literal: He set a Way altar atop the pit; each dawn he bowed toward it.
translations.idiomatic: Each dawn he bowed to a stone altar.

sentences.zh: 食用瓦器，鑿石為釜。

translations.literal: For food he used pottery vessels and carved stone for a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: He ate from pottery, cooked in stone pots.

sentences.zh: 左右居人饋之衣食，一無所受。

translations.literal: Neighbors left him food and clothing; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors offered clothes; he refused.

sentences.zh: 好事少年頗或問以水旱之祥，忠曰：「天不言而四時行焉，萬物生焉，陰陽之事非窮山野叟所能知之。

translations.literal: Curious youths sometimes asked about omens of flood or drought; Zhong said, "Heaven does not speak yet the four seasons proceed; the myriad things are born; matters of yin and yang are not what a poor old man of the deep mountains can know.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about omens he said, 'Heaven needs no words to run the seasons—what would I know of yin and yang?'

sentences.zh: 」其遣諸外物，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " His pushing away the various outer things was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed the world off so in every case.

sentences.zh: 年在期頤，而視聽無爽。

translations.literal: His years reached the hundred-cycle yet sight and hearing were unimpaired.
translations.idiomatic: Past a hundred he saw and heard clearly.

sentences.zh: 苻堅遣使徵之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian sent an envoy to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian summoned him.

sentences.zh: 使者至，忠沐浴而起，謂弟子曰：「吾餘年無幾，不可以逆時主之意。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, Zhong bathed and rose, saying to disciples, "My remaining years are not many; I may not oppose the intent of the ruler of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed and told his pupils, 'I am old—I cannot defy an emperor's call.'

sentences.zh: 」浴訖就車。

translations.literal: " When the bath finished he boarded the cart.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted the carriage when dry.

sentences.zh: 及至長安，堅賜以冠衣，辭曰：「年朽發落，不堪衣冠，請以野服入覲。

translations.literal: Arriving at Chang'an, Jian granted him cap and robes; he declined, saying, "Years rotted, hair fallen—I cannot bear cap and robes; please let me enter audience in wild dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an he refused court dress: 'Let this wild man meet you in hemp.'

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " He followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 及見，堅謂之曰：「先生考磐山林，研精道素，獨善之美有餘，兼濟之功未也。

translations.literal: When they met, Jian said to him, "Sir, you have examined the rock in mountains and forests, ground fine the Way in plainness; the beauty of cultivating alone is more than enough, yet the work of aiding all is not yet done.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, 'You perfected the private Way—now help the world.'

sentences.zh: 故遠屈先生，將任齊尚父。

translations.literal: Therefore I have summoned you from afar, intending to appoint you like the Grand Duke of Qi to Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He offered him the role of Jiang Ziya to the king of Qi.

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「昔因喪亂，避地泰山，與鳥獸為侶，以全朝夕之命。

translations.literal: " Zhong said, "Formerly because of ruin and chaos I fled to Mount Tai, kept company with birds and beasts, to preserve life from dawn to dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong answered, 'I fled to Tai with the beasts to save my skin.'

sentences.zh: 屬堯舜之世，思一奉聖顏。

translations.literal: Now in a Yao-Shun age I wished once to behold the sage countenance.
translations.idiomatic: I longed to see a sage king once.

sentences.zh: 年衰志謝，不堪展效，尚父之況，非敢竊擬。

translations.literal: Years decline and intent fades; I cannot bear to display service; the comparison to the Grand Duke is not what I dare steal.
translations.idiomatic: I am too old for office—do not call me Jiang Ziya.'

sentences.zh: 山棲之性，情存岩岫，乞還餘齒，歸死岱宗。

translations.literal: The nature of mountain roosting—my feeling lodges in crags and peaks; I beg to return my remaining years to die on Dai's lord.
translations.idiomatic: Let me end my days on sacred Tai.'

sentences.zh: 堅以安車送之。

translations.literal: Jian sent him back with peace carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent him home in the honor coach.

sentences.zh: 行達華山。

translations.literal: He traveled and reached Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Mount Hua westward.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「我東嶽道士，沒于西嶽，命也，奈何！

translations.literal: He sighed, saying, "I am an eastern marchmount Daoist who will perish on the western marchmount—fate—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: He cried, 'An eastern hermit dies on the western peak—fate.'

sentences.zh: 行五十里，及關而死。

translations.literal: He went fifty li and died at the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li on he died at the barrier.

sentences.zh: 使者馳驛白之，堅遣黃門郎韋華持節策吊，祀乙太牢，褒賜命服，諡曰安道先生。

translations.literal: The envoy raced post-horses to report; Jian sent palace attendant Wei Hua with staff of authority to convey condolences, sacrificed with grand tai lao, praised and granted mandated robes, posthumous title Master Who Pacifies the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent rites, grand sacrifice, posthumous name Master of the Peaceful Way.

sentences.zh: 石垣，字洪孫，自雲北海劇人。

translations.literal: Shi Yuan, styled Hongsun, called himself a man of Ju in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yuan claimed origin from Ju in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 居無定所，不娶妻妾，不營產業，食不求美，衣必粗弊。

translations.literal: He dwelt without fixed place, did not take wife or concubine, did not manage property, did not seek fine food in eating, in clothing insisted on coarse and tattered.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered, no wife, no land, coarse food, ragged coat.

sentences.zh: 或有遺其衣服，受而施人。

translations.literal: If someone left him clothing, he accepted and gave it away to others.
translations.idiomatic: He passed on any gift of clothes.

sentences.zh: 人有喪葬，輒杖策吊之。

translations.literal: When people had burials, he then staff in hand went to condole.
translations.idiomatic: He walked any distance to mourn the dead.

sentences.zh: 路無遠近，時有寒暑，必在其中；

translations.literal: Whether the road was far or near, sometimes in cold or heat, he was always among them;
translations.idiomatic: Heat or cold, near or far, he always arrived—

sentences.zh: 或同日共時，咸皆見焉。

translations.literal: or on the same day at the same time, all saw him.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes the same mourners saw him twice at once.

sentences.zh: 又能暗中取物，如晝無差。

translations.literal: Moreover he could take objects in the dark as in daylight without error.
translations.idiomatic: He could pick objects in pitch dark as if at noon.

sentences.zh: 姚萇之亂，莫知所終。

translations.literal: In Yao Chang's disorders none knew where he ended.
translations.idiomatic: He vanished in Yao Chang's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 宋纖，字令艾，敦煌效穀人也。

translations.literal: Song Xian, styled Ling'ai, was a man of Xiaogu in Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xian, courtesy name Ling'ai, from Xiaogu in Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 少有遠操，沈靖不與世交，隱居于酒泉南山。

translations.literal: In youth he had far-reaching conduct, sunk in stillness, not associating with the world; he hid on South Mountain of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He hid on Jiuquan South Mountain.

sentences.zh: 明究經緯，弟子受業三千餘人。

translations.literal: He clearly investigated classics and weft texts; disciples who received instruction were more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He taught three thousand students astronomy and classics.

sentences.zh: 不應州郡辟命，惟與陰顒、齊好友善。

translations.literal: He answered no commandery summons; only with Yin Yong and Qi Liang was he friendly.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke only to Yin Yong and Qi Liang.

sentences.zh: 張祚時，太守楊宣畫其象於閣上；

translations.literal: Under Zhang Zuo, Prefect Yang Xuan painted his likeness in the pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yang Xuan hung his portrait in the gallery—

sentences.zh: 出入視之，作頌曰：「為枕何石？

translations.literal: going out and in he looked at it and composed a praise, saying, "For pillow what stone?
translations.idiomatic: and wrote, 'What stone for pillow?

sentences.zh: 為瀨何流？

translations.literal: For rapid what stream?
translations.idiomatic: What rapid for ford?

sentences.zh: 身不可見，名不可求。

translations.literal: The body cannot be seen; the name cannot be sought.
translations.idiomatic: The man stays hidden—only the name rings.'

sentences.zh: 」酒泉太守馬岌，高尚之士也，具威儀，鳴鐃鼓，造焉。

translations.literal: " Jiuquan Prefect Ma Ji, a man of lofty conduct, fully set out guards, beat gongs and drums, and visited him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Ma Ji marched with full pomp to call.

sentences.zh: 纖高樓重閣，距而不見。

translations.literal: Xian in a high tower and double gallery kept distance and would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xian barred his high gate.

sentences.zh: 岌歎曰：「名可聞而身不可見，德可仰而形不可睹，吾而今而後知先生人中之龍也。

translations.literal: Ji sighed, saying, "The name can be heard yet the body cannot be seen; virtue can be looked up to yet form cannot be viewed—I from today onward know the master is a dragon among men.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ji sighed, 'Hearing his name yet never his face—he is a dragon among men.'

sentences.zh: 」銘詩於石壁曰：「丹崖百丈，青壁萬尋。

translations.literal: " He inscribed a poem on the stone cliff, saying, "Cinnabar cliff a hundred yards, green cliff ten thousand fathoms.
translations.idiomatic: He carved on the cliff: red walls, green peaks—

sentences.zh: 奇木蓊鬱，蔚若鄧林。

translations.literal: Strange trees luxuriant, lush as Deng's grove.
translations.idiomatic: trees thick as the magic grove—

sentences.zh: 其人如玉，維國之琛。

translations.literal: That man is like jade, the state's precious gem.
translations.idiomatic: that man is jade, the state's jewel—

sentences.zh: 室邇人遐，實勞我心。」

translations.literal: The chamber is near, the man far—truly it wearies my heart."
translations.idiomatic: his hut is near yet he is far—my heart aches.'

sentences.zh: 纖注《論語》，及為詩頌數萬言。

translations.literal: Xian annotated the Analects and moreover composed poems and praises numbering ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten thousand words of poetry and Analects notes.

sentences.zh: 年八十，篤學不倦。

translations.literal: At eighty he loved learning and did not tire.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty he still studied.

sentences.zh: 張祚後遣使者張興備禮徵為太子友，興逼喻甚切，纖喟然歎曰：「德非莊生，才非幹木，何取稽停明命！

translations.literal: After Zhang Zuo later sent envoy Zhang Xing with full ritual to summon him as friend to the heir apparent, Xing pressed the instruction very urgently; Xian sighed and said, "Virtue I am not Zhuangzi; talent I am not Duanmu Gan—why take delay in stopping the bright command!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo summoned him as crown prince's friend; he sighed, 'I am no Zhuangzi—why defy a clear edict?'

sentences.zh: 」遂隨興至姑臧。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he followed Xing to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Guzang.

sentences.zh: 祚遣其太子太和以執友禮造之，纖稱疾不見，贈遺一皆不受。

translations.literal: Zuo sent his heir apparent Taihe to visit him with the rite of equal friend; Xian claimed illness and would not see him, and accepted none of the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince called; he feigned illness and took no gifts.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子太傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to grand tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上疏曰：「臣受生方外，心慕太古。

translations.literal: Before long he submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject received life outside the square, heart admiring high antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, 'I was born for the hills, my heart in high antiquity.'

sentences.zh: 生不喜存，死不悲沒。

translations.literal: In life I do not rejoice in surviving; in death I do not grieve perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Life does not delight me; death will not grieve me.'

sentences.zh: 素有遺屬，屬諸知識，在山投山，臨水投水，處澤露形，在人親土。

translations.literal: Plainly I have left instructions to my friends: in mountains cast me in mountains, by water cast in water, in marshes expose the form, among men kin the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Bury me in mountain stone or river—no word home.'

sentences.zh: 聲聞書疏，勿告我家。

translations.literal: If sound or letter comes, do not tell my household.
translations.idiomatic: Let no letter reach my kin.'

sentences.zh: 今當命終，乞如素願。

translations.literal: Now as I am about to end life, I beg according to my plain wish.
translations.idiomatic: Now I ask only that wish.'

sentences.zh: 」遂不食而卒，時年八十二，諡曰玄虛先生。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he refused food and died at age eighty-two; posthumous title Master of Mysterious Emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: He fasted to death at eighty-two, styled Master of Dark Void.

sentences.zh: 郭荷，字承休，略陽人也。

translations.literal: Guo He, styled Chengxiu, was a man of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo He, courtesy name Chengxiu, from Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 六世祖整，漢安順之世，公府八辟，公車五徵，皆不就。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zheng, in the Shun'an era of Han, the ducal offices summoned him eight times, the state carriage five times—he took none.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Guo Zheng refused eight ducal calls and five carriages under the Han.

sentences.zh: 自整及荷，世以經學致位。

translations.literal: From Zheng down to He, generation after generation rose by classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: The clan rose on the classics for generations.

sentences.zh: 荷明究群籍，特善史書。

translations.literal: He clearly investigated all writings, especially skilled in histories.
translations.idiomatic: Guo He mastered every corpus, best in histories.

sentences.zh: 不應州郡之命。

translations.literal: He answered no commandery orders.
translations.idiomatic: He refused local office.

sentences.zh: 張祚遣使者以安車束帛徵為博士祭酒，使者迫而致之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuo sent envoys with peace carriage and bundled silks to summon him as libationer erudite; the envoy forced him and brought him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo's envoy dragged him to the libationer post.

sentences.zh: 及至，署太子友。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was appointed friend to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At court they named him the crown prince's companion.

sentences.zh: 荷上疏乞還，祚許之，遣以安車蒲輪送還張掖東山。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial begging to return; Zuo permitted it, sending him with peace carriage and rush-wrapped wheels back to East Mountain in Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for release and rode home to eastern Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 年八十四卒，諡曰玄德先生。

translations.literal: At eighty-four he died; posthumous title Master of Mysterious Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-four as Master of Dark Power.

sentences.zh: 郭瑀，字元瑜，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yu, styled Yuanyu, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu, courtesy name Yuanyu, from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 少有超俗之操，東遊張掖，師事郭荷，盡傳其業。

translations.literal: In youth he had conduct surpassing the vulgar; he east wandered to Zhangye and studied under Guo He, fully receiving his enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Guo He in Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 精通經義，雅辯談論，多才藝，善屬文。

translations.literal: He penetrated the classics' meaning, was refined in debate, had many talents, skilled at composing texts.
translations.idiomatic: He debated well and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 荷卒，瑀以為父生之，師成之，君爵之，而五服之制，師不服重，蓋聖人謙也，遂服斬衰，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When He died, Yu considered that the father begat him, the teacher completed him, the lord ennobled him, yet in the five garments' system the teacher does not wear heavy mourning—because the sages were modest—thereupon he wore hemmed sackcloth and hut by the tomb three years.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his teacher Guo He with three years' sackcloth by the grave.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，隱於臨松薤穀，鑿石窟而居，服柏實以輕身，作《春秋墨說》、《孝經錯緯》，弟子著錄千餘人。

translations.literal: When rites were finished, he hid at Xie Valley of Linsong, chiseled a stone grotto and dwelt, ate cypress fruit to lighten the body, composed "Spring and Autumn Ink Discourse" and "Analects Mismatched Wefts"; disciples recorded numbered over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He carved a cave in Linsong, ate pine nuts, wrote commentaries, taught a thousand pupils.

sentences.zh: 張天賜遣使者孟公明持節，以浦輪玄纁備禮徵之，遺瑀書曰：「先生潛光九皋，懷真獨遠，心與至境冥符，志與四時消息，豈知蒼生倒懸，四海待拯者乎！

translations.literal: Zhang Tianci sent envoy Meng Gongming with staff, with rush wheels and dark silks in full ritual to summon him, leaving Yu a letter saying, "Sir, you hide your gleam in the nine marshes, embrace the true alone far off; heart silently matches the utmost realm, intent with the four seasons waxes and wanes—do you not know the black-haired people hang upside down, the four seas await rescue!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianci wrote begging him to save the northwest.

sentences.zh: 孤忝承時運，負荷大業，思與賢明同贊帝道。

translations.literal: I shamefully inherit the season's fortune, bear the great enterprise, wish with the wise and clear jointly assist the imperial Way.
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked him to join the government.

sentences.zh: 昔傳說龍翔殷朝，尚父鷹揚周室，孔聖車不停軌，墨子駕不俟旦，皆以黔首之禍不可以不救，君不獨立，道由人弘故也。

translations.literal: In old days Fu Yue soared in Yin court, the Grand Duke hawk-displayed in Zhou house, Confucius' cart did not stop its tracks, Mozi's carriage did not wait for dawn—all because the black-haired people's calamity could not go unaided, the lord does not stand alone, the Way is enlarged by men.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Fu Yue, Jiang Ziya, Confucius, Mozi.

sentences.zh: 況今九服分為狄場，二都盡為戎穴，天子僻陋江東，名教淪于左衽，創毒之甚，開避未聞。

translations.literal: Moreover now the nine domains are split into Di arenas; both capitals are wholly barbarian dens; the Son of Heaven is cramped in humble Jiang east; name-teaching sinks under left-lapel; the wound of creation—such opening and fleeing has not been heard.
translations.idiomatic: He said Jin was cornered east while the north fell to barbarians.

sentences.zh: 先生懷濟世之才，坐觀而不救，其于仁智，孤竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Sir, you embrace talent to aid the age, yet sit and watch without saving—in regard to benevolence and wisdom, I alone am puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: He asked how a sage could watch and not save.

sentences.zh: 故遣使者虛左授綏，鶴企先生，乃眷下國。

translations.literal: Therefore I send an envoy, emptying the left seat and handing the tether, crane-standing for the sir, turning fondly to the lower state.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a carriage with empty seat of honor.'

sentences.zh: 」公明至山，瑀指翔鴻以示之曰：「此鳥也，安可籠哉！

translations.literal: " When Gongming reached the mountain, Yu pointed to soaring wild geese and showed him, saying, "This is a bird—how can it be caged!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yu pointed at wild geese: 'You cannot cage that bird.'

sentences.zh: 」遂深逃絕跡。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he fled deep and cut off traces.
translations.idiomatic: He fled deeper into the hills.

sentences.zh: 公明拘其門人，瑀歎曰：「吾逃祿，非避罪也，豈得隱居行義，害及門人！

translations.literal: Gongming seized his disciples; Yu sighed, saying, "I fled stipend, not crime—how can I keep hidden conduct and righteousness yet harm disciples!
translations.idiomatic: When pupils were seized he said, 'I flee salary, not justice—I cannot let pupils suffer.'

sentences.zh: 」乃出而就徵。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he came out and answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court.

sentences.zh: 及至姑臧，值天賜母卒，瑀括發入吊，三踴而出，還于南山。

translations.literal: Arriving at Guzang, it happened Tianci's mother died; Yu tied hair and entered to condole, leapt the three leaps and came out, returned to South Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned Tianci's mother with curt rites then fled back south.

sentences.zh: 及天錫滅，苻堅又以安車徵瑀定禮儀，會父喪而止，太守辛章遣書生三百人就受業焉。

translations.literal: When Tianci fell, Fu Jian again with peace carriage summoned Yu to fix ritual; it happened his father died and stopped; Prefect Xin Zhang sent three hundred students to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian later summoned him for rites; father's death stopped him; three hundred students came to his cliff.

sentences.zh: 及苻氏之末，略陽王穆起兵酒泉，以應張大豫，遣使招瑀。

translations.literal: At the end of the Fu clan, Lueyang Wang Mu raised troops in Jiuquan to answer Zhang Dayu and sent an envoy to summon Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu rebelled in Jiuquan and called on Guo Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑀歎曰：「臨河救溺，不卜命之短長；

translations.literal: Yu sighed, saying, "To save the drowning by the river, one does not divine whether life is short or long;
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'To save a drowning man you do not cast lots—

sentences.zh: 脈病三年，不豫絕其餐饋；

translations.literal: to nurse sickness three years, one does not beforehand cut off meals;
translations.idiomatic: to nurse a patient three years you do not withhold food—

sentences.zh: 魯連在趙，義不結舌，況人將左衽而不救之！

translations.literal: Lu Zhong in Zhao, in righteousness did not seal his mouth—how much more when men will wear left lapel and not save them!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhong never held his tongue—how can I stay silent while men go barbarian?'

sentences.zh: 」乃與敦煌索嘏起兵五千，運粟三萬石，東應王穆。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with Su Gu of Dunhuang he raised troops five thousand, transported grain thirty thousand shi, east to answer Wang Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He raised five thousand men and thirty thousand shi for Wang Mu.

sentences.zh: 穆以瑀為太府左長史、軍師將軍。

translations.literal: Mu made Yu grand clerk of the treasury on the left and army director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu made him chief clerk and strategist.

sentences.zh: 雖居元佐，而口詠黃老，冀功成世定，追伯成之蹤。

translations.literal: Although he occupied chief aide, his mouth chanted Huang-Lao, hoping when merit was done and the age settled to follow the tracks of Bo Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Though a minister he chanted Daoism, dreaming of returning like Bo Cheng.

sentences.zh: 穆惑於讒間，西伐索嘏，瑀諫曰：「昔漢定天下，然後誅功臣。

translations.literal: Mu was deluded by slander between factions, west attacked Su Gu; Yu remonstrated, saying, "In old days when Han settled the realm, afterward they executed the merit ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He warned Wang Mu not to kill allies like Han did.

sentences.zh: 今事業未建而誅之，立見麋鹿游於此庭矣。

translations.literal: Now the enterprise is not yet established yet you execute them—standing soon you will see deer roam this court.
translations.idiomatic: Strike now and deer will graze your courtyard.'

sentences.zh: 」穆不從。

translations.literal: Mu would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu ignored him.

sentences.zh: 瑀出城大哭，舉手謝城曰：「吾不復見汝矣！

translations.literal: Yu went out of the city and greatly wept, raised his hands and thanked the city, saying, "I shall not see you again!
translations.idiomatic: He wept at the gate, 'I will not see this city again.'

sentences.zh: 」還而引被覆面，不與人言，不食七日，與疾而歸，旦夕祈死。

translations.literal: " Returning he pulled the quilt over his face, spoke with no one, did not eat seven days, feigned illness and returned, morning and evening prayed for death.
translations.idiomatic: He hid under his quilt, fasted seven days, begged for death.

sentences.zh: 夜夢乘青龍上天，至屋而止，寤而歎曰：「龍飛在天，今止於屋。

translations.literal: At night he dreamed riding a green dragon up to heaven, stopping at the roof; waking he sighed, saying, "The dragon flies in heaven; now it stops at the roof.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed a dragon stopped on a roof—

sentences.zh: 屋之為字，屍下至也。

translations.literal: The character for roof is corpse above;
translations.idiomatic: 'Roof' writes as corpse over a beam—

sentences.zh: 龍飛至屍，吾其死也。

translations.literal: the dragon flies to corpse—I am about to die.
translations.idiomatic: a dragon to a corpse means I die.'

sentences.zh: 古之君子不卒內寢，況吾正士乎！

translations.literal: The gentlemen of old did not end inside the inner chamber—how much more I, an upright man!
translations.idiomatic: Sages die not in women's quarters—nor shall I.'

sentences.zh: 」遂還酒泉南山赤崖閣，飲氣而卒。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he returned to Red Cliff Pavilion on South Mountain of Jiuquan and expired by breath-control.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Chiya pavilion and died meditating.

sentences.zh: 祈嘉，字孔賓，酒泉人也。

translations.literal: Qi Jia, styled Kongbin, was a man of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jia, courtesy name Kongbin, from Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 少清貧，好學。

translations.literal: In youth he was clear and poor, loving learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was poor and book-loving.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，夜忽窗中有聲呼曰：「祈孔賓，祈孔賓！

translations.literal: Past twenty, at night suddenly in the window a voice called, "Qi Kongbin, Qi Kongbin!
translations.idiomatic: At night a voice cried his name—

sentences.zh: 隱去來，隱去來！

translations.literal: Hide away, come hide away!
translations.idiomatic: 'Flee and hide, flee and hide!'

sentences.zh: 修飾人世，甚苦不可諧。

translations.literal: To polish and trim the human world is very bitter and cannot be harmonized;
translations.idiomatic: The world bruises those who dress it—

sentences.zh: 所得未毛銖，所喪如山崖。

translations.literal: what you gain is not yet a hair's tip; what you lose is like a mountain cliff.
translations.idiomatic: gain is a hair's weight, loss a cliff of stone.'

sentences.zh: 」旦而逃去，西至敦煌，依學官誦書，貧無衣食，為書生都養以自給，遂博通經傳，精究大義。

translations.literal: " At dawn he fled away, west to Dunhuang, relied on the school officer to recite books; poor without clothes or food, he became steward for the students to supply himself; thereby he broadly penetrated the classics and traditions, finely investigated great meanings.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Dunhuang, worked as a school cook, and became a scholar.

sentences.zh: 西游海渚，教授門生百餘人。

translations.literal: He west wandered to sea islets and taught more than a hundred disciples.
translations.idiomatic: He taught a hundred pupils on the western shore.

sentences.zh: 張重華徵為儒林祭酒。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua summoned him as libationer of the forest of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua named him erudite libationer.

sentences.zh: 性和裕，教授不倦，依《孝經》作《二九神經》。

translations.literal: By nature harmonious and ample, he taught tirelessly, relying on the Classic of Filial Piety to compose the "Two-Nine Spirit Classic".
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Two-Nine Spirit Classic from the Filial Piety, teaching without weariness.

sentences.zh: 在朝卿士、郡縣守令彭和正等受業獨拜床下者二千餘人，天錫謂為先生而不名之。

translations.literal: At court ministers, commandery and county magistrates such as Peng Hezheng and others who received instruction, alone bowing at the couch-side, numbered more than two thousand; Tianci called him Master and did not use his name.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand officials bowed to Qi Jia as 'Master' without daring his name.

sentences.zh: 竟以壽終。

translations.literal: In the end he ended life at a full old age.
translations.idiomatic: He died full of years.

sentences.zh: 瞿硎先生

translations.literal: Master of the Quxing Cliff
translations.idiomatic: Master of the Quxing Cliff

sentences.zh: 瞿硎先生者，不得姓名，亦不知何許人也。

translations.literal: The Master of the Quxing cliff—his name could not be obtained, nor was it known what place he was from.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse of Quxing cliff—name and home unknown.

sentences.zh: 太和末，常居宣城郡界文脊山中，山有瞿硎，因以為名焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Taihe he constantly dwelt within the bounds of Xuancheng commandery on Mount Wenji; the mountain had a Quxing cliff, and by this he took his name.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on Mount Wenji in Xuancheng near the Quxing grotto.

sentences.zh: 大司馬桓溫嘗往造之。

translations.literal: Grand marshal Huan Wen once went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen climbed to his cave.

sentences.zh: 既至，見先生被鹿裘，坐於石室，神無忤色，溫及僚佐數十人皆莫測之，乃命伏滔為之銘贊。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he saw the master draped in deerskin, sitting in a stone chamber, spirit without offending color; Wen and several tens of aides and staff all could not fathom him; then he ordered Fu Tao to compose an inscription and praise for him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan found him in deerskin in a stone room, baffled his retinue, and had Fu Tao write his praise.

sentences.zh: 竟卒於山中。

translations.literal: In the end he died in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the hills.

sentences.zh: 謝敷，字慶緒，會稽人也。

translations.literal: Xie Fu, styled Qingxu, was a man of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fu, courtesy name Qingxu, from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 性澄靖寡欲，入太平山十餘年。

translations.literal: By nature clear, still, with few desires, he entered Mount Taiping more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He hid on Mount Taiping ten years.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍郗愔召為主簿，台徵博士，皆不就。

translations.literal: General Who Stabilizes the Army Xi Yin summoned him as chief clerk; the ministry summoned him as erudite—he took neither.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin and the ministry summoned him; he refused.

sentences.zh: 初，月犯少微，少微一名處士星，占者以陷士當之。

translations.literal: At first, the moon trespassed on Shaowei; Shaowei has another name, the star of retired scholars; astrologers thought it meant a scholar would fall.
translations.idiomatic: A moon omen touched the hermit star—seers said a recluse would die.

sentences.zh: 譙國戴逵有美才，人或憂之。

translations.literal: Dai Kui of Qiao had fine talent; some worried for him.
translations.idiomatic: People feared for Dai Kui.

sentences.zh: 俄而敷死，故會稽人士以嘲吳人云：「吳中高士，便是求死不得死。」

translations.literal: Soon Fu died; therefore men of Kuaiji to mock men of Wu said, "Among Wu's lofty gentlemen, they are the sort who seek death yet cannot die."
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Fu died, Kuaiji wits mocked Wu: 'Their hermits cannot even manage to die.'

sentences.zh: 戴逵，字安道，譙國人也。

translations.literal: Dai Kui, styled Andao, was a man of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Kui, courtesy name Andao, from Qiao.

sentences.zh: 少博學，好談論，善屬文，能鼓琴，工書畫，其餘巧藝靡不畢綜。

translations.literal: In youth he was broadly learned, loved discussion, skilled at composing texts, could strum the zither, was skilled at calligraphy and painting; of the other clever arts none he did not combine.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered debate, letters, lute, painting, and every art.

sentences.zh: 總角時，以雞卵汁溲白瓦屑作《鄭玄碑》，又為文而自鐫之，詞麗器妙，時人莫不驚歎。

translations.literal: In boyhood he kneaded egg white with white tile crumbs to make a Zheng Xuan stele, also composed the text and personally engraved it; the words lovely, the vessel subtle—people of the time none did not marvel.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he carved a Zheng Xuan stele in mortar—crowds marveled.

sentences.zh: 性不樂當世，常以琴書自娛。

translations.literal: By nature he did not delight in serving the age; constantly he took zither and books to amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: He lived for lute and books, not office.

sentences.zh: 師事術士范宣于豫章，宣異之，以兄女妻焉。

translations.literal: He studied under the technician Fan Xuan in Yuyang; Xuan marveled at him and gave him his elder brother's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: His teacher Fan Xuan gave him a niece in marriage.

sentences.zh: 太宰、武陵王晞聞其善鼓琴，使人召之，逵對使者破琴曰：「戴安道不為王門伶人！

translations.literal: The grand steward and prince of Wuling, Xi, hearing he was skilled at the zither, sent men to summon him; Kui to the envoy broke the zither, saying, "Dai Andao will not be a house entertainer to princes!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi summoned him to play; Kui smashed his lute: 'I will not be a prince's jester.'

sentences.zh: 」晞怒，乃更引其兄述。

translations.literal: " Xi was angry, then instead summoned his elder brother Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi called his brother Dai Shu instead.

sentences.zh: 述聞命欣然，擁琴而往。

translations.literal: Shu hearing the order was pleased, hugging his zither and going.
translations.idiomatic: Shu happily took his lute to the palace.

sentences.zh: 逵後徙居會稽之剡縣。

translations.literal: Kui afterward moved to dwell in Shan county of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kui moved to Shan in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 性高潔，常以禮度自處，深以放達為非道，乃著論曰：

translations.literal: By nature lofty and clean, he constantly used ritual measure to order himself; deeply he took unrestrained license as not the Way; therefore he composed a treatise, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He condemned 'free and easy' excess and wrote:

sentences.zh: 夫親沒而采藥不反者，不仁之子也；

translations.literal: For parents to die yet one gathers herbs and does not return—such is an unfilial son;
translations.idiomatic: To roam while parents need you is unfilial;

sentences.zh: 君危而屢出近關者，苟免之臣也。

translations.literal: for the lord to be in peril yet one repeatedly goes out near the passes—such is a minister who seeks bare escape.
translations.idiomatic: to bolt the border while the throne totters is cowardice.

sentences.zh: 而古之人未始以彼害名教之體者何？

translations.literal: Yet the men of old never began to let those things harm the substance of name-teaching—why?
translations.idiomatic: The ancients never let conduct wreck the teaching—why?

sentences.zh: 達其旨故也。

translations.literal: Because they grasped the meaning, therefore they did.
translations.idiomatic: They grasped the meaning.

sentences.zh: 達其旨，故不惑其跡。

translations.literal: Because they grasped the meaning, therefore they were not deluded by traces.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the root, they ignored the pose.

sentences.zh: 若元康之人，可謂好遁跡而不求其本，故有捐本徇末之弊，舍實逐聲之行，是猶美西施而學其顰眉，慕有道而折其巾角，所以為慕者，非其所以為美，徒貴貌似而已矣。

translations.literal: As for the men of Yuankang, one may say they loved hiding traces but did not seek the root; therefore there was the fault of casting away the root and pursuing the twigs, conduct of abandoning substance and chasing rumor—it is like admiring Xishi and studying her knitted brow, admiring the Way yet folding the kerchief corners; what they admired was not what made beauty beautiful; they valued only seeming resemblance.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked Yuankang poseurs who mimicked reclusion without virtue.

sentences.zh: 夫紫之亂硃，以其似硃也。

translations.literal: Purple confuses vermilion because it resembles vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: Purple passes for crimson because it looks like crimson.

sentences.zh: 故鄉原似中和，所以亂德；

translations.literal: Therefore the village worthy resembles the mean—thereby he confuses virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Village worthies mimic the mean and rot virtue;

sentences.zh: 放者似達，所以亂道。

translations.literal: the unrestrained resemble free passage—thereby they confuse the Way.
translations.idiomatic: libertines mimic freedom and ruin the Way.

sentences.zh: 然竹林之為放，有疾而為顰者也，元康之為放，無德而折巾者也，可無察乎！

translations.literal: Yet the Bamboo Grove's unrestraint was having illness and thereby knitting the brow; Yuankang's unrestraint was lacking virtue yet folding the kerchief—can one fail to examine!
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo Grove had excuse; Yuankang only aped the scarf.

sentences.zh: 且儒家尚譽者，本以興賢也，既失其本，則有色取之行。

translations.literal: Moreover Confucians who esteem fame originally meant to raise the worthy; once they lose the root, then there is conduct of seizing color.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians chase fame and lose the substance.

sentences.zh: 懷情喪真，以容貌相欺，其弊必至於末偽。

translations.literal: Harbor feeling and lose the genuine, cheat one another with looks—the fault must reach utmost falsity.
translations.idiomatic: They trade masks until all truth dies.

sentences.zh: 道家去名者，欲以篤實也，苟失其本，又有越檢之行。

translations.literal: Daoists who cast away names wished to make solid truth; if they lose the root, again there is conduct that leaps the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Daoists flee names yet leap bounds.

sentences.zh: 情禮俱虧，則仰詠兼忘，其弊必至於本薄。

translations.literal: When feeling and ritual both fail, then they look up chanting both forgotten—the fault must reach root thinness.
translations.idiomatic: Both schools thin to hypocrisy.

sentences.zh: 夫偽薄者，非二本之失，而為弊者必托二本以自通。

translations.literal: The falsely thin are not the two roots' failure, but those who make the fault must borrow the two roots to excuse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hypocrites hide behind Confucius and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 夫道有常經而弊無常情，是以六經有失，王政有弊，苟乖其本，固聖賢所無奈何也。

translations.literal: The Way has constant classics but faults have no constant temper; therefore the six classics have failures, royal government has faults; if one strays from the root, indeed even sages and worthies cannot help it.
translations.idiomatic: When the root rots, neither sage can save it.

sentences.zh: 嗟夫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 行道之人自非性足體備、暗蹈而當者，亦曷能不棲情古烈，擬規前修。

translations.literal: Men who walk the Way, unless nature is complete in the body and they darkly tread what fits, how can they not lodge feeling in ancient ardor and model former cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you are born whole, model the ancients with care.

sentences.zh: 苟迷擬之然後動，議之然後言，固當先辯其趣舍之極，求其用心之本，識其枉尺直尋之旨，采其被褐懷玉之由。

translations.literal: If only after delusion in modeling one moves, after deliberation one speaks, one must first distinguish the utmost of choosing and rejecting, seek the root of the mind's use, know the meaning of bending a foot to gain a fathom, gather the reason for wearing coarse cloth while cherishing jade.
translations.idiomatic: Judge ends and means before you act.

sentences.zh: 若斯，途雖殊，而其歸可觀也；

translations.literal: If so, though roads differ, their convergence can be observed;
translations.idiomatic: Paths differ yet aim one way;

sentences.zh: 跡雖亂，而其契不乖也。

translations.literal: though traces are tangled, their tally is not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: tracks tangle yet the tally holds.

sentences.zh: 不然，則流遁忘反，為風波之行，自驅以物，自誑以偽，外眩囂華，內喪道實，以矜尚奪其真主，以塵垢翳其天正，貽笑千載，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: If not, then drifting one forgets the return, making conduct of wind and wave, driving oneself with things, deceiving oneself with sham, outwardly dazzled by clamorous splendor, inwardly losing the Way's substance, letting boastfulness rob the true lord, letting dust and filth dim heaven's uprightness—laughter for a thousand ages—can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Else you chase fashion, lose the core, and earn a thousand years' mockery.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝時，以散騎常侍、國子博士累徵，辭父疾不就。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was repeatedly summoned as attendant censor regular and national university erudite; he pleaded father's illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu called him to court; he pleaded his father's health.

sentences.zh: 郡縣敦逼不已，乃逃于吳。

translations.literal: Commandery and county pressed urgently; then he fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Officials hounded him until he fled to Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳國內史王珣有別館在武丘山，逵潛詣之，與珣遊處積旬。

translations.literal: Interior secretary of Wu Wang Xun had a separate lodge on Mount Wuqiu; Kui secretly went to him and with Xun roamed and dwelt accumulating ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He hid with Wang Xun on Mount Wuqiu for weeks.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史謝玄慮逵遠遁不反，乃上疏曰：「伏見譙國戴逵希心俗表，不嬰世務，棲遲衡門，與琴書為友。

translations.literal: Interior secretary of Kuaiji Xie Xuan, worrying Kui would flee far and not return, therefore submitted a memorial, saying, "I humbly see Dai Kui of Qiao set his heart outside the vulgar, not entangle in worldly affairs, linger at a brushwood gate, befriend zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan memorialized that Dai should be left alone to save his health.

sentences.zh: 雖策命屢加，幽操不回，超然絕跡，自求其志。

translations.literal: Although summons with tally came many times, his hidden resolve did not turn; transcendentally he cut traces and sought his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Summons never moved his resolve.

sentences.zh: 且年垂耳順，常抱羸疾，時或失適，轉至委篤。

translations.literal: Moreover years hung near ear-harmony; he constantly embraced a wasting illness; sometimes unwell, it turned to utter exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: He was past sixty and frail.

sentences.zh: 今王命未回，將離風霜之患。

translations.literal: Now the king's command has not returned; he will leave wind and frost's affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Another summons might kill him.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已愛而器之，亦宜使其身名並存，請絕其召命。

translations.literal: Your majesty already loves and treasures him—you ought also to let body and name together survive; I beg cut off his summons.
translations.idiomatic: Xie asked the throne to leave him in peace.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，帝許之，逵復還剡。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was presented, the emperor permitted it; Kui again returned to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; Dai Kui went home to Shan.

sentences.zh: 後王珣為尚書僕射，上疏復請徵為國子祭酒，加散騎常侍，徵之，復不至。

translations.literal: Later when Wang Xun became vice-director of the secretariat, he submitted a memorial again requesting summon as national university libationer, adding attendant censor regular; they summoned him; again he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun tried again; Dai stayed away.

sentences.zh: 太元二十年，皇太子始出東宮，太子太傳會稽王道子、少傅王雅、詹事王珣又上疏曰：「逵執操貞厲，含味獨遊，年在耆老，清風彌劭。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taiyuan, when the crown prince first left the eastern palace, grand tutor to the crown prince Dao Wang Daozi, junior tutor Wang Ya, and chamberlain Wang Xun again submitted a memorial, saying, "Kui holds conduct chaste and stern, tastes meaning alone and roams; years in hoary age, pure wind ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace begged Dai as tutor.

sentences.zh: 東宮虛德，式延事外，宜加旌命，以參僚侍。

translations.literal: The eastern palace lacks virtue; the model extends beyond service; it is fitting to add bannered mandate to join the staff and attend.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted him as palace tutor.

sentences.zh: 逵既重幽居之操，必以難進為美，宜下所在備禮發遣。

translations.literal: Kui since he esteems hidden dwelling's conduct, surely takes hard to advance as beautiful; it is fitting to order the place to prepare ritual and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: They knew he would spurn pomp—send full ritual anyway.'

sentences.zh: 」會病卒。

translations.literal: " It happened he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking the post.

sentences.zh: 長子勃，有父風。

translations.literal: The eldest son Bo had the father's air.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dai Bo matched his spirit.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，以散騎侍郎徵，不起，尋卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, summoned as attendant gentleman cavalier, he did not rise; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Bo was summoned in Yixi and died unreached.

sentences.zh: 龔玄之

translations.literal: Gong Xuanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Gong Xuanzhi

sentences.zh: 龔玄之，字道玄，武陵漢壽人也。

translations.literal: Gong Xuanzhi, styled Daoxuan, was a man of Hanshou in Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Xuanzhi, courtesy name Daoxuan, from Hanshou in Wuling.

sentences.zh: 父登，歷長沙相、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Deng had served as minister of Changsha and attendant censor regular.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong Deng had been minister and attendant.

sentences.zh: 玄之好學潛默，安於陋巷。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi loved learning and was silent, content in a poor lane.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and quiet alleys.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，公府辟，不就。

translations.literal: The province raised him cultivated talent; the ducal offices summoned him; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He refused nominations.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝下詔曰：「夫哲王禦世，必搜揚幽隱，故空谷流縶維之詠，丘園旅束帛之觀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict, saying, "When a wise king governs the age, he must search and raise the hidden; therefore empty valleys flow the ode of the white horse, hill gardens display bundled silks.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu's edict praised recluses.

sentences.zh: 譙國戴逵、武陵龔玄之並高尚其操，依仁遊藝，潔己貞鮮，學弘儒業，朕虛懷久矣。

translations.literal: Dai Kui of Qiao and Gong Xuanzhi of Wuling together are lofty in conduct, rely on benevolence and roam in arts, cleanse themselves chaste and fresh, learning broadens Confucian enterprise; I have long held an empty bosom toward them.
translations.idiomatic: The edict paired Dai Kui and Gong Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 二三君子，豈其戢賢於懷抱哉！

translations.literal: You several gentlemen—how could you hoard worthies in your bosom!
translations.idiomatic: Why hide such men?

sentences.zh: 思挹雅言，虛誠諷議，可並以為散騎常侍，領國子博士，指下所在備禮發遣，不得循常，以稽側席之望。

translations.literal: I wish to draw in fine words, with empty sincerity seek counsel; both may be appointed attendant censor regular, concurrently national university erudite; order the place below to prepare ritual and dispatch; do not follow routine, thereby delaying the hope of the vacated mat.
translations.idiomatic: Both were named attendant and erudite with full honors.'

sentences.zh: 」郡縣敦逼，苦辭疾篤，不行。

translations.literal: " Commandery and county pressed urgently; he bitterly pleaded grave illness; did not go.
translations.idiomatic: County officers pressed; both pleaded mortal illness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: Soon he died at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Gong died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 弟子元壽，亦有德操，高尚不仕，舉秀才及州辟召，並稱疾不就。

translations.literal: The disciple Yuan Shou also had virtue and conduct, lofty and not serving; raised cultivated talent and provincial summons together he claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: His pupil Yuan Shou also refused office.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝以太學博士、散騎侍郎、給事中累徵，遂不起。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu repeatedly summoned him as grand university erudite, attendant gentleman cavalier, and palace counselor; in the end he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu hounded Yuan Shou in vain.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan died at home.

sentences.zh: 陶淡，字處靜，太尉侃之孫也。

translations.literal: Tao Dan, styled Chujing, was a grandson of Grand Commandant Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Dan, courtesy name Chujing, was Tao Kan's grandson.

sentences.zh: 父夏，以無行被廢。

translations.literal: His father Xia was dismissed for misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao Xia was disgraced.

sentences.zh: 淡幼孤，好導養之術，謂仙道可祈。

translations.literal: Dan in youth was orphaned, loved methods of guidance and nurturing, said the immortal Way could be prayed for.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned, he chased immortality.

sentences.zh: 年十五六，便服食絕穀，不婚娶。

translations.literal: At fifteen or sixteen he swallowed elixirs and cut grain, did not marry.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped eating grain and never wed.

sentences.zh: 家累千金，僮客百數，淡終日端拱，曾不營問。

translations.literal: Household piled a thousand in gold, retainers and guests in the hundreds; Dan all day sat upright, never managing or asking.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored vast wealth and many servants.

sentences.zh: 頗好讀《易》善卜筮。

translations.literal: Somewhat he loved to read the Changes and was skilled at divination.
translations.idiomatic: He read the Book of Changes and divined.

sentences.zh: 于長沙臨湘山中結廬居之，養一白鹿以自偶。

translations.literal: On Mount Linxiang of Changsha he built a hut and dwelt, raising a white deer for company.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut in Linxiang hills with a white deer.

sentences.zh: 親故有候之者，輒移渡澗水，莫得近之。

translations.literal: When kin and old friends came to visit, he always moved them across a gully stream; none could draw near.
translations.idiomatic: He moved visitors across a stream they could not ford.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，淡聞，遂轉逃羅縣埤山中，終身不返，莫知所終。

translations.literal: The province raised him cultivated talent; Dan hearing it, then turned and fled to Mount Pi in Luo county, to the end of life did not return; none knows where he ended.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned he fled to Pi mountain and vanished.

sentences.zh: 陶潛，字元亮，大司馬侃之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Tao Qian, styled Yuanliang, was a great-grandson of Grand Commandant Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian (Yuanming), courtesy name Yuanliang, great-grandson of Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 祖茂，武昌太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao was governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tao Mao governed Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 潛少懷高尚，博學善屬文，穎脫不羈，任真自得，為鄉鄰之所貴。

translations.literal: Qian in youth cherished lofty conduct, was broadly learned and skilled at composing texts, outstanding and unbridled, yielding to truth and self-content; the village honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful, proud, learned, the hamlet esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《五柳先生傳》以自況曰：「先生不知何許人，不詳姓字，宅邊有五柳樹，因以為號焉。

translations.literal: Once he composed the "Biography of Master Five Willows" to compare himself, saying, "The master did not know what place he was from; surname and personal name not detailed; beside his house were five willow trees, and by this he took his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: His 'Five Willows' self-portrait begins:

sentences.zh: 閒靜少言，不慕榮利。

translations.literal: Leisurely quiet, few words, not admiring glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet, terse, no taste for rank.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，不求甚解，每有會意，欣然忘食。

translations.literal: He loved reading books, did not seek to penetrate deeply; whenever he had a meeting of meaning, gladly forgot eating.
translations.idiomatic: He read for joy, not pedantry, and forgot meals when moved.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，而家貧不能恆得。

translations.literal: By nature he loved wine, but the household was poor and could not constantly obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine but stayed poor.

sentences.zh: 親舊知其如此，或置酒招之，造飲必盡，期在必醉。

translations.literal: Kin and old friends knowing this, sometimes set out wine and summoned him; when he went to drink he always finished, expecting surely to get drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Friends poured for him; he drank to blackout.

sentences.zh: 既醉而退，曾不吝情。

translations.literal: When drunk he withdrew, never stinting feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He left drunk without fuss.

sentences.zh: 環堵蕭然，不蔽風日，短褐穿結，簞瓢屢空，晏如也。

translations.literal: His ring of walls was bleak, not sheltering wind and sun; short coat patched and tied, gourd and ladle often empty—yet he was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: His hut leaked; he wore patches; his ladle was empty—yet he smiled.

sentences.zh: 常著文章自娛，頗示己志，忘懷得失，以此自終。

translations.literal: He constantly composed texts to amuse himself, somewhat showing his intent, forgetting gain and loss, by this ending himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote for himself, forgot fortune, accepted his end.

sentences.zh: 」其自序如此，時人謂之實錄。

translations.literal: " His self-account was thus; people of the time called it truthful record.
translations.idiomatic: People called his self-sketch honest.

sentences.zh: 以親老家貧，起為州祭酒，不堪吏職，少日自解歸。

translations.literal: Because parents were old and household poor, he rose as libationer for the province; he could not bear clerical duty; in few days himself resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He took a small post for his parents' rice, quit at once.

sentences.zh: 州召主簿，不就，躬耕自資，遂抱羸疾。

translations.literal: The province summoned him chief clerk; he did not go, personally plowing to supply himself; then he embraced a wasting illness.
translations.idiomatic: He refused clerkship, farmed, and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 復為鎮軍、建威參軍，謂親朋曰：「聊欲弦歌，以為三徑之資可乎？

translations.literal: Again he became adviser to the army who stabilizes and the army who establishes might; he said to kin and friends, "I merely wish to strum and sing to supply funds for three paths—may I?
translations.idiomatic: He told friends he would take a stint as magistrate for farm money.

sentences.zh: 」執事者聞之，以為彭澤令。

translations.literal: " Those in charge hearing it, made him magistrate of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him magistrate of Pengze.

sentences.zh: 在縣，公田悉令種秫穀，曰：「令吾常醉於酒足矣。

translations.literal: In the county he ordered all public fields planted in glutinous millet, saying, "Let me always be drunk on wine—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: He planted the county fields to glutinous rice for wine.

sentences.zh: 」妻子固請種粳。

translations.literal: " Wife and children firmly begged to plant non-glutinous.
translations.idiomatic: His family begged for food grain.

sentences.zh: 乃使一頃五十畝種秫，五十畝種粳。

translations.literal: Then he made one qing fifty mu glutinous, fifty mu non-glutinous.
translations.idiomatic: He split the fields half for wine, half for rice.

sentences.zh: 素簡貴，不私事上官。

translations.literal: Plain and simple he esteemed, did not privately serve superiors.
translations.idiomatic: He scorned toadying to superiors.

sentences.zh: 郡遣督郵至縣，吏白應束帶見之，潛歎曰：「吾不能為五斗米折腰，拳拳事鄉里小人邪！

translations.literal: The commandery sent a postal inspector to the county; clerks reported he should bind his sash to see him; Qian sighed, saying, "I cannot for five pecks of rice bend my waist, diligently serving petty men of the village!
translations.idiomatic: He said he would not bow for a clerk's pay.

sentences.zh: 」義熙二年，解印去縣，乃賦《歸去來》。

translations.literal: " In the second year of Yixi he unsealed the seal and left the county, then composed "Returning Home".
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 2 he quit and wrote 'Returning Home.'

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text said:
translations.idiomatic: It begins:

sentences.zh: 歸去來兮，田園將蕪胡不歸？

translations.literal: Away home! The fields and gardens will waste—why not return?
translations.idiomatic: Home again! The fields run wild—why stay away?

sentences.zh: 既自以心為形役，奚惆悵而獨悲？

translations.literal: Since I let the heart be slave to the body, why mourn alone in sorrow?
translations.idiomatic: I let flesh rule soul—why grieve alone?

sentences.zh: 悟已往之不諫，知來者之可追。

translations.literal: I see the past cannot be remonstrated, yet what comes may still be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Past faults cannot be mended; the future may yet be caught.

sentences.zh: 實迷途其未遠，覺今是而昨非。

translations.literal: Truly the lost road is not far; I know today is right and yesterday wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I strayed but a little; today I know right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 舟遙遙以輕颺，風飄飄而吹衣，問征夫以前路，恨晨光之希微。

translations.literal: The boat drifts lightly on the wave; the wind flutters blowing the robe; I ask the traveler the road ahead, resent the morning light's faint gleam.
translations.idiomatic: Boat and breeze bear me; I ask the way; dawn comes too slow.

sentences.zh: 乃瞻衡宇，載欣載奔。

translations.literal: Then I gaze at my lintel, now glad, now running.
translations.idiomatic: I see my eaves and run.

sentences.zh: 僮僕來迎，稚子侯門。

translations.literal: Servants come to welcome; children wait at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Boys wait at the gate.

sentences.zh: 三徑就荒，松菊猶存。

translations.literal: Three paths verge on waste, yet pines and chrysanthemums remain.
translations.idiomatic: Weeds choke the paths—pines and mums still stand.

sentences.zh: 攜幼入室，有酒盈樽。

translations.literal: Leading the young inside, wine fills the cup.
translations.idiomatic: Wine brims the cup with children by my side.

sentences.zh: 引壺觚以自酌，眄庭柯以怡顏，倚南窗以寄傲，審容膝之易安。

translations.literal: I lift the kettle and goblet to pour for myself, glance at the courtyard trees to ease my face, lean on the south window to lodge my pride, know that a space that fits the knees is easy to be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I pour my own cup, smile at the trees, lean on the southern sill—this little room is enough.

sentences.zh: 園日涉而成趣，門雖設而常關；

translations.literal: Daily I walk the garden and it grows delightful; though a gate is set, it is often shut;
translations.idiomatic: I stroll the garden daily; the gate stays shut;

sentences.zh: 策扶老而流憩，時翹首而遐觀。

translations.literal: I lean on my staff and wander to rest, sometimes raise my head and gaze far.
translations.idiomatic: I lean on a cane, lift my eyes to the hills.

sentences.zh: 雲無心而出岫，鳥倦飛而知還；

translations.literal: Clouds leave the peaks without intent; birds weary of flying know to return;
translations.idiomatic: Clouds drift from peaks without a plan; tired birds know the way home;

sentences.zh: 景翳翳其將入，撫孤松而盤桓。

translations.literal: the sunlight dims as it is about to enter; I stroke the lone pine and linger.
translations.idiomatic: Sunset dims; I linger by a lone pine.

sentences.zh: 歸去來兮，請息交以絕遊，世與我而相遺，復駕言兮焉求！

translations.literal: Away home! I beg to cease mixing and cut off wandering; the age and I forsake each other—why drive forth words and seek again!
translations.idiomatic: I end visits—world and I have parted—why chase more words?

sentences.zh: 悅親戚之情話，樂琴書以消憂。

translations.literal: I delight in kin's heartfelt talk, take joy in zither and books to melt sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and books and lute melt my care.

sentences.zh: 農人告餘以春暮，將有事乎西疇。

translations.literal: The farmer tells me spring is late; work will begin in the western field.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers say spring is late—west field calls.

sentences.zh: 或命巾車，或棹孤舟，既窈窕以尋壑，亦崎嶇而經丘。

translations.literal: Sometimes order the scarf carriage, sometimes paddle a lone boat; both winding deep to seek ravines, also rugged crossing knolls.
translations.idiomatic: Cart or skiff—winding dales, rugged hills.

sentences.zh: 木欣欣以向榮，泉涓涓而始流，善萬物之得時，感吾生之行休。

translations.literal: Trees flourish toward glory; springs trickle beginning to flow; I marvel that the myriad things catch their season, yet feel my life will soon rest.
translations.idiomatic: Woods thrive, springs run—I envy things their hour, know my life ebbs.

sentences.zh: 已矣乎！

translations.literal: Enough!
translations.idiomatic: Enough!

sentences.zh: 寓形宇內復幾時，曷不委心任去留，胡為乎遑遑欲何之？

translations.literal: How long will this form lodge in the universe—why not give the heart to go or stay—why hurry, hurry, whither would you go?
translations.idiomatic: Why not trust the heart to stay or go—why scurry with nowhere bound?

sentences.zh: 富貴非吾願，帝鄉不可期。

translations.literal: Wealth and honor are not my wish; the imperial city cannot be counted on.
translations.idiomatic: Rank is not my wish; heaven's court is not for me.

sentences.zh: 懷良晨以孤往，或植杖而芸秄，登東皋以舒嘯，臨清流而賦詩；

translations.literal: I cherish fine mornings to go alone, or plant my staff and weed the glutinous, climb the eastern height to loose a long whistle, face clear stream and compose a poem;
translations.idiomatic: Dawn walks, weeding, whistle on the eastern mound, poems by the stream—

sentences.zh: 聊乘化而歸盡，樂夫天命復奚疑！

translations.literal: for now I ride transformation to the end, joyfully trust heaven's command—what doubt remains!
translations.idiomatic: I ride change to the end and doubt heaven no more!

sentences.zh: 頃之，徵著作郎，不就。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as editorialist; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The court called him editor; he stayed away.

sentences.zh: 既絕州郡覲謁，其鄉親張野及周旋人羊松齡、寵遵等或有酒要之，或要之共至酒坐，雖不識主人，亦欣然無忤，酣醉便反。

translations.literal: Having cut off commandery visits, if his townsman Zhang Ye and those he moved among such as Yang Songling and Pang Zun sometimes had wine and invited him, or invited him together to a wine seat, though he did not know the host, still he was pleased without offense, and when dead drunk then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He drank with anyone who offered, even strangers, until blind drunk.

sentences.zh: 未嘗有所造詣，所之唯至田舍及廬山遊觀而已。

translations.literal: He never made purposeful visits; where he went was only to farmsteads and to roam and view Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He only visited farms and Lu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 刺史王弘以元熙中臨州，甚欽遲之，後自造焉。

translations.literal: Inspector Wang Hong in the Yuanxi years came to the province, greatly admired and waited for him, afterward personally visited him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong came to govern and longed to meet him.

sentences.zh: 潛稱疾不見，既而語人云：「我性不狎世，因疾守閑，幸非潔志慕聲，豈敢以王公紆軫為榮邪！

translations.literal: Qian claimed illness and would not see; afterward said to people, "My nature does not cozy with the world; because of illness I guard quiet—luckily it is not a clean intent admiring fame—how dare I take a prince's bending axle as glory!
translations.idiomatic: He said he shunned fame, not princes' chariots.

sentences.zh: 夫謬以不賢，此劉公幹所以招謗君子，其罪不細也。

translations.literal: To be wrongly deemed unworthy—that is why Liu Gonggan drew slander from gentlemen; the fault is not small.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Liu Zhen's warning against false slander.

sentences.zh: 」弘每令人候之，密知當往廬山，乃遣其故人龐通之等齎酒，先於半道要之。

translations.literal: " Hong always ordered men to watch him; secretly knowing he would go to Mount Lu, then sent his old friend Pang Tongzhi and others carrying wine beforehand to waylay him halfway.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong sent a friend with wine mid-road to Lu.

sentences.zh: 潛既遇酒，便引酌野亭，欣然忘進。

translations.literal: When Qian met the wine, he then drew drink in a wild pavilion, gladly forgot to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Tao stopped for wine and forgot the journey.

sentences.zh: 弘乃出與相見，遂歡宴窮日。

translations.literal: Hong then came out and met him; then they feasted merrily all day.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong joined the feast.

sentences.zh: 潛無履，弘顧左右為之造履。

translations.literal: Qian had no sandals; Hong looked to left and right to have sandals made for him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had no shoes; Wang ordered sandals made.

sentences.zh: 左右請履度，潛便於坐申腳令度焉。

translations.literal: Attendants asked for foot measure; Qian at the seat stretched out his feet and let them measure.
translations.idiomatic: Tao stretched his bare feet to be measured.

sentences.zh: 弘要之還州，問其所乘，答云：「素有腳疾，向乘藍輿，亦足自反。

translations.literal: Hong invited him back to the province, asked what he rode; he answered, "Plainly I have foot ailment; lately I ride a blue litter—still enough to return myself.
translations.idiomatic: He said he needed a litter for bad feet.

sentences.zh: 」乃令一門生二兒共轝之至州，而言笑賞適，不覺其有羨于華軒也。

translations.literal: " Then he ordered one student and two sons together to carry him to the province, yet talking and laughing at ease, not letting them feel he envied splendid carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Students carried his chair; he chatted as if no shame.

sentences.zh: 弘後欲見，輒于林澤間候之。

translations.literal: Hong afterward when wishing to see him, then waited for him among woods and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang met him only in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 至於酒米乏絕，亦時相贍。

translations.literal: As for when wine and rice failed, sometimes he also supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang sent grain when the larder ran dry.

sentences.zh: 其親朋好事，或載酒肴而往，潛亦無所辭焉。

translations.literal: When kin and friends who loved affairs sometimes carried wine and dishes and went, Qian also declined none.
translations.idiomatic: Friends brought feasts; he never refused.

sentences.zh: 每一醉，則大適融然。

translations.literal: Each time drunk, then he was greatly pleased and melting.
translations.idiomatic: Each drunk brought pure joy.

sentences.zh: 又不營生業，家務悉委之兒僕。

translations.literal: Again he did not manage livelihood; household tasks he entirely entrusted to sons and servants.
translations.idiomatic: He left chores to servants.

sentences.zh: 未嘗有喜慍之色，惟遇酒則飲，時或無酒，亦雅詠不輟。

translations.literal: Never did he show joy or anger; only when he met wine he drank; sometimes when there was no wine, still he chanted elegantly without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He showed no temper except toward wine; sober, he still sang.

sentences.zh: 嘗言夏月虛閑，高臥北窗之下，清風颯至，自謂羲皇上人。

translations.literal: He once said in summer months idle and quiet, lying high below the north window, when clear wind arrived in rustling gusts, he called himself a man before the Emperor Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Summer nap by the north window—he called himself older than history.

sentences.zh: 性不解音，而畜素琴一張，弦徽不具，每朋酒之會，則撫而和之，曰：「但識琴中趣，何勞弦上聲！

translations.literal: By nature he did not understand music, yet he kept one plain zither without strings and studs; whenever friends gathered with wine, then he stroked it in harmony, saying, "Only know the zither's inner interest—why trouble the sounds on the strings!
translations.idiomatic: He strung a soundless lute: 'Taste the music in the mind, not the ear.'

sentences.zh: 」以宋元嘉中卒，時年六十三，所有文集並行於世。

translations.literal: " He died in the Yuanjia period of Song at age sixty-three; his collected writings all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He died under Song at sixty-three; his works survive.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：君子之行殊途，顯晦之謂也。

translations.literal: The historian says: The gentleman's path has many roads—this is called showing or hiding.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: office and reclusion are one man's two roads.

sentences.zh: 出則允釐庶政，以道濟時；

translations.literal: Going out, then he harmonizes the myriad policies and aids the age with the Way;
translations.idiomatic: In court he orders the state;

sentences.zh: 處則振拔囂埃，以卑自牧。

translations.literal: dwelling, then he shakes off clamor and dust and keeps low to nurture the self.
translations.idiomatic: at home he washes off dust and feeds the soul.

sentences.zh: 詳求厥義，其來夐矣。

translations.literal: Examining closely their meaning, its origin is remote.
translations.idiomatic: Both ways are ancient.

sentences.zh: 公和之居窟室，裳唯編草，誡叔夜而凝神鑒；

translations.literal: Gonghe's dwelling in a pit-chamber, garments only woven grass—warning Shuye yet concentrating spirit mirror;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng in his cave, Dong Jing in straw—

sentences.zh: 威輦之處叢祠，衣無全帛，對子荊而陳貞則：並滅景而弗追，柳禽、尚平之流亞。

translations.literal: Weinian's place among clustered shrines, clothes without whole silk—facing Zijing he set forth chaste rule: together they dimmed their gleam and would not be pursued—next in rank to Liuqin and Shangping.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jing in rags—men like Liu Ling and Shang Ziping.

sentences.zh: 夏統遠邇稱其孝友，宗党高其諒直，歌《小海》之曲。

translations.literal: Xia Tong far and near praised his filial piety and friendship; lineage honored his honesty and straightness; singing the song of the Little Sea—
translations.idiomatic: Xia Tong's filial name rang far; his kin prized his blunt truth; when he sang the 'Little Sea'—

sentences.zh: 則伍胥猶存；

translations.literal: then Wu Zixu still survives;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu seemed to walk again;

sentences.zh: 固貞石之心，則公閭尤愧，時幸洛濱之觀，信乎茲言。

translations.literal: as for the steadfast stone heart, then even Gonglu would feel shame; when they chanced on the sight at Luo's shore, truly this saying holds.
translations.idiomatic: and that flint heart of his shamed even Jia Chong—on the Luo embankment the crowd saw it was true.

sentences.zh: 宋纖幼懷遠操，清規映拔，楊宣頌其畫象，馬岌歎其人龍，玄虛之號，實期為美。

translations.literal: Song Xian in youth cherished far-reaching conduct, pure measure shining transcendent; Yang Xuan praised his painted image; Ma Ji sighed he was a dragon among men—the title Mysterious Emptiness truly matched the beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xian earned the name Master of Dark Void.

sentences.zh: 餘之數子，或移病而去官，或著論而矯俗，或箕踞而對時人，或弋釣而棲衡泌，含和隱璞，乘道匿輝，不屈其志，激清風于來葉者矣。

translations.literal: As for the several men beyond, some moved illness to leave office, some composed treatises to correct custom, some squatted with knees spread facing men of the time, some shot fish and lodged at brushwood gates—holding harmony, hiding the unpolished gem, riding the Way, concealing radiance, not bending their intent, stirring clear wind for later leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Others fled office, wrote, fished, hid jade in sackcloth—each stiffened the breeze for later ages.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：厚秩招累，修名順欲。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Thick salary summons trouble; polished name follows desire.
translations.idiomatic: The verse says: fat pay brings grief; fame chains desire.

sentences.zh: 確乎群士，超然絕俗。

translations.literal: Firm are these gentlemen, transcendent beyond the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these men stood clear of both.

sentences.zh: 養粹岩阿，銷聲林曲。

translations.literal: They nurtured purity in cliff hollows, erased sound in forest bends.
translations.idiomatic: They fed the spirit in cliffs and woods.

sentences.zh: 激貪止競，永垂高躅。

translations.literal: They stung greed and stopped rivalry, forever leaving lofty tracks.
translations.idiomatic: They shamed the greedy and left high footprints.
